We invite you to join me and authors Rachel Page, Dina Dechmann, Teague O’Mara and Marco Tschapka, for a public webinar on Wed Dec 13 at 10am Panamá time. Together, the five of us will discuss our newly published book, BAT ISLAND, taking you on a photographic journey to the rainforests of Barro Colorado Island, Panamá, to meet the 76 species of bats that occupy this small space, and learn about their stunning natural history, physiology, evolution, sensory adaptations, foraging behavior, and social systems.
 
Join us on zoom at http://www.stri.si.edu/batisland

After years of anticipation, we're thrilled to present our bat book: ‘BAT ISLAND’, a tribute to our dear friend, Dr. Eli Kalko. Her visionary work in bat research set a remarkable course for many careers. Collaborating with exceptional authors - Dr. Rachel Page from STRI (Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute) @smithssonianbatlab, Dr. Dina Dechmann @DechmannLab (Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior) @mpi_animalbehav , Dr. Marco Tschapka from the University of Ulm, and Dr. Teague O'Mara from Bat Conservation International - has been an incredible journey spanning two decades.

Our friendship with Eli and our shared passion for bats inspired this project. Over the last two decades, I've had the privilege of photographing the phenomenal and mysterious night flyers that continue to intrigue and inspire us.

The release of ‘BAT ISLAND’ marks a milestone, sharing the captivating natural history, ecological insights, and social behavior of Barro Colorado Island's bats.

Published by Insight Editions, with authors from the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute @smithsonianpanama, this book is an homage and testament to the profound legacy of Eli Kalko, and the impact she has had on tropical bat biology.

🦇 Looking for the perfect Christmas gift? Look no further! 🎁 'BAT ISLAND’ is a treasure trove that captures the essence of these night flying wonders. With 160 pages of stunning imagery, BAT ISLAND delves into the captivating lives, diverse foraging habits, roosting secrets, and the fascinating social systems of Neotropical bats.

Ideal for both bat enthusiasts and inquisitive families, this book is more than just pages—it's an immersive experience into the lives of a remarkable group of animals. Whether exploring their nocturnal adventures or learning about their ecological importance, BAT ISLAND is an ideal gift to inspire awe and appreciation for the wonders of nature. Grab your copy now and gift the magic of bat exploration this holiday season! 🌟🦇🎄

Back from a very nice vacation, and I'm excited to share more Bonobo moments, starting with this incredible mongoose scene!

I am honored to have won the portrait category in 'Nature in focus' with this image – thank you all for your support, especially the jury !

During my adventures near LuiKotale field station in the Democratic Republic of Congo I had a remarkable encounter. I witnessed a young male Bonobo tenderly petting a small mongoose.

This fascinating moment continued as he carefully held the mongoose while enjoying fruit in a nearby tree with the rest of his group.

However, this bond may not be as innocent as it seems. Bonobos occasionally include meat in their diet, and it's likely this young mongoose was caught when its mother was hunted by the group.

Christopher Anderson - Family Trilogy

📍L’Appartement – Espace Images Vevey
LES CHAMBRES

Christopher Anderson a commencé à photographier sa famille de manière quasiment organique dès la naissance de son fils Atlas en 2008. À la naissance de sa fille Pia il poursuit cette quête d’un père essayant d’arrê­ter le temps, de ne laisser fuir aucun instant de sa nouvelle vie. Marion est omniprésente dans ces albums à la fois comme femme, mère et partenaire. En tant que photographe documentaire, Anderson n’avait jamais considéré ces photos personnelles comme une véritable série, jusqu’à ce que le photographe de guerre Tim Hetherington lui dise : « Il s’agit du temps qui passe ». Anderson a commencé à voir ses images personnelles sous un nouveau jour et a fini par penser que ces photo­graphies étaient l’oeuvre de sa vie. Pia, Son et Marion ont été publiés en trois livres distincts, formant une trilogie familiale unique, tendre et intime.

- - -

Christopher Anderson naturally began photographing his family after his son Atlas came into the world in 2008. When his daughter Pia was born, he continued the fatherly attempt to stop time and not let a single moment of this new life slip away. Marion features throughout these albums, as a woman, mother, and partner. As a documentary photographer, Christopher Anderson had never considered these personal photos as a ‘series’, but his opinion changed when war photographer Tim Hetherington pointed out that “They’re all about the passage of time.” Christopher Anderson began seeing his family pictures in a new light and realised that they may well be his best work. Pia, Son and Marion were published as three separate books, forming a unique and moving intimate family trilogy.

time for a story. I wanted to create with Inja for a long time. she’s an actress that moved to LA from Slovenia. super down to earth and fun to chat with, but also crazy expressive and emotional in front of the camera. an absolute dream to work with. she has so much energy and personality that you hardly have to direct, if at all. 

we got coffee way back when. for one reason or another, our schedules never lined up. finally, a couple years later we ended up dialing in a shoot. an adventure, rather. 

we snuck our way into this big historic apartment complex downtown LA. once we reached the top floor, we climbed out the window at the end of the hallway onto the fire escape. the first photo from the set is there. from there, the ladder to the top of the roof was really sketchy. it went up the side of the building about 20 feet, mind you we are 20 stories up. suddenly, something fell from her pocket... a neckless. I could hear it slipping through all the cracks of the metal escape. I asked her if it was valuable. her response, “it was silver. my mother gave it to me. it’s ok though.” we kept climbing.

The Ford GT90 Concept Car 

Unveiled in 1995 to celebrate Ford's 90th anniversary and honor the iconic GT40, the Ford GT90 concept car was a bold statement of automotive innovation. It housed a potent quad-turbocharged 6.0-liter V12 engine generating up to 720 horsepower. 

It included advanced features like carbon fiber construction, traction control, and active suspension, the GT90 boasted impressive performance figures, reportedly hitting a top speed of 253 mph (407 km/h) and achieving 0-60 mph in just 3.1 seconds. Despite its acclaim, the GT90 never saw production, serving as a testament to Ford's boundary-pushing engineering and design capabilities.

Rumor has it that only one GT90 Concept Car was ever made, and it currently resides at the Hajek Motorsports Museum in Ames, Oklahoma.

One of the most exciting shoots I did last year was working with the @eastafricanreptiles & Taylor Ashe Antivenom center in Watamu, Kenya to photograph spitting cobras. This particular snake is a Red Spitting Cobra (Naja pallida). Photographing these snakes is a challenge because they are not only highly venomous but they can be very aggressive/defensive as well. I had to wear a full face shield, which allowed me to avoid getting any of the venom they spit in my eyes, nose or ears.

Snakes are sadly often misunderstood and killed on sight no matter the circumstance, which is horrible because they are such a vital part of the eco systems we all live in. Organizations like East Africa Reptile's focus much of their attention not only on education and safety,  but in helping to safely remove snakes from people's homes and properties around Kenya, further increasing their chances of survival.

Ingredients:

Super Easy 4 Ingredient peanut butter cookies! 🍪 Crispy golden edges, gooey peanut butter centers. Bookmark these for your next sweet tooth! 

PEANUT BUTTER COOKIES: 
1 ½ cups smooth peanut butter 
1 ½ cups brown sugar 
2 large eggs, at room temp
1 ½ tsp baking soda 
1 tsp vanilla paste, optional 

Instructions: 

1. Preheat the oven to 350 F. Line two medium rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper and set aside. 
2. In a bowl with a stand mixer or a medium bowl with a hand mixer add peanut butter and brown sugar. Mix together on medium-high for 2-3 minutes. 
3. Add eggs, baking soda and vanilla bean paste if using and mix together for another minute. 
4. With a 1 inch cookie scoop, scoop dough balls onto the baking sheet and create a criss cross pattern with a fork. Top with a little extra brown sugar if desired. 
5. Bake for 8-9 minutes or until the edges are slightly golden brown. Remove from the oven and leave on the baking sheet for an additional 3-5 minutes. Transfer to a wire baking rack to finish cooling.

Going without costs the program more. 

Rox has been a part of my life for the past six years. I've made new friends, shared backcountry experience & knowledge while climbing outdoors and learned from each other on how to address the challenges of race in the United States. 

If you believe in the mission of @memphisroxclimbing please consider a donation. It will be put to good use. If you have the chance to visit Memphis, stop by the gym. You'll find family by the time you have warmed up.

(South East Ridge) Established in 1970 by Cesare Maestri with a gasoline powered drill, the controversial route sported a stack of bolts and was the quick way to the top. 

John and I enjoyed the climb,  yet these was something amiss. The wildness of this peak was sacrificed for human ego. Maestri, making up for his fanciful ascent of 1959, bolted the peak into submission. 
 
In 2012 the late Hayden Kennedy and

Kyle Allen Rott 1987 - 2023 
On  November  25th we lost Kyle in a fall in Hyalite Canyon, Montana. My heart goes out to his mother and sister and the South Dakota family of this fine man.  For his friends the loss is immediate. The years of being together,  weaving the fabric of friendship through shared experiences are gone.

Kyle was a climber. Once he realized that the pursuit of gravity was his life's calling,  he lived with a singular purpose. "Let's go climb."

As someone close to Kyle, his "uncle" by age and knowing him with our family, his loss is another weight on the scale of "is it worth it".

Many of my close friends are introverts. In school we found each other and climbing self selected us. Kyle and I climbed together for 15 years - most of the time hiking the folds of Southwest Montana looking for the cliffs and drips that sustain us. In between climbs he helped out by housesitting for the climbing community. For those of that trusted Kyle without houses and animals - you know how conscientious he was.  Kyle's humble approach to life - not entertaining anything superfluous - was reflected by living in his truck.  Which made housesitting a good balance. 

While Kyle was quiet and shy in a room of his peers, there was this friendly side that Kyle shared with people in life. More than once he would carefully explain the gadgets needed to climb to curious people on the trail. This translated well to the guiding he did with Montana Alpine Guides and the Mountain School in Yosemite. 

At our service for Kyle we wrote in a small book for his mother and family. His worldly possessions, kept tidy in a Livingston storage locker, spread out over a picnic table, passed to his friends. They will cherish his memory and then ply the seas of gravity, risking it all for the moment. For his age peers, dealing with non sequential death, many for the first time, left adrift questioning and bonding closer with those that stand. I was there. And now 30 years later as an elder, with culpability and responsibility.

We love you Kyle for energy you brought to our climbing adventures. 

We love you for the reminder to live calm.

The curb weight of the Porsche 356, the first Porsche automobile, was 1700 – 2,296 lbs. The weight of the Porsche name is much heavier. Ferdinand ‘Ferdi’ Porsche, an architect by trade and the great grandson of the company’s founder Prof. Ferdinand Porsche, is now adding his fingerprint to the family’s rich motor-sports legacy.

At 30 yrs old, Ferdi defies all the seriousness and pomp of racing cars. He’s affable, warm, and almost boyish in his excitement. To put it bluntly, he’s ‘cool’ without effort, working hard to invite the next generation into the motorsports world.

 On February 24, Ferdi’s F.A.T. International held its first ice race in Zell am See, Austria, and has followed it up in Aspen, Colorado. Over the past two days on an icy track in Carbondale, the race has included models from the @aetherapparel Half11 (half Porsche, half F1) to the Rivian R1T, to a host of various Mobil 1 cars tearing around corners, over-steering, under-steering, and generally bringing joy as they spit rooster tails of snow from their tires. 

I watch as an enthusiast warm his hands in the exhaust of a loud engine. He brings them to his nose, closes his eyes and inhales deeply, letting his senses coalesce into something whole and visceral. Ferdi sits in his car nearby grinning. It’s an expression of sincere, palpable joy. As an arm drops, he accelerates onto the track. In a burst of exhaust, something old becomes new again. It’s a Herculean task and these are enormous shoes to fill, but Ferdi seems to be carrying the weight of legacy effortlessly.

Words by Ben Ayers @jetbutterflies // The highway is a perpetual a fever dream of construction and destruction. Dust, scattered pavement, clawed ridges of clay are punctuated with the idle carcasses of heavy equipment, thin herds of goats, and garish tractors bouncing between knee-deep ruts. When you don’t have any lanes, you’re always splitting lanes.
 
Six days ago, Cory did what any responsible motorcyclist would do: he watched a YouTube video titled “How to Ride a Motorcycle in ONLY 1 HOUR,” which, it turns out, was only twenty minutes long. 
 
Cory then traced the backstreets of Santa Monica on a tiny café racer for five days before boarding a plane for Kathmandu. Now, eight hours of riding on Nepal’s worst and busiest highway later, the sun collapses across rice paddies heavy with grain. We still have hours to go.
 
In this perpetual present, when you’re gripped, you experience the relativity of time. It slows to a game of seconds until, as if by magic, hours have passed.

I’ve known Ben Ayers @jetbutterflies for over a decade. He’s a Kathmandu staple and has called Nepal home for twenty some years. He came for the mountains and stayed for the people, starting and running non-profits for pieces of the community. At his heart, he’s an artist and filmmaker. He’s also a ferocious writer. I’ve been to Mustang with him before on assignment for NG. But this trip is just for us. The following posts are his words.
 
Our other companion is Todd Hoffman. He doesn’t use Instagram. He’s one of those leather-faced legends of the eighties who lived hard and fast enough to know when to leave the racetrack. Even if you hardly know him, you want him on your team. At your back. If he looks familiar, it might be from that one time he took Pepsi to task over a Harrier jump jet.

RECEITA: SALADA DE BATATA COM CEBOLA CARAMELIZADA E CREAM CHEESE 🥔 ✨ 

Eu amo salada de batata com maionese. É um dos meus pratos preferidos. Decidi fazer uma versão um pouco mais elaborada, com sabores não tão comuns em uma batatonese. Me inspirei em uma das primeiras receitas do blog, uma Pasta de cebolas caramelizadas com cream cheese. Misturei isso com batatas cozidas despedaçadas com as mãos e o resultado foi esse acompanhamento perfeito para qualquer ceia de final de ano.

A quantidade dos ingredientes é relativa à quantidade de batatas que você for usar. Meu cálculo base é 1 batata grande por pessoa e 1 cebola para cada 2 batatas. Agora para o cream cheese e maionese o cálculo é o seguinte: para cada 5 ou 6 batatas - 1 pote de 150gr de cream cheese e 2 colheres de sopa de maionese. O papel dessa maionese é soltar um pouco esse creme, pra ficar mais leve e mais “espalhável”.

INGREDIENTES
para 6 pessoas

6 batatas grandes
3 cebolas
150gr de ream cheese
2 colheres de sopa de maionese (pode ser industrializada mesmo)
cebolinha, para finalizar

Cozinhe as batatas inteiras em água fria com bastante sal. Assim que ferver, abaixe o fogo e cozinhe até que elas fiquem bem macias, com a casca rachando. Retire do fogo, escorra e deixa esfriar.

Descasque e pique as cebolas. Em uma frigideira, aqueça um fio de azeite, adicione as cebolas, tempere com uma pitada generosa de sal, misture e tampe com uma tampa qualquer (não precisa ficar perfeitamente vedado). Deixe assim sem mexer, em fogo baixo, por uns 10 minutos, para a cebola soltar bastante líquido. Tire a tampa e continue cozinhando, mexendo bastante, até que elas fiquem caramelizadas, macias, doces, douradas, mas sem queimar. Retire do fogo, escorra e deixa esfriar.

Assim que as batatas estiverem mornas o suficiente para você pegar na mão sem se queimar, despedace elas com os dedos, em pedaços bem disformes. Em uma tigela grande, misture cream cheese, maionese, cebola caramelizada, sal e pimenta do reino. Misture com as batatas, com vontade, para quebrá-las ainda mais. Sirva com bastante cebolinha por cima e mais um pouco de pimenta do reino.

RECEITA: AZEITONAS MARINADAS E QUEIJO DE CABRA

Um jeito perfeito de transformar azeitonas medianas em azeitonas maravilhosas.

O azeite que sobra dela fica com um toque cítrico, super saboroso, perfeito pra molhar o pão.

Os ingredientes aqui são sugestões. Pode fazer com o que preferir, ou o que tiver em casa.

INGREDIENTES
Dentes de alho
Casca de laranja
Casca de limão siciliano
Pimenta calabresa
Ramos de alecrim
Folhas de louro
Azeitonas variadas
Azeite de oliva
Queijo de cabra tipo Boursin ou Feta

Misture os temperos em um vidro. Esmague as azeitonas levemente com a palma da mão. Misture tudo, cubra com azeite de oliva e deixe na geladeira por uns dias. O azeite pode solidificar e ficar amarelo opaco, é normal. Na hora de servir, deixe em temperatura ambiente por uma hora, despeje em um prato, despedace o queijo por cima e sirva com pão.

SALADA DE ERVAS 🌿 Em almoços especiais, eu amo servir uma mistura de ervas frescas e sementes tostadas. É quase uma salada, é quase um tempero. É um pouco de cada. Elas deixam todos os pratos mais refrescantes, mais aromáticos, mais interessantes.

O que eu normalmente uso:
Salsinha,
Hortelã,
Coentro,
Dill,
Semente de Girassol,
Semente de Abóbora.

Se não gosta ou não tem alguma delas, não use. Pode usar só as ervas sem as sementes também.

É só despedaçar as folhas, misturar, espalhar as sementes por cima e deixar na mesa. Eu costumo não temperar, para que elas fiquem bem frescas mesmo. A ideia é acompanhar pratos que já são bem temperados, que não precisam de mais sal.

RECEITA: PALETA DE CORDEIRO ASSADA, COM FRUTAS CÍTRICAS e ERVA DOCE

O prato principal do almoço que fiz com o @oiotavio ✨

Para variar a carne dos encontros de final de ano, cordeiro é uma opção maravilhosa. Uma carne saborosa, especial e linda. Aqui a gente assou ela por 4 horas, até ficar desmanchando soltando do osso. Uma marinada simples básica na noite anterior. E na hora de servir uma salada de laranjas, toranjas e tangerinas, erva-doce finamente fatiada e uma mistura de ervas aromáticas.

Inspirada em uma receita da @bonappetitmag 🍴 

INGREDIENTES

para a marinada:
6 dentes de alho
1 colher de chá de sal
uma pitada de pimenta calabresa
1 galho de alecrim
raspas da casca de 1 laranja
pimenta do reino

para assar:
1 paleta de cordeiro
1 cabeça de alho
casca de 1 laranja
1 xícara de vinho branco

salada para servir:
2 laranjas
1 tangerina
1 toranja/grapefruit
1 erva-doce
folhas variadas: salsinha, hortelã, dill e coentro

Na noite anterior, faça a marinada para o cordeiro. Esmague os dentes de alho com o sal em um pilão (ou com a faca em uma tábua). Adicione a pimenta da calabresa, as folhas de alecrim picadas, a raspa de laranja e a pimenta do reino. Misture bem.

Coloque o cordeiro em uma assadeira e faça cortes com a ponta da faca em toda a paleta, dos dois lados. Espalhe a marinada bem em toda a carne. Cubra com plástico filme e deixe na geladeira de um dia para o outro.

No dia seguinte, pré-aqueça o forno a 150ºC. Coloque embaixo do cordeiro uma cabeça de alho cortada e as cascas de laranja. Adicione o vinho branco, feche com papel alumínio bem fechadinho e leve ao forno por 4 horas. Verifique depois de umas 2 horas para ver se não está secando. Se estiver, adicione um pouco de água quente. Ao final ela deve estar super macia, soltando do osso. Se ainda não estiver deixe mais um pouco. Retire do forno e deixe descansar meia hora.

Para a salada, retire toda a casca das frutas e fatie. Fatie a erva-doce também. Misture tudo, tempere com um pouco de sal e azeite de oliva.

Transfira a paleta para um prato de servir, regue com os caldos da assadeira e arrume a salada ao redor. Finalize com as ervas frescas.

RECEITA: GRANITA DE LARANJA COM CAMPARI, pra beber com Espumante 🍊 

Essa é uma das receita do mini-almoço de final de ano que fiz com o @oiotavio  É sobremesa, é drink, é o melhor jeito de começar ou terminar um almoço ou jantar!

Granita é um tipo de raspadinha. Você mistura os ingredientes, deixa no congelador em uma travessa rasa, e vai raspando com um garfo à medida que ela vai congelando. No final o resultado é essa raspadinha alcóolica doce-amarga. Dá pra comer pura, ou dá pra fazer que nem a gente fez, e tomar com espumante.

A receita é inspirada em uma da @inagarten minha musa dos Hamptons que faz jantares maravilhosos para seus amigos.

Ela leva Campari, mas eu imagino que deve ficar uma maravilha também com Aperol. Se experimentar me conta.

O mais importante aqui é ter tempo para ela congelar com calma e raspar ao longo do tempo. Como é cheia de açúcar e álcool, a mistura demora mais pra congelar. Faça no dia anterior, ou até uns 2 dias antes. Deixe a granita em forma de raspadinha no congelador, e na hora de servir é só raspar mais uma vez.

INGREDIENTES
1 xícara de açúcar
1 xícara de água
1 xícara de Campari
2 xícaras de suco de laranja fresco
suco de 1 limão
espumante, para finalizar

Em uma panela pequena, misture o açúcar com a água e cozinhe só até dissolver.

Separe uma travessa/assadeira que caiba no seu congelador. Misture dentro dela o xarope de açúcar, o Campari, o suco de laranja, o de limão e misture bem.

Feche com plástico filme e leve ao congelador por umas 2 horas. Depois desse tempo misture com um garfo de meia em meia hora, até ela começar a congelar e a formar cristais de gelo. Quanto mais você raspar, mais soltinha ela fica.

Na hora de servir, despeje em copos ou taças, finalize com um pouco de espumante e sirva.

FINAL DE ANO ✨ 
Finalmente chegou o fim de ano desse ano que precisava acabar logo.
Não foi fácil pra ninguém, mas tá acabando.

Para terminar o ano com receitas gostosas e fotos lindas, me juntei com meu amigo @oiotavio (que tem um canal de receitas no IGTV só com coisa linda) e fizemos um mini-almoço de final de ano. Mini porque não é hora de aglomeração. Aproveite essa deixa para fazer pratos que sempre sonhou mas que eram inviáveis na ceia para dezenas de familiares famintos.

Todas as louças e utensílios nas fotos são da @nodacozinha a nova loja de objetos de cozinha do @oiotavio e do @avilapedro 🍴

Farofa crocante com castanha de cajú.

RECEITA: PIMENTÕES ASSADOS 🌶

Pimentões doces e suaves. Cozidos e sem a pele eles perdem toda a picância e aquele sabor forte que fica na memória daqueles que não o amam.

INGREDIENTES

pimentões
azeite de oliva
sal

Lave e seque os pimentões. Coloque-os diretamente sobre a chama mais forte do seu fogão e cozinhe-os no fogo até que eles fiquem queimados. Vire-os com uma pinça várias vezes, para queimar todos os lados. Eles tem que ficar totalmente pretos mesmo, pode demorar um pouquinho.

Transifra para uma tigela e cubra imediatamente com plástico filme. O vapor irá terminar de cozinhá-los, deixando-os ainda mais doces. Deixe descansar por meia hora.

Hora de descascá-los. Raspe a casca com a faca e retire os pedaços pequenos esfregando um papel toalha. Caso alguns pedaços de casca não saiam não tem problema. Retire o caule de cima, abra o pimentão e retire as sementes de dentro.

Corte em tirinhas, transfira para um pote ou vidro, tempere com uma pitada de sal e azeite de oliva. Está pronto pra servir! Ele pode ficar até uma semana na geladeira, pronto para usar quando quiser.

O azeite usado no cozimento das batatas para a tortilla é muito especial. Ele fica com um aroma de cebola e batata, e uma cor dourada linda. Guarde em uma garrafa e use onde quiser.

Receita completa da Tortilla está no feed e nos destaques dos stories.

RECEITA: TORTILLA DE PATATAS

Um clássico espanhol da Catalunha. Um omeletão de batatas e muito azeite de oliva.

Pode servir em fatias grandes com salada, ou servir em cima de fatias de pão e algum complemento em cima. Assim os espanhóis chamam de Pintxos.

Obs:

_A medida é 2 pra 1, dois ovos pra cada batata.

_Cozinhe as batatas em muito azeite de oliva antes de fazer a tortilla. Depois você vai escorrer e guardar o azeite para usar em outras receitas, é ótimo.

_O jeito espanhol é cozinhar de um lado, virar e cozinhar do outro, o que exige uma certa técnica. Dá pra usar aquelas omeleteiras que tem duas frigideiras que se encaixam. E também dá pra terminar o cozimento no forno, porém precisa de uma frigideira que vai ao forno.

para 6 porções

8 ovos
4 batatas
1 cebola
1 xícara de azeite de oliva (ou mais)
sal 

para servir:
fatias de baguete
pimentões assados (tem receita amanhã!)
azeitonas
jamón

Descasque as batatas, corte ao meio e fatie-as. Se tiver um mandolim, perfeito, senão pode fazer na faca. Fatie a cebola também.

Coloque as batatas e cebolas em uma frigideira antiaderente cubra com azeite, suficiente para que elas fiquem quase submersas. Leve ao fogo e cozinhe, sem ferver loucamente, até que as batatas estejam macias, mas não desmanchando. Retire do fogo, espere esfriar um pouco e escorra. Guarde o azeite em uma garrafa.

Em uma tigela grande bata os ovos e adicione as batatas mornas. Tempere com uma pitada de sal e misture bem. Deixe descansar por 15 minutos.

Na mesma frigideira, adicione umas colheradas do azeite, aqueça no fogo médio e despeje a mistura. Cozinhe até que a parte de baixo esteja bem dourada. A parte de cima ainda vai estar meio líquida. 

Para terminar o cozimento:
No forno: pré- aquecido a 180ºC por uns 10 a 15 minutos.
Na frigideira: deslize a tortilla para um prato grande, coloque a frigideira em cima e vire de uma vez. Termine de cozinhar até o outro lado ficar dourado também.

Retire, deixe descansar e sirva em temperatura ambiente.

Para servir como pintxos, corte em quadradinhos, finalize com as azeitonas, pimentões e jamón e coloque sobre fatias de baguete. Como prato principal, corte em fatias e sirva com uma salada.

Ovos, batatas, pimentões e um toque de drama espanhol 🌶️

BODY BOOKWORM / SOMATIC SCHOLAR 

During the time I’ve been with my husband my body has seen many changes. Seemingly subtle ones that speak loud as women’s bodies do in all our many stages. These are changes that a superficial mind conditioned by a skin-deep culture would label as not attractive. I remember my EX-husband being disgusted by my armpit & random nipple hairs which I thought was hilarious, after all women have testosterone helping us produce new blood cells, maintain bone health, libido & boost other reproductive hormones. I’ve been learning more about hormone changes as I approach menopause which is incredibly fascinating & always reiterates to me how wise the body is in adapting throughout its phases. 

The body is a book that reads of its lifetime. Birthmarks, scars, aging marks, wrinkles, tattoos, spots, hair loss, stretch marks, some of us lose limbs or gain “extra” parts along the journey. The book of the body is beautiful in its creativity. It tells a rich story. Looking at a dead body is captivating in a way, being that the soul has left its shell. It’s like an artifact left behind with stories of the past written on its skin. A tangible object the soul crafted while here on earth. But the beauty of an alive body is that the soul is still inhabited & can continue to write. Creating until its very last day. I want my body to be a museum when my soul leaves it. 

Often my clients are surprised that I know so many intimate details about their inner world without them having to tell me.  They say “how did you know that?” “It’s like you’re inside me!” “You were saying what I was thinking as I was thinking it! How do you know that?” Well, I’ve read a lot of bodies in my lifetime & it’s my gift (one could say). I’m a body bookworm or a somatic scholar. The beauty of the way the body reads is that it doesn’t lie like the mind does. It’s vulnerable (even if you think you’re not). It’s incapable of lying; just like an aged body cannot look young no matter how hard you or your plastic surgeon try to turn back time. That’s what I find stunning about aging & my work as a somatic healer. It’s honest AF & the Scorpio in me doesn’t do casual or roundabout.

I was asked if I could talk about my positive mindset towards aging: 

The older I get the smaller my ego becomes. As the persona dies I embrace my authentic self/true essence more (what people describe as “more comfortable in your own skin”).Not placing so much attention on the superficial I have loads of time/mind/energy space to be without the “noise”. It’s an ALWAYS VACATION. But most of my comfort is directly linked to my comfort with death. The reason our culture is so afraid of getting old is because they are afraid of death. So we don’t talk about death, we talk about aging when we should be talking about death. 

There are many reasons why people fear death. Where do we go? What happens? We imagine the worst. There are those (including myself) that have had near death experiences & have crossed the veil which gives us a sneak peek into the other-side BUT unless you know someone that was straight dead & has come back to share the mystery… The mystery remains & that’s what freaks people out & fascinates me so. Our brains are wired to reduce uncertainty & death is the epitome of uncertainty which is why life’s greatest practice is to get comfortable with the uncomfortable which in essence is practicing death. 

But think of it in this way; Look at history & our current world. War. Pain. Struggle. Hurt. Greed. Violence. It’s all fucked. And we think the other-side is scary?! That makes me LOL! Life isn’t easy & it’s purposefully designed that way! The longer you live the more of a chance you get to get comfortable with the uncomfortable, that means embracing aging (death). That is if you understand that’s what life is for. If you don’t aging will become the living death you fear & it will become your reality. The more you repress the process the more the fear virus will spread within you. The more you embrace it the more “life” you get.

CREATIVITY IS THE GREATEST HEALING TOOL

I give a lot of credit to my creativity in terms of my healing abilities in myself & in guiding others. Creativity is the greatest facet to human intelligence & consciousness. There’s no greater tool than creativity when it comes to EVERYTHING. 

Just look at the world we’ve created through our creativity. We generate all sorts of new ideas, continual advancement, solve all sorts of problems & make phenomenal works of art that move us, connect us & help us express & communicate the wordless parts of us. Yet I’ve found that when it comes to healing trauma, reconnecting energetically, getting past our emotional wounds, the power of creativity gets overlooked or even laughed at. 

The brain says “why are we playing around making art when you’re in pain?” Well brain to answer your question: because through abstract expression & creative sourcing I discombobulate your narrative & give myself an outlet of energy, thus giving IT a voice instead of you continuously reciting the same ol’ wack narrative that keeps me stuck! 

Creativity is empowering. The fearful brain doesn’t want you playing around with new ideas. It wants you safe & sound staying in its “known” state so it doesn’t have to be left in some weird unknown where it can’t “protect” you. But the body wants to express itself freely. They both have good intentions & find themselves disagreeing. The brain is the more careful fearful parent; the body the free-spirited parent. The compromise is in creativity. Safe enough for the brain, adventurous enough for the body, giving you TONS of options on how to approach the problem(s). 

Where we tend to get stuck in our healing is that we always go the same route, ending up at the same point. Creativity gives you different routes, new scenery, new possibilities, different end points. A huge part of my practice & work with my clients is focused on creativity. How can we give the same old story a boost & reboot? How can we turn the boring old mind dance into a new & exciting vibrant masterpiece? MovMEANT.com for a whole new perspective on healing.

Feelings are our friends. I know some will roll their eyes & be like “yeah right”. Feelings can feel like the enemy but it’s only because you’re taking it personally. Have you ever tried listening & observing the feelings as a witness or vessel instead of the persona of which they are happening to? It won’t feel like an attack but an important message. Because it is. 

Imagine not having feelings. Btw, repressing feelings isn’t NOT having feelings. Repressed feelings still live in you, even louder in-fact. I’d say it’s the opposite of not having feelings. Repression/suppression amplifies the feelings, it does not rid you of them. By doing so you’re only building a stronger army inside you. 

There is no person without feelings. Those are called robots. To feel is to be alive. Feelings are essential, vital information you need to communicate with your inner & outer worlds. They help us survive, grow, adapt, connect. When you don’t allow them to speak you’re left lost in the world without your emotional GPS. The feelings only scream louder, the emotions move stronger in you. Suppress more & they’ll stop nudging & start fighting. Cage them up for long enough & they’ll start rotting in you. Disease. 

All they wanted was to let you know they had something important to tell you cause they care about you. If you didn’t agree at least you could have had a conversation with them instead of locking them away. Sitting & talking to your feelings is the most important conversation you’ll ever have. Learn how they speak & you’ll want them around more often.

3 Reasons your glutes aren’t going 🍑

Building muscle is hard work and takes time. You have to be patient and consistent to see results. Here are some reasons you may not be seeing results and how to overcome them: 

1️⃣ Inadequate Training Volume or Intensity:

Issue: Building muscle requires adequate training stimulus. If you’re not training with enough intensity (upping your weights and training close to failure for at least your first compound lift) your glutes may not be receiving the necessary stimulation to grow.

Solution: Focus on increasing the intensity of your workouts by increasing the weight you’re lifting, incorporate progressive overload and include more glute-focused exercises in your routine. 

2️⃣ Inadequate Nutrition or Recovery:

Issue: Not fuelling your body properly and overtraining can hinder your results. 

Solution: Muscles need proper nutrition and recovery to grow. If you’re not consuming enough calories, particularly protein, your body may lack the essential building blocks for muscle growth. Additionally, inadequate rest and recovery can hinder progress. Make sure you’re getting enough quality sleep, managing stress and allowing your muscles to recover between workouts.

3️⃣ Not following a structured program 

Issue: Changing your workouts every session isn’t going to help you build your glutes.It can be tempting to jump on the latest glute building trend or exercise that promises to build your glutes after 1 session but the reality is that building your glutes takes time and requires you to perform the same workouts for at least 4 - 6 weeks, progressively increasing the intensity (progressive overload). 

Solution: Following a program that incorporates progressive overload and has a well structured exercise selection will help you maximise your gains.

More views from Vienna, this time from October 2023 on the new Phoenix color film.

The last few years have been (mostly) good for analog photography: the new Leica M6, increased use of ECN-2 film stocks and processing, news of a new line of Pentax film cameras — while we’re also facing rising film prices and ongoing economic issues elsewhere, I’ll take positive news when it comes.

When Phoenix was released, there was a certain amount of negativity about who was sent sample rolls as the launch coverage and reviews rolled out. The common complaint was that it was only sent to “influencers” — not a term I love, though people with influence have always been a good strategy for getting the word out.

The implication was that if Phoenix had been sent to “real” photographers for testing, the images would have been better, or the reviews wouldn’t have been as favorable, etc. — and that the generally-positive public feedback on the new film was only due to said influencers not wanting to get on Harman’s bad side.

This sort of commentary smells like jealousy, and I get it — there are a LOT of amazing photographers out there who haven’t been blessed by social media’s algorithmic deities, and it can be frustrating to see opportunities being handed to other people when you feel you could do better. However, indignance doesn’t do anyone any favors.

It’s also easy to be jaded, and say companies like @harmanphoto are making a money-grab by selling a limited edition product — though I’d wager most of the folks who made that argument happily took advantage of Black Friday deals.

Harman launched a new, niche product, and you can’t do that without promotion — if you can get the bulk of your press by sending people free product, more power to you.

So, let people be excited about new film! The world has enough darkness right now — choose to shine a light where you can.

Packed with plant protein, these sticky miso tofu bowls with peas, edamame and ginger are nourishing, flavoursome and super easy to make. Thanks @deliciouslyella. 

Ingredients 
2 servings of basmati rice, (about 100g / 3.5 oz) rinsed 
1 tablespoon olive oil 
Small chunk of ginger, (about 20g / 0.7 oz) cut into matchsticks/grated 
2 large cloves garlic, thinly sliced 
1 tablespoon tamari 
100g / ¾ cup / 3.5 oz frozen peas, defrosted 
100g / ¾ cup / 3.5 oz frozen edamame beans, defrosted 
Pinch of sea salt 

For the sticky tofu 
1 tablespoon olive oil 
1 block firm smoked tofu, (about 280g / 10 oz) drained & cut into bite-sized pieces 
1 tablespoon tamari 
2 tablespoons maple syrup 
2 tablespoons brown rice miso paste 
2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar 

Method  

Pour the rice into a small saucepan, along with 200ml / 7 fl oz water and a large pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes until all of the water has been absorbed. Remove from the heat and set aside. 
 
While the rice is cooking, warm 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan set over medium–high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until crisp and golden on all sides. 
 
Next, whisk together 1 tablespoon tamari, the maple syrup, miso paste and rice wine vinegar. Once the tofu is cooked, pour the sauce into the pan and let it reduce to create a sticky sauce that coats the tofu. Remove the tofu from the pan and set aside on a plate. 
 
Pour 1 tablespoon of olive oil into the same pan, followed by the cooked rice, ginger and garlic. Fry for 5 minutes, until crisp, then stir in the tamari, peas, edamame beans and crispy tofu. Divide between 2 bowls and serve with your favourite crispy chilli oil/sauce.

I’m making this on repeat at the moment, so wanted to share the recipe with you. It’s a family favourite, such a good staple and one of the easiest ways to up your veggie intake. It’s a nice one for food waste too, simply swap the veg for anything you’ve got lying around at home - leeks, whole tomatoes, courgettes, leafy greens etc are all delicious additions, likewise white beans instead of chickpeas and any pasta shape instead of orecchiette (broken pieces of lasagne are fab, as is orzo). Dial the chilli up or down to taste, or simply add it at the end if you’re making this for little ones (once you’ve served them) 

For the nourishing veggie broth with orecchiette, you’ll need 
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 carrots, halved lengthways & cut into 1cm half moons
- 2 sticks of celery, finely chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed/finely chopped
- 2 bay leaves
- small handful of thyme sprigs
- 1 tablespoon tomato purée
- 1 tablespoon brown rice miso paste
- 1 x 400g tin chopped tomatoes
- 1 x 400g tin chickpeas, drained
- 1¼ litre vegetable stock
- 3 servings of orecchiette (about 225g)
- large handful of basil
- pinch of dried red chilli flakes
- pinch of sea salt

Ну вот опять - вместо того, чтобы упражняться в изобретении какого-нибудь интересного десерта, приходится упражняться в математике, английском и рисовании 😅Так что в промежутках между занятиями, можно успеть приготовить что-то очень простое и быстрое. 🙌🏻
Ловите рецепт бискотти …ну или вкусных сухарей! )) 🤪
Рецепт:
2 яйца
100 гр кокосового сахара (для сладкоежек рекомендую 150 гр, можно использовать тростниковый или сахарозаменитель)
50 гр сливочного масла
щепотка соли
1 ч л (без горки) разрыхлителя
200 гр цельнозерновой муки спельты
100 гр муки из зеленой гречки
(Можно взять 300 гр пшеничной муки)
50 гр сырого фундука
50 гр очищенных фисташек
сушеные ягоды малины (или изюм 50 гр)

Приготовление:

Яйца взбить с сахаром до пышности. Добавить мягкое сливочное масло, взбить еще раз. Ввести муку (сразу вместе два вида), разрыхлитель и соль. Тесто будет упругое. Добавить орехи, ягоды или изюм и быстро замесить тесто руками. Сформировать тесто в форме плоского рулета. Поставить в разогретую до 180С духовку. Выпекать в течение 25 минут. Затем достать заготовку из духовки, дать постоять в течение 5 минут. Затем нарезать на отдельные кусочки (толщиной 2 см). Снова выложить на противень. Выпекать в течение 5 минут, затем перевернуть кусочки и снова запечь в течение 5 минут. Остудить на решетке.

В моем детстве пищевые красители для яиц были на вес золота. Помню, как баночки с разведенными красками передавали от соседа к соседу, так что всему подъезду хватало и у всех были одинаково-красивые яйца. Красить луковой шелухой было скучно и слишком просто, нужен был вот этот интересный квест по охоте за пищевыми красителями 🤪
Хотя я считаю, что самый красивый оттенок дает именно луковая шелуха - такой багряно-красный, насыщенный❤️
Сейчас в магазинах такое разнообразие всяких решений для декора пасхальных яиц, что даже как-то скучаешь по тому захватывающему квесту. Всем таким же ностальгирующим предлагаю устроить охоту на самый уникальный оттенок, добытый природными красками 😉🙌🏻Я уже не первый год это практикую и каждый раз прихожу в восторг от самого процесса и иногда неожиданного результата. Есть один оттенок, которого я пока еще не смогла добиться - это зеленый🌱Все попытки использовать зеленые продукты чаще дают скудный желтый. Слышала про листья березы. Кто-то пробовал?🧐
В этот раз даже порошок витграсса в ход пошел )) но все, что получилось - это высохшие, слегка зеленоватые разводы от порошка. 
Мои неизменные фавориты - голубика / черника, каркадэ, краснокочанная капуста, куркума, сафлор (или дикий шафран), черный чай или цикорий, свекла (порошок из сушеной свеклы отлично работает!).
В этот раз все оттенки я получила окрашиванием сваренных и холодных яиц. Выдержка в растворе 12 часов. 
Каркадэ, чай, цикорий, куркуму, сафлор я заваривала кипятком. Замороженная голубика - пюрированная с добавлением небольшого количества холодной воды. Порошок из свеклы развела водой комнатной температуры. 
В карусели я подписала, какие оттенки получились от каких продуктов. 
Добавление уксуса придает окрашивающим свойствам цепкости, но может менять оттенок некоторых продуктов, например у голубики, капусты, каркадэ и свеклы. 
Делитесь в комментариях своими интересными решениями и удачных вам экспериментов!

Waiting for Serhiy

His attempts to escape the Russian siege had failed. He and his fellow Ukrainian Marines were surrounded, dozens of miles from friendly lines. They were nearly out of food and ammunition. Some panicked, others quietly resigned themselves to what would come next.
Then, a few days later, senior sailor Sergey Hrebinyk and his comrades emerged from the sprawling Ilyich Iron and Steel works in the southern Ukrainian city of Mariupol. He quickly messaged his older sister: “Hi Anna. Our brigade surrenders. In captivity today. I also don’t know what will happen next. I love you.”
It was April 12, 2022.

Nearly two years later, on the second anniversary of the start of Russia’s full scale invasion, Serhiy Hrebinyk, 24, remains in captivity as a prisoner of war, held somewhere in Russia. His family sits in purgatory, trapped between that day in April and the present.

The initial panicked flurry of calls to the Red Cross, the Ukrainian military and local officials subsided as official proof of life took months to come. The war dragged on, and now, like thousands of other Ukrainian families with relatives in captivity, the Hrebinyks wait.

“Life, of course, has changed. Almost every day is filled with tears,” said Svitlana Hrebinyk, Serhiy’s mother.

I get asked all the time whether or not I bait my camera traps. My answer is that if you can find a place that the animal wants to go naturally, you’re way better off than trying to convince a wild animal to go somewhere you want it to you. I caught these two young bull moose going head to head on one of the camera traps we had set up in @isleroyalenps.  This pretty much sums up the new techniques I’ve been using in my camera traps lately. Autofocus 😬. No lights 😳. Silent cameras 😎. It’s pretty tough going, but when it works, man it works.  I also think it’s a lot more likely to generate images capturing better behavior as there are no sounds or lights to disturb the animals while they’re doing their thing. What do you think?

Mirror, Mirror | “Mirror, Mirror, on the wall, who’s the fairest of them all?” This now ubiquitous English phrase came from a Disney movie, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.⁣
⁣
In photography, mirrors play an important role, serving as a compositional device, and as an element that makes the image more magical, dramatic, mysterious or just visually engaging. The creative use of mirrors in photography gives a poetic license to create imagery that is less obvious or straightforward, but allows for alternative ways of capturing a moment, a character and a scene. It can also be an effective way of avoiding direct contact with a subject or to render a sensitive or difficult situation without direct confrontation.⁣
⁣
These images from my archive reflect the multitude of ways mirrors serve as visual devices in photography.⁣
⁣
Captions:⁣

1. Donia Remedios, 73, who has pancreatic cancer, spends time at home with her daughter, Orlanda Hernandez Ramirez Remedios, 44, at their family compound. MEXICO 2014⁣

Working hours: 12 pm- 9 pm

The oldest continuously used Muslim Cemetery in the world, the City of the Dead, with history tracing back to the seventh century. Cairo’s vast 13th century cemetery, the only living occupants, were caretakers paid by families to maintain their ancestral mausoleums.
In 1993, over one hundred and twenty thousand people lived, worked, shopped, and went to school in and among the mausoleums. Today, that number is much higher, huts are built around tombstones, between which laundry is hung to dry, and masses of people live and work in dwellings built amongst the grand burial sites of famous religious and political figures of Egypt’s rich history. This exhibition pays tribute to the historic area, its people & their stories.
This exhibition is sponsored by the US embassy in Cairo.

A recent article in The Economist reported on the issue of stray cows in India and how the right’s pro-cow policies are doing little to protect the sacred animals. I’ve traveled to India over 10 times on assignment and have seen with my own eyes the way cows are a part of daily life. I’ve always been fascinated by the special position cows have in Hindu society. At first I thought it was unusual, but over the years and many visits I’ve come to not only appreciate the beliefs around a cow’s sacredness, but also understand that virtually every part of a cow, from their feces, meat, bones, skin, urine, etc, has a value. Whether it’s using their feces for fuel or building your home, to their skin for clothing and protection, it’s incredible what overall value, at least from a human’s perspective of dominion over the natural world, represents. No wonder cows are considered sacred. ⁣
⁣
But I’ve also seen the downside of this reverence, where cows are left to wander and get sick and literally die on the streets. The ruling conservative party, BJP, has passed several “pro-cow” policies like a ban on cow slaughter, but that has only led to the proliferation of stray cows, now numbering over 5 million. 

Abandoned, they often feed on plastic bags and other garbage, and can cause car crashes and destroy crops. One thing is certain – the current situation is untenable and more must be done to protect India’s stray cows.⁣
⁣

⁣
From the romantic to the traumatic, how do two people hold together and why or what brings them together. In some sense, it’s the most desired and natural relationship humans strive to attain, yet two people can be brought together for reasons or circumstances that are not positive or romantic or comforting.
⁣
There have been couples I’ve met in my lifetime, and I imagine anyone reading this has experienced the same thing, who are so perfectly matched, that if they were to ever break up you’d think the world was coming to an end. The qualities that I see exemplifying coupling are trust, care, being able to listen and make space for a mate’s feelings and thoughts, and of course being able to laugh with each other. Yet, some people couple out of desperation, need, economics, lust and social pressures.⁣

“Light Walker”

A self portrait series from just a few weeks ago in Deadvlei, Namibia.  A place I’ve dreamed of visiting for a decade… and yet being there in person, walking barefoot across the dead marsh under these 600-900 year old skeleton trees, was such a surreal experience unlike what I imagined it would be.  It’s strange to walk through a place that feels so long dead and forgotten - yet still full of life and wonder.

I originally had an entirely different series of images in my mind for here, involving a couple of different colourful dresses (red and gold) and dance poses mimicking and flowing with these trees… but when I arrived here, just as the sun rose and lit up my surroundings and as I walked over the last sand dune to see the dead pan valley floor below, all those earlier visions I had simply vanished. Thankfully, tucked away in the bottom of my backpack under my camera gear and red/gold dresses (anyone else cram dresses and chocolate into their backpack as a general hiking norm?), I had also this white dress as a back-up… and I was so glad I brought it, because all I could actually envision in person here was a balance of death and life, light and dark, a dream walking through decay. 

And so that’s how I spent the next 3 hours - walking and running around barefoot, feeling connection, contrast and awe, and creating this new series as it came to me. 🤍 What a surreal place.

“The Essence of Lightness”

A self portrait taken at midnight in Iceland last summer (the time of endless light!). 💙

So far every morning this year I’ve been deep diving into my journal, writing out and contemplating what it would be like to live lighter.  To cultivate an ease and lightness in my mind, to be less busy, to be more trusting in the unknown future.  To play more, and let my inner child lead me romping through the woodlands and meadows, inspired by my imagination. 

I thought I’d share this lil blurb I brain-barfed out onto the pages this morning. 🤓⬇️

“This year I want to let go of pressure.  Both the pressure I put on myself, and the pressure the societal world puts on us all. 

I let go of the pressure to be perfect. The pressure to look a certain way. The pressure to post every day. I let go of the pressure I put on myself to create better and better images, videos and paintings.

This year I embrace lightness. I celebrate imperfection, because when I allow myself and my creations to be made imperfectly with my mind open, it creates space for a world of new ideas, opportunities and surprise happenings I never would have dreamed up myself in my “perfect world”.

This year I let my true essence take the seat of my mind and being. I take time to intentionally practice dwelling in my truest state - the state of complete trust, leading to peace and joyful lightness, where I feel the most myself. 

This year I allow myself to live. Not by someone else’s standards, and not by the standards I once thought I should hold over myself. 

I live by listening. I listen intently to what brings me a sense of joy, rightness and lightness. I listen to what I can give - what I can naturally offer and help bring out in others.

I live by being kind. I live in gratitude for the freedom I’m so, so, so incredibly fortunate to have access to.

I allow this freedom to be protected, nurtured and loved, to not let this gift be taken for granted or hijacked by the endless hustling pressures of the world.

This year I embrace lightness. I put my heart first, and I let love, trust and wonder lead the way down this path of life. This one chance we have to truly live.” 🤍

Spinach and ricotta shells 😋

This recipe is one of my favourite pasta dishes, so easy to make and a great one for entertaining too 🤌🏼

Ingredients: - 250g ricotta - 3 tbsp lemon juice - 100g chopped spinach - 1 tbsp minced garlic - 1 tsp salt - cracked pepper, to taste - 700g passata - handful of fresh basil leaves - 12 pasta shells - sprinkle of parmesan - 1 tbsp pine nuts

Method:
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C fan-forced and place a large pot of water to boil over the stove, on high heat.
2. Once water is boiled, add the pasta shells to the pot. Cook as per packet instructions, ensuring not to overcook. Then, drain and rinse with cold water.
3. Add passata, fresh basil leaves, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper to a 30cm x 20cm baking dish and mix, spreading evenly.
4. Add ricotta, lemon, spinach, garlic, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper to a bowl and mix well to combine.
5. One-by-one, spoon approx 2 tbsp of the ricotta mixture into each shell and place into the baking dish. Repeat until shells and ricotta mixture are all used up.
6. Sprinkle with parmesan and pine nuts, and place into the oven to bake for 15-20 minutes, or until pine nuts and pasta shells begin to brown.
7. Serve hot & enjoy!

This delicious, creamy ramen is perfect in the cooler months 🍜 Packed full of veggies and tofu for protein, it’s also super easy to make 🌱 This recipe is on page 70 of my 3rd cookbook, Simple Vegan Kitchen. Enjoy!

Ingredients:
1 tbsp oil, any kind for frying
1 cup/100 g finely sliced shiitake mushrooms
1 x 400g can of corn, drained
1 pak choy bunch, roughly chopped
2 spring onions, finely sliced
300g soft tofu, drained and cut into 1-2cm cubes

1 nori sheet, shredded
Broth:
1 veggie stock cube
1.5 tbsp miso paste
1 tbsp soy sauce

1.5 cup boiling water
1 tbsp sesame oil
Optional
Sriracha 
Japanese seasoning 

Method:

El ”Zorro orejas de murciélago” es una especie de zorro conocida como zorro ojerudo o zorro orejas de murciélago (Otocyon megalotis). Esta especie se caracteriza por tener orejas grandes y puntiagudas, que pueden recordar a las orejas de un murciélago, de ahí su nombre común. Es nativo de África y se encuentra en regiones como el sur y este del continente. Su dieta consiste principalmente en insectos, aunque también puede alimentarse de pequeños mamíferos y frutas. Su aspecto peculiar y sus hábitos alimenticios lo hacen una especie interesante para estudiar en el campo de la ecología y la conservación.

Sharing this scares the sh*t outta me, but here goes…😬🫣

I’ve always felt like I’m “strange” & misunderstood, & have never felt I belong in the world. I’m super sensitive, think differently, overthink, catastrophize, hyper focus & have multiple thoughts at the same time NON-STOP. Daily tasks at times are impossible for me, & sometimes just stepping out of the house feels terrifying. 

I’ve just been diagnosed with ADHD & RSD (Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria) - which explains why I people-please so much & get so upset when faced with rejection, or even the perception of it - which tends to be my default reaction!

The fear of rejection is paralyzing at times, hindering me from taking action. It’s likely the reason I place immense pressure on myself to achieve perfection... a goal that is unattainable & often leads to more distress, ultimately resulting in inaction.

Throughout my life, I’ve carried the belief that I am broken, incompetent, & unintelligent, harboring deep self-hatred as a result. 😢 The burden of guilt & resentment towards myself has been overwhelming.

Living within my own mind for the past 39 years has been undeniably exhausting, at times making me wish I could escape my own thoughts. I’ve long been aware that I don’t fit the mold of what is considered “neurotypical” & I’ve found relief & validation in officially getting a diagnoses. I can now help myself & show self compassion. 🙌🏼

I am so thankful for my family & true friends who accept & love me no matter what. 🙏🏼 I’m especially grateful for Dec, who has stood by my side for the past 14 years, despite the challenges of living with me. It still surprises me that he wants to marry me haha! 😆

I am also grateful for the decision to start exercising in my 20s, as it is the one consistent factor that helps me tremendously.

ADHD & RSD do NOT define me, nor do they render me broken. I am wonderfully unique, just like every individual in this world. I believe there is no such thing as “normal” anyway. 🥰🫶🏼

If you feel comfortable sharing, have you received a neurodivergent diagnosis as an adult?

We are not alone. 😘

“You’re meant to be a fitness professional, but you’re weak, unfit & pathetic!“ - these are not words from other people, they’re words from my own head! 😫 Yep, I can be my own worst enemy! 😔 Words have great power & we need to be careful what we tell ourselves. 
I’m actively working on reprogramming the way I talk to myself to be more positive, kinder & more encouraging. I need to believe in myself as I believe it’s the first & most important step towards achieving success!
This workout absolutely destroyed me. 🥵 But I did it & I’m proud of myself! 👏🏼
Getting back into my training has been a struggle. I’m lacking motivation & consistency feels like a distant dream. I’ve been beating myself up over the strength & fitness I’ve lost. Rehabbing injuries for several months has left me feeling discouraged, & it’s hard not to compare myself to who I used to be.

Fitness professionals like me are not immune to struggles. We may know WHAT to do, but we still have to put in the work for results. The mental game is the toughest part, especially when starting over feels like a never-ending cycle. Life throws curveballs that make it hard to stick with something long-term. But I’m determined to reclaim my fitness, strength, & get back to feeling incredible again.

Negative self-talk doesn’t do us any good. Deep down, we know this, but we need reminders. We have to consciously choose to focus on the positive, even when it feels like an uphill battle. It’s not easy, but it’s necessary.

Remember; If it were easy, everyone would be doing it. The path to fitness is tough, but it’s worth every bit of effort. So I’m taking charge, setting realistic goals, & celebrating every small victory along the way. Consistency is my anchor, & I’m committed to showing up for myself every single day.

It does get easier, I know this because I’ve done it many times before. Each day I put in the effort, I know I’ll get stronger & fitter. Progress may be slow, but it’s progress nonetheless. 
Let’s embrace the struggle, be proud of our efforts, & keep pushing forward. We have the power to transform our lives, & it’s time to unleash that power. 👊🏼

The last five days have been a whirlwind. I had my last day at Circle Round and left a little bit unceremoniously since we had to fly to Arizona the next morning very early. Adam‘s mom had a stroke and he flew here a few days before. My mom and stepdad were in Arizona already for the gem show, and so we got to spend one glorious afternoon and evening with them before they flew back to Connecticut. 
This trip has been quite a bit different than many in the past. We’ve spent a lot of time going to visit Adam‘s mom in the hospital and a lot of time at home cooking and running around after Palomino. There’s a level of breathtaking that I am finding myself becoming more aware of. 
My personal breath. I realize how much I hold without breathing. And then when I finally sit down, my nervous system feels so frazzled. Adam is doing so amazing, holding space supporting his dad being so calm and loving and kind. It’s his nature. But it still fills me with gratitude to experience the calmness of his loving heart.  How he shows up in crisis and in calm. 
We have a few more days down here and then we fly home to start the next adventure which includes taking a well deserved break, pivoting @modernmacrame /closing down, dreaming up the next direction of focus for my creative entrepreneurial spirit, and BEING. Being for myself. For Pal. For Adam. For my family. For my community.
I will share more about my departure from Circle Round soon, but for now I’m focusing on being present, playing with Pal, we took our first bike ride together today!
It’s a mix of grief and gratitude.
Sending love and peace to all.

The king of wands

The King of Wands represents pure fire energy in its masculine form. Unlike the other Wands court cards, the King is not so interested in creation and creativity, or in dreaming up ideas and implementing them himself. Instead, he is more inclined to take an idea and then enlist others to help him actualise it. Thus, when the King of Wands appears in a Tarot reading, it is a sign you are stepping into the role of a visionary leader, ready to direct your people towards a common goal. You have a clear vision of where you want to go, and now you are manifesting that vision with the support of those around you. Others naturally gravitate towards you because you are charismatic, focused, and determined, and they believe in you and your vision. They want to be a part of what you are manifesting and are here to support you one hundred percent of the way. You are also masterful at getting other people to do your work for you while keeping them on-side throughout the process.
The King of Wands reminds you to lead your life with intent, vision and a long-term view. You have a grand idea of what is truly possible, and you will stop at nothing to see it through. You achieve a lot because you are clear about your future direction and how you will get there – and do not waste your time on activities or relationships you believe will lead nowhere. You never just go with the flow; instead, you prefer to embark on a direct and robust course of action. And you are inspired by long-term, sustainable success, wanting to have a lasting impact. You are here to leave a legacy.
The appearance of the King of Wands also suggests that an opportunity is presenting itself to you, and you now have the power to take on the challenge. You are the determining factor in this situation. If you want it to be successful, it will. And equally, if you do not fully commit to it, this seed will struggle to blossom and grow. You can create any outcome you wish, so be mindful about your intentions and vision. You hold the power.

The story of Donut:
After about a year of living together one day Adam said what do you think about getting a dog. I thought hey how about we foster one instead. We have such busy lifestyles and maybe we should see if bringing a dog into our lives will be a good fit. That was on a Friday. On Monday this little scruffy sickly fearful creature showed up to our house,  he had eaten an entire plastic bowl and wouldn’t eat in front of us for months. After just a few days we decided there was no way we could give him back and we just we named him Donut after the tiny donut shaped ball he curled up into. Circa 2013?

Donut was our eternal adventure buddy. He came everywhere with us. He came to work every single day to the Macramé studio and Adam’s screen printing space. He climbed ladders. He rode in backpacks. He hiked mountains. He’s snuggled under blankets and sleeping bags in tents and in the back of our Ford truck. He was a protector. All that he wanted was love. And we gave him as much as we could.

Ouvi muitas vezes que relacionamentos eram difíceis. Ouvi também que o primeiro ano de casamento era confuso, de adaptações e muito conhecimento. Ouvi perguntas de pessoas que estavam até preocupadas: “E aí, como está sendo esse primeiro ano do casamento?” E todas perguntas foram respondidas com um sorrisão no rosto: “Casar é bom demais!”

Se você tem ouvido que relacionamentos são complicados, se você perdeu a esperança porque tudo que viveu até agora não passou de sofrimento eu venho te dar palavras de alegria! O amor é simples demais quando é do jeito de Deus.

Esqueça as brigas, os ciúmes, as crises e discussões. Esqueça a desconfiança, o medo e a incerteza. O jeito de Deus é leve, “não inveja, não se vangloria, não se orgulha. Não maltrata, não procura seus interesses, não se ira facilmente, não guarda rancor.” E quando for do jeito de Deus, VOCÊ IRÁ SABER.

O amor que vem de Deus te traz paz. Te aproxima Dele. Te convida a ter um olhar belo sobre tudo. Tem seus desafios, mas tudo é resolvido com joelho no chão e lealdade um com o outro. Os problemas vêm, mas o casal não se volta contra si, e sim contra o que tem de ser resolvido.

Portanto ore e aproveite as oportunidades que Deus te dá. Cultive um relacionamento de mesma fé e tenha certeza de que Deus irá te abençoar.

Информации на эту тему читала много, и, думаю,  продолжу этим заниматься. 🙂
По-хорошему, это должно быть одним из главных наших хобби 🙋🏼‍♀️ На сайте tarkvanem.ee (что переводится как - “мудрый родитель”, сайт есть и на русском) есть конкретные советы по данной теме. Возьмите себе на заметку! 📝 

Если немного порассуждать, то у любой эмоции и проблемы есть причина. Очень часто всё это у нас накапливается, смешивается и решать уже приходится в авральном режиме. И без конкретных техник в такой ситуации уже не справиться. Поэтому, надо быть готовой и иметь в заготовках необходимые решения. Мы -  родители тоже не идеальные, чего-то не углядели, на что-то закрыли глаза, не смогли отследить и прочувствовать какие-то события и переживания ребенка. Но, конечно,  это не должно быть оправданием своей лени и «глухоты», ведь проблемы ребёнка во многом являются отражением наших собственных нерешенных проблем.

📝Приготовление:
Смешиваем воду сахар и дрожжи до полного растворения
Всыпаем просеянную муку, соль и начинаем замешивать тесто. Когда тесто собралось в комок, добавляем масло и вымешиваем мин 10, до тех пор, пока тесто не начнет отставать от рук.
Оставляем тесто на час подходить в тёполом месте
Делим тесто на 6/12 частей, формируем тонкие жгутики, складываем каждый вдвое, перекручиваем между собой и соединяем в кольцо.
Обмакиваем бублики в медовой воде а затем в маке или сахаре и корице
Выкладываем на противень, застеленный пергаментной бумагой, накрываем и даём подняться при комнатной температуре минут 40
Выпекаем бублики в разогретой до 180 градусов духовке 15-20 мин.

Santorini, the most magical of the Greek islands. This island of the Cyclades offers a multitude of activities to its visitors.

From discovering its historical heritage to watching the sunset over the Aegean Sea, to black sand beaches and boat trips, there is something for everyone. Here's a rundown of the best things to do in Santorini.

Fira, the capital, is one of the places not to be missed. With its white and blue houses, small cobbled streets, fashion boutiques and luxury hotels with swimming pools, it represents the essence of the island.

The village of Oia is also not to be missed for its spectacular beauty

The archaeological site of Akrotiri is an exciting getaway for history and culture lovers.

The ancient city of Thera is also worth a visit to learn more about the island's history

For food lovers, the Greek cuisine in Santorini is not to be missed, especially the famous souvlaki

Boat trips around the island are a pleasant way to discover the wonders of Santorini. The boat cruise, which allows you to visit the volcanic island and to reach the top of the crater of the volcano Nea Kameni, is a very popular activity

Sea kayaking from the red beach is also a fun activity that allows you to discover the volcanic coast and the fabulous sea caves

To finish the day, the sunset on Oia is one of the most famous activities in Santorini.

However, for those who are looking to watch the sunset from the water, the alignments may be better in Fira or Imerovigli.

Take a voyage back in time to Rothenburg, a medieval German town that is considered the most charming in Bavaria.

Rothenburg has a rich history that dates back to the Middle Ages. The town was founded in 1170 and thrived due to its strategic location on an important trade route. The town's historic buildings have been preserved in their original state and offer visitors a unique glimpse into life in the Middle Ages.

Start by walking through the streets of the old town, admiring the historic buildings and beautiful views.

Be sure to visit the city hall, built in 1250, as well as climb the steps of the clock tower for a spectacular view of the city's rooftops, churches and historic buildings.

Last but not least, don't miss a visit to the medieval fortress called Burggarten, which also offers a breathtaking view of the city. It's the perfect place to take memorable pictures.

🫐 Blueberry Negroni 🫐
Makes 2 Servings

2 ounces @empress1908gin
2 ounces Luxardo bitter bianco
1 1/2 ounces sweet vermouth
1 ounce blueberry concentrate

Stir together all ingredients in a mixing glass with a few cubes of ice. Strain and pour into 2 chilled rocks glasses filled with ice. Serve immediately.

Blueberry Concentrate

1 cup blueberries, fresh or frozen
1 tablespoon finely grated orange zest
2 tablespoons sugar
1/2 cup water

Bring to a boil over med-high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer until blueberries release their juices, about 10 minutes. Place a sieve over a small bowl and strain, using a spoon to press the blueberries to get as much liquid as possible. Reserve the liquid and discard the blueberry pulp. Cool to room temperature then refrigerate in an airtight container.

Where we ended up, and how we got there ➡️👀 I’m breaking down how I use layering to add dimension +  texture in captures, and you can get the full behind-the-scenes emailed to you by commenting LAYER below or via the link in my profile! 💌

And if you’re wondering what this golden concotion is, it’s a creamy and ultra-comforting roasted parsnip soup 🍜💛

Because I’m obsessed with all things both salty and sweet, I caramelized some leeks and pureed them into the soup with the roasted parsnips, and sprinkled some on top as well for texture.

Leeks have much less moisture than onions, so they caramelize much quicker in the pan. But be careful! That also means it’s easier to burn them if you’re not paying attention since they dry out faster. 🔥

And for a slight bit of crunch and a wonderfully toasted flavor, there’s some roasted hazelnuts sprinkled on top. The tired cook might say “meh, I don’t really need those” and cut them from the grocery list, but let me insist, that you *do* in fact need them. They are SUCH a good complement to the roasted parsnip soup, and if you get tired of the same texture easily like I do, they add a really nice crunch to an otherwise super smooth soup. And they’re super easy to make (less than 10 minutes to toast them, I promise!) Live a little and go for it, I say! 🙌

You can find the recipe at AdventuresInCooking.com 😋Wishing you the most fantastic week ahead, my friends! 💛💛💛

Halloween, first referred to by this name in 1775, traces its roots to the ancient Celtic pagan festival of Samhain. 

This festival, celebrated on November 1st, signaled the end of harvest and the onset of winter, and was the highlight of the Celtic calendar. 

As Christianity spread, it absorbed the customs and traditions of Samhain, morphing them into Christian celebrations that coincided with the same period. 

In England, Halloween traditions slowly faded and were replaced by Guy Fawkes Day on November 5th. However, in Scotland and Ireland, Halloween continued to be celebrated with fervor.

The early settlers in the Americas brought these traditions with them, with Anglican and Catholic settlers both observing the holiday, but not the Puritans up in New England - they were generally against everything.

In conclusion, Halloween is deeply rooted in ancient traditions that have evolved and survived the passage of time.

O Superbird foi desenvolvido em túnel de vento para demonstrar a superioridade da Chrysler Corporation nas competições da NASCAR. A intenção era poder entrar na concessionária e poder levar para casa um modelo semelhante ao usado nas clássicas provas de corrida americanas 🇺🇸 

Estamos falando de uma versão modificada do Road Runner, projetado com traços do irmão Dodge Charger Daytona Talladega, mas ainda mais aerodinâmico. O objetivo dos dois era vencer o Ford Torifo e vencer na NASCAR.

O Superbird recebeu esse nome por sua associação ao desenho animado Road Runner (do papa-léguas). O nome aparece em um adesivo colocado nas laterais das aletas verticais do aerofólio traseiro, assim como uma imagem do personagem do desenho animado segurando um capacete de corrida.

Na década de 60, a NASCAR exigia que os veículos a serem usados nas corridas tinham de estar disponíveis para o público no geral e ser vendidas pelo menos 500 unidades, um requisito conhecido como homologação.

Porém com a virada para o ano 1970, foi aumentada a exigência para uma unidade produzida para cada 2 revendedores do fabricante nos EUA. Isso significou para a Plymouth a productives 1920 unidades do Superbird. Logo, como 1970 foi seu único ano de produção, faz desse muscle car ser uma verdadeira lenda 🤩

“As I made these images, I was becoming aware that my body was remembering what it had gone through and was going through,” the photographer Veronica Cruz (@veronicacrruz) says. “But I was also learning that it was okay to let it out and feel all of this without shame and without feeling like I had to hide it.”
.
In Little Earthquakes, the artist navigates childhood trauma through photography. Cruz was raped as a child. At the age of twelve, she had emergency brain surgery and was hospitalized due to an AVM, an abnormal connection between the arteries and veins in her brain.
.
Little Earthquakes is a work-in-progress, following the artist as she revisits the past and copes with the ongoing tremors reverberating in the aftermath of trauma. In some ways, the photographs represent an acknowledgment of the artist’s younger self—seen figuratively in an empty swing set.
.
Each time the artist herself appears throughout Little Earthquakes, whether she’s gazing directly at the camera or cradling her body, she reinforces the simple fact of her survival: she’s still here.

Vast and ever-shifting, the sea has always been emblematic of life’s dualities: beautiful but treacherous, clear yet vague, the beginnings and inevitable endings. “All at Sea” is a project focussing on the expansive and unpredictable nature of the ocean and linking it with our own human emotions. New year, new personal project.

My son and I recently discussed The Soul Hypothesis - the belief that souls exist and that humans have them. This immaterial part of a human being, often regarded as immortal, is impossible to prove or disprove, but a good portrait is universally thought capable of immortalising or carrying the soul, so he set me the challenge. I hand-painted a canvas backdrop over the holidays with the intention of making a series of new portraits this year. I am limited to simple setups that lean on purposeful, elegant posing – something of a test, as much of my photography falls into the environmental category. My backdrop can travel to locations, but its physical constraints will force me to work with just the person themselves—my only aid: light and an ability to relate.  

So here we go, some slides from my first session yesterday. Thank you, @hayward151, for assisting, and @cloudmaker_and_the_wolf, for bringing your boys and the whirlwind surrounding them to my backdrop. The last slide shows these wee legends turning the tables on their photographer - I love it.
