This has always been one of my favorite stretches, so I snuck in a few extra rounds after teaching today ❤️ 

I haven’t had much time or energy to train recently, but it feels good to sneak it small moments here and there when I can. Usually I try to prioritize my training, but right now I’m focused on making one of my biggest dreams come true: creating a home that I never want to leave and that I can bring my students and friends to 🥹

Somewhere along the way we got this idea that change is something to be feared. But what if, instead of fearing change, we actually gave ourselves the space to grow into something different, something unexpected. The unknown might be scary, but it’s also the only place that endless possibilities exist. No one knows what the future holds for any of us, so instead of spending another second focusing on the things I can no longer do, I’m going to spend each day finding out what I CAN do and being extremely grateful for those things. Because one day that will change, too. 

Thank you all so much for the love and support on my last post, I didn’t realize how much better I would feel after sharing with you all 🥲

I was inspired by @erin.skye.circus and @_fleximon to try this leg movement that they did in handstand, anyone else want to try it out?

I’m glad I knew exactly how much of a gift it was every time I was able to press into handstand, because it is a skill I will likely never be able to do again. 

It’s pretty amazing that I was able to do any of the harder handstand skills I did with a decaying bone in my wrist, and I’m so grateful I was able to push it as hard as I did when I did.

I got an MRI recently that confirmed my fears, and the bone in my wrist that is decaying has started to fragment and other parts of my wrist are becoming affected now as well. I didn’t need imaging to tell me things were getting worse, I could feel it. The good news is I can still do a few handstands here and there for now and demo basic skills in classes, but I will no longer be training handstands regularly or pushing to advance my skills at all. 

There’s too much to say about all of this, so I’m not going to say much else right now. I’m so lucky because I have a lot of amazing things happening in my life that I can focus on, and I can continue sharing my love for handstands through teaching and my students. 

At this point all treatment options are experimental, but don’t worry I will definitely be over here getting whatever experiments done that I can 🔬

Thanks for reading ❤️

My mom wants to learn how to lift weights, so here’s a recap of what we did on her first session! 

She has been teaching yoga for a long time and is very active, but her doctor recommended that she build more leg muscle.  She’s never really lifted weights (more than a few pound dumbbells), so we are building from the ground up with both compound and isolated exercises. 

We started with a standing warm up focusing on balance and leg mobility (I couldn’t film everything!)
Then we worked on hanging with supported hangs and scapular shrugs (grip strength is super important for older adults and also hanging is great for shoulder health + more)

Then she did:
3 x 10 Goblet Squats
2 x 10 RDLs
2 x 10 Leg Extension Machine (single leg)
2 x 10 Hamstring Curl (both legs)
2 x 15 Hip Abduction
2 x 10 Hip Adduction

Let me know if you found this interesting and I will film her again next time ❤️

I’ve been putting in a lot of work on the shop renovation and we’ve got a lot of material to move around including framing lumber, OSB, and a ton of bagged insulation. It’s not light work, but I enjoy the hard work and just putting my head down and going. @timberlandpro sent me their Morphix 5-Pocket Athletic pants and Morphix 6” Outdoor Boot to check out and I’ve been wearing them on the job.

The Morphix line is lightweight and flexible which I LOVE in workwear. I’m not a fan of the big stiff canvas type work pants. The pants have some clever features like a tape measure guard, doubled up cuffs so your boots don’t tear them up, and an extra little loop for your EDC to hang from.

And the boots are also flexible and lightweight with composite safety toes and waterproofing. They’re comfortable too which I assume comes from their Hover Spring midsole. If you’ve been looking for something more flexible and athletic that’s still tough then give these a look, link in my bio.

Photo by @FransLanting On February 15, we celebrate the 150th birthday of the great Antarctic explorer, Sir Ernest Shackleton. He died on remote South Georgia Island and that is where I photographed his grave where sailors visit to pay their respect to the man known as “The Boss.” Shackleton’s Endurance expedition is one of the great exploration epics of all time and it continues to inspire people, including me. The Boss will be commemorated on February 15 with a special ceremony in Westminster Abbey and the announcement of a new Endurance mission. Follow us @FransLanting and @ChristineEckstrom for more stories from Antarctica.

Photos by @FransLanting Today is Western Monarch Day. One of the most important overwintering sites for Western Monarch butterflies is just a few minutes from our Studio in Santa Cruz, California, along the coast. The butterflies there survived the extreme storm event we experienced yesterday, but whether they can weather the bigger issues they are confronted with remains a question.

The first image in this post was made this winter. It shows a small cluster of Monarchs in the same place where I made the second image in 1986. You can see the dramatic decline in the overwintering populations. The Western Monarch population has decreased more than 98% from the 1980s due to pesticide use in their summer areas, habitat loss, climate change, and other threats. Yet insects can bounce back quickly when conditions improve and people can help make that happen.

FYI, Western Monarchs spend their summers farther inland and go all the way to the Rocky Mountains. The Eastern Monarch population is much larger and overwinters in Mexico. The @NatGeo story about Monarchs published January 2024 photographed by my friend and colleague, @JaimeRojo, gives a great overview of what Monarchs are faced with. Check the organizations named below to learn more about how you can support Monarchs. And follow us @FransLanting and @ChristineEckstrom for more stories from the frontlines of our changing planet.

Photo by @FransLanting When chinstrap penguins display, they raise themselves to show off their black chinstraps while flapping their flippers and screaming at the top of their lungs. Sometimes this triggers a raucous response from other birds nearby. I was impressed by this male who had found a rocky perch that elevated him above his neighbors. Not sure if he succeeded in attracting any females, but he certainly looked like a performer. 

Things are different for visitors to Antarctica this year because of an outbreak of bird flu which has potentially disastrous consequences for penguins, other birds, and marine mammals. Visitor rules have been tightened up to prevent the spread of this highly contagious disease. Check my stories to see how I adapted my gear to operate within the new guidelines. And follow us @FransLanting and @ChristineEckstrom for more stories about our changing planet.

Photo by @HIPAae Frans was honored recently by the Crown Prince of Dubai, His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, with a special Photography Appreciation Award that recognizes Frans Lanting's life's work. During a ceremony held at Dubai's Opera House, Lanting and the Crown Prince were joined onstage by His Excellency Ali Khalifa bin Thalith, the Secretary General of HIPA, an influential international photo competition that celebrates the art of photography.

“Receiving HIPA’s Appreciation Award is an honor I accept with gratitude,” said Lanting. "I use my work to express wonder about the natural world and concern about the perils it faces. This award validates my belief that photography is a global language which can connect people everywhere.”

We’re happy to share that the incredible Frans Lanting will be on the @nature_org 2023 Global Photo Contest judging panel. Hailed as one of the great nature photographers of our time, Lanting’s influential work appears in numerous publications and exhibitions around the world. For more than three decades he has documented wildlife from the Amazon to Antarctica to promote understanding about the Earth and its natural history through images that convey a passion for nature and a sense of wonder and concern about our living planet.

Lanting has received honors and acclaim for his work. H.R.H. Prince Bernhard inducted him as a Knight in the Royal Order of the Golden Ark, the Netherlands’ highest conservation honor. He has received top honors from World Press Photo, the title of BBC Wildlife Photographer of the Year, and the Sierra Club’s Ansel Adams Award. He has been inducted as a Fellow of the Royal Photographic Society in London and is a recipient of Sweden’s Lennart Nilsson Award. Lanting acts as an Ambassador for the World Wildlife Fund Netherlands and sits on the National Council of the World Wildlife Fund USA, as well as on the Leadership Council of Conservation International, and on the International Board of WildAid. He is also a Trustee of the Foundation Board of the University of California Santa Cruz. He is a co-founder of the North American Nature Photographers Association and a Fellow of the International League of Conservation Photographers

Lanting’s mission is to use photography to help create leverage for conservation efforts ranging from local initiatives to global campaigns, through his publications, alliances, public appearances, and active support of environmental organizations. Along with his wife and partner Christine Eckstrom, Lanting recently launched Bay of Life: From Wind to Whales. This project explores and educates on the importance of California’s Monterey Bay ecosystem, which The Nature Conservancy identified as the “hottest hot spot for biodiversity in North America.”

Time is running out. Help give voice to nature and enter your best images by September 29th. Follow the link in our bio for more details.

Photo by @FransLanting Our friend Morad Tahbaz flew to freedom earlier today with four other American citizens after the Biden administration negotiated their release from prison in Iran. Morad is a cheetah conservationist with whom I had the pleasure to work while I documented Asia’s last cheetahs, which survive only in Iran. Morad, along with his colleagues from the Persian Wildlife Heritage Foundation, had been wrongly accused of using their camera traps to spy on military activities in Iran. 

We are grateful for Morad’s release, and thank everyone who played a role in this. But we also want to draw attention to the plight of his colleagues who remain in jail. Niloufar Bayani, Sepideh Kashani, Amirhossein Khaleghi, Taher Ghadirian, Sam Radjabi, and Houman Jowkar deserve to be freed as well to pave the way for new international cooperation efforts that will benefit big cats and people alike. 

Please spread the word and follow us @FransLanting and @ChristineEckstrom for more stories from the frontlines of conservation.

Recently I stayed at a hotel in London designed by Kit Kemp and I found myself loving the feeling of it without liking all of the elements of the decor, and I liked that I didn't like it all because it challenged my sense of taste.

It was an interesting experience about something that's been ringing a bell inside of me for a while-the fact that I could easily settle into a comfortable "pleasing" sense of taste, specifically for interiors. 

I think it's the Pinterest effect, probably a lack of confidence but also the fact that everywhere, homes feel less and less personal and more and more like they're coming out of a catalog and a specific "vibe," such as the "neutral countryside style" or the "LA mid century" or the more recent round shapes and soft colors. 

So now I am trying to build my confidence, because without confidence all we can do is... Sort of become generic. 

I also try to push myself to make "mistakes" and just go with my gut, which is really hard as I HATE being caught in a moment of bad taste 😂😂😂

Anyway here are a few images of what challenges me, and that I therefore should explore...

1/ the mix of prints. I actually love bold prints on sofas but I've always been too scared of regretting them to go ahead.

2/ photos and paintings in the kitchen. I'd love to see that more often!

3/ absolute mix of everything. So personal I love it. The computer shows it's an old image. I think homes in the 90s where quite good at capturing this sense of freedom...

4/ super bold and awesome matchy-matchy moment.

5/ joyfully not aligned plates on the wall.

6/ layering rugs (that I've always loved doing)

7/ loving the very bold wallpaper!

I don't have credits for these photos so let me know if you do! The first and last ones are from the @nmbr.16 by @kitkempdesignthread

It's so fun to discover another world, right at your doorstep. Yesterday on our way back from Devon we stopped in Broadhembury for a meal at the Drewe Arms and felt like we had stepped back in time. 

There really a bit of magic in these untouched English landscapes, and true joy in finding oneself in these uncomplicated interiors that look like everything we try to reproduce today. 

And there is also something wonderful about the old pubs, the locals sharing a beer at the bar with their friends (it was packed that day, I just took photos at the rare moments when the tables emptied) their dogs, their muddy boots and the warmth of it all... 

I discovered the Sunday Roast tradition when I moved to England and it's one of my favourite things. For the food, but also for the vibe. I completely forgot to take a photo of the meal because it was so good, but you can see in one of the photos that Lulu was certainly on it!

Let’s make a clarified whiskey sour!

For centuries, milk has been an essential ingredient in many culinary and beverage creations. From creamy soups to decadent desserts, milk has proven to be a versatile and beloved ingredient. However, one particularly interesting use of milk in the culinary world is its role in clarifying cocktails.

The process of clarifying cocktails using milk is not a new concept. In fact, it dates back to the early 19th century when the technique was first documented in Jerry Thomas’ 1862 book “How to Mix Drinks or The Bon Vivant’s Companion.” In this book, Thomas describes a technique called “milk clarifying” that uses milk to remove impurities and sediment from alcoholic mixtures.

The process itself is quite simple. It involves mixing milk with an acidic component such as lemon juice or vinegar and then combining it with the alcoholic mixture. As the mixture sits, the milk proteins bind with the impurities and sediment, causing them to separate and sink to the bottom. The result is a clear and visually appealing cocktail.

But why use milk in this process? The key lies in its composition. Milk contains casein, a protein that has strong binding properties. When combined with acid, the casein forms clumps that trap impurities and sediment, making it easier to remove them. This technique is similar to how egg whites are used in fining wines, although milk does not alter the flavor of the cocktail like egg whites can.

In conclusion, the history of clarifying cocktails using milk is a rich and time-honored tradition. From its first mention in a 19th-century cocktail book to its recent revival, this technique showcases the creativity and ingenuity of bartenders and mixologists throughout the ages. So the next time you enjoy a clear and pristine cocktail, remember the role that milk played in perfecting its appearance and taste. #milkpunch #clarifiedcocktail #whiskeysour

Also a member of the Ukrainian National Guard, he was detained by Russian troops during their occupation of Chornobyl two years ago.

She is heartbroken because she has not yet received any sign that he is alive. In November of last year, I photographed Viktoriia in an unmarked room to protect her and her husband's identities. She remains cautious and fearful for his fate.

I have been documenting the aftermath of the Chornobyl catastrophe for many decades. Since the Russian occupation after the start of the war in Ukraine, I have felt that my work remains unfinished. Following 10 months of negotiations, I was finally granted permission to re-enter the exclusion zone last October. This photograph will be included in my upcoming bilingual book BEUYS LAND, published by Edition Lammerhuber, which will be printed later this month and available April/May 2024.

Joseph Beuys, one of the most influential artists of the 20th century, talking about his art in the kitchen of his residence/studio at Drakeplatz in Düsseldorf. This photograph will be included in my upcoming book BEUYS LAND, published by Edition Lammerhuber, available late April of 2024. 

BEUYS LAND is the first book to centralize the natural landscape of the Lower Rhine and Joseph Beuys' purported birthplace, Kleve, within the artist's universe. In January 1978, I captured how Beuys revisited his past in Kleve and its Lower Rhine environs, the place where his journey began. My collection of photographs predominantly features Beuys amidst the characteristic landscape of dykes, ponds, poplar-lined avenues, and the local populace. These images palpably convey the interdependence of Beuys' art concept and the starkness of his landscape. The book also includes never-before-published photographs of Beuys and his wife Eva at their residence/studio in Düsseldorf and the Basler Fasnacht (Carnival of Basel) in Switzerland.

Let’s make Breakfast Cake a thing! 
We have been making Baked Oatmeal for more than a decade and a couple of years ago I started transforming that recipe into a cake. Key is to get the crust on the sides while still keeping that creamy oatmeal consistency in the center. And I always top with crunchy and sweet nuts and seeds on top. I really nailed it this morning so I thought I’d share the recipe:
…
Raspberry Breakfast Cake
…
2 eggs
500 ml / 2 cups oat milk
1 carrot, peeled and grated
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 tsp salt
1/2 tsp ground cardamom
1/2 tsp ground ginger
500 ml / 2 cups rolled oats
125 ml / 1/2 cup almond flour
3 tbsp buckwheat flour
1 tsp baking powder
200 g frozen raspberries
5 tbsp butter
5 tbsp honey
1 cup mixed seeds and nuts
…
Whisk the eggs in a mixing bowl. Add the milk, grated carrot and spices and whisk until combined. 
Add the oats, almond flour, buckwheat flour and baking powder and stir. Let sit for 10 minutes while setting the oven to 180C / 360F and lining a 20 cm / 8 inch baking tin with baking paper.
Add 1/3 of the raspberries to the bottom of the pan and stir in 1/3 of them into the oat batter.
Melt butter and honey and pour half of it into the oat batter. Pour the oats into the cake tin.
Add the nuts and seeds to the remaining melted honey butter and stir around until everything is coated. Spread the nuts and seeds on top of the oats and finish with the remaining raspberries. Bake in the oven for approx 35 minutes.
Serve in bowls with warm foamy oat milk. Enjoy!

If you need a recipe for an epic Tofu Cashew Masala, I’ve got you. 🧡
We first featured this recipe in Little Green Kitchen (swipe for cute kid) and since then we have cooked and tweaked it so so many times. Most recently this weekend when my mom came for dinner. This a great autumn meal and easy with the kids too. The original recipe only features chunks of tofu in the sauce but here we also added cauliflower and chickpeas.
This is the recipe 👇🏻
…
1. Start by letting 100 g (2/3 cup) cashew nuts soak in water.
2. Add 2 tbsp coconut oil to a large thick bottomed sauce pan on low/medium heat. Then add 1 chopped onion, 2 coarsely chopped garlic cloves, 1 finely chopped carrot, 1 big chunk fresh grated ginger, 1 tsp ground paprika, 1 tsp ground turmeric, 1 tsp ground cardamom, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Let sauté for 15 minutes until soft. 
3. Add 1 can of crushed tomatoes and let simmer for 15 more minutes. 
4. Take it off the heat and stir in the soaked cashew nuts and 250 ml water (you can also use cream or coconut cream) and use a hand mixer or heatproof blender to mix into a smooth sauce. 
5. Chop 1 small cauliflower into florets and dice 400 g / 14 oz tofu, dry with paper towels and add to the masala sauce along with 1 can of chickpeas. 
6. Let cook for 20 minutes. If you want an extra round flavor, stir in a big chunk of butter towards the end. Taste and season to your preference. Serve with cooked rice, lemon kale salad, a dollop of yogurt and toasted cashews. Enjoy!

1. Add coconut oil + coconut cream or ordinary cream to a sauce pan along with maple syrup and a pinch of salt.

So many of us are afraid to be ourselves and live our truth. This #song and #music video #Learn2Love is about the journey of self discovery and how it can make you feel lonely and isolated from everyone. Sometimes everything on the surface seems fine but below the surface is pain and you feel like you can’t breathe. Know that you’re not alone because I live that life for a very long time, afraid to be myself and what happens is you end up hurting everyone around you including yourself. It can take time for you to be ready to break through and have the strength to come out of darkness. I hope this song and video helps give you the confidence and strength to know your story can have a happy ending.
🧜🏼‍♂️I am no longer afraid 🧜🏼‍♂️

Flew to the land down under few days ago and I finally got to see Canberra. I must say this beautiful city is more quiet and laidback as compared to the vibrant and busy Sydney.

With many things in mind, visiting the National Gallery of Australia is on the top our list. Inside it we saw a lot of amazing masterpieces, but what struck me the most is James Turrell's 'Within without' Skyspace, a viewing chamber (or a "stupa") highlighted by turquoise water that surrounds it. This work shows the way we percieve the sky depending on the time of the day. They say it is at its most dramatic and complex form during dawn and dusk, marking the transition between day and night. Truly a remarkable work of art where nature, art, and architecture meet!

Excited to share more snaps and stories from the many things we saw and learned about this city. Big thanks to my travel partner @bigskynationph for keeping us connected everywhere we go with their travel wi-fi!

The beetle of rebirth 🪲🌞
At the end of November 2021 we were at a friends house about to leave when a golden beetle posed on my hand. It had been a long time since I saw one or at least payed close attention to it. I feel that many times we experience things often but don’t really give importance to them until we feel it is needed, then it becomes something meaningful. I started drawing the beetle on my notebook, carefully placed the insect on my finger it was holding my index with his tiny legs and thought about a ring! 
It gave me nostalgia of when the world was different and when we could travel, reminded me of our time in Egypt and in some way gave me hope, Cairo 2019 was also where I first saw a beetle ring from Tutankamon in the museum. I was amazed by Egyptian culture, art and mostly jewelry I thought it was cool but I never really questioned the symbolism of the elements and characters they used back then and why, but that day the golden beetle that posed on my hand made me curious and I started reaserching what it means, the meaning varies depending the culture but what I took from the Egyptians is that: the beetle symbolized the sun, a new day, a new opportunity, a cicle, knowing that the sun rises every day no matter what, rebirth! I thought the meaning was beautiful and felt like the right timing for me to start a process of “rebirth” this was right before 2021 ended, 

which had been a though year, I was not feeling too motivated, my grandma had just passed away a couple months before, and some little struggles that made me feel a bit stuck and not at my best. I didn’t know it at the time but from that day it was going to take 5 months to have the finished ring in my hands. Not because the actual process takes that long but in a way I wanted to have it ready whenever I felt better with myself, finishing this ring will mean to have a rebirth in a way, learnt the lessons, feel more motivated and in a better mental space.

I've always had a fascination with the underground world. At first, I was obsessed with being one of the few people who could go into a cave. As my career progressed what caves preserve began to be more important. The underground world can act as a time capsule holding artwork made by people long before us. Those ancient artists are sending us messages from the past. My friend @dustign calls them "love notes in a bottle" from our ancestors. 
Those artists in the past are speaking to us if we let them. They are not just telling us who they were, they are telling us who we all are.

This literally saved my life (and grades) in uni!! ⬇️✅💯👩🏼‍🎓

The Issue 😭: 
There’s SO MUCH more content to learn in uni than compared to high-school 📚
Furthermore, lecturers are often experts in their field, with years and years of experience, and when they get excited about what they’re teaching, they may go way way overboard, and share more than you need to know for your exams.

The Solution ✨: 
Focus on high-yield content. This is the content that will get you the most marks on your exam & assignments, and thus is the best use of your time.

You can find this through the learning objectives (usually at the start of each lecture or in your study guide) or by doing practice exams (as often the same questions/topics are repeated). 📝

An effective method I used was to turn each dot-point in the learning objectives into a question, then look through the lecture slides and other materials to answer the question, rather than reading every single page in the textbook or slides. ✅✅

The most IMPORTANT step in exam revision ✅💯🧠👩🏼‍🎓
-
WHAT IS TIMED PRACTICE? ⏰ 
This is where you do practice exams under full exam conditions (eg without notes, complete silence, reading time if applicable and no breaks).

This is a MUST do when preparing for exams because: 
📕 It helps you learn how to APPLY the knowledge. You could memorise the whole textbook and still do poorly on the exam if you don’t learn how to respond to questions the way examiners want you to. 
This is why so many students often complain that they get questions on the exams that they weren’t prepared for or have never seen before.
Exam questions often don’t ask you to just regurgitate definitions word for word, instead they will present a real world example (and likely a new one every time) to see if you can apply your knowledge to solve the problem! 
By doing practice questions and comparing your exams to the marking scheme, you will develop this skill quickly, and be prepared for ANY question you could get. 

📕 It helps you perfect your exam technique. By replicating the exam conditions, you will develop your own rhythm in terms of what you do during reading time, how long you spend on each questions, what you do for questions you don’t know etc. 
This is a skill itself, entirely seperate from knowing the content, that needs to be developed. 

📕 It giving you an idea of how much time you have & how quick you need to be!! Exams can be long, and being able to pace yourself and stay focused for the entire duration is something that also needs to be developed with practice.

The Hack: SPACED REPETITION 📆
This is a highly effective revision technique where you review content at regular, increasing intervals. 

For example: 
Say you learn something in class that day.
You would then review the content… 
—> when you get home from school 
—> again that weekend 
—> the weekend after 
—> in a fortnight 
—> in a month 
—> in 3 months.

To take it one step further and make it even MORE effective, you should try to review using Active Recall, especially Practice Questions (eg from the textbook, past year papers). 

This will help you start perfecting your exam technique EARLY, help you commit the information to long-term memory, and understand the content on a deeper level.

So that when it comes to exam season, you won’t even NEED to revise because you’ll know everything!! ✅🏆💯

1️⃣ Be willing to give everything a go 🙋🏼‍♀️- if you haven’t done it before or unsure, don’t be scared to ask for help! Tell your supervisor that you’ll give it your best shot, but may need to be supervised or taught.

.
2️⃣ Close the Loop 🔁- at the end of every meeting or conversation, report back what you understood as actions you need to do & by when. Then, as you complete those actions, report back to inform the person they are done & any other information that might be useful (eg if doing research, what the main findings were. If reaching out to someone, what their response was).

Similarly, if you need help with something/are stuck, or there is something blocking your progress, let them know too (eg “the contact is away on leave and will be back Monday, which is when I will follow up again”).

Don’t wait for them to have to chase you to figure out that the task has been done or has been held up.

Closing the loop helps build trust. It lets your supervisor know that you are reliable and they can delegate important tasks to you.

HOW TO STUDY EFFECTIVELY 🏆:
1️⃣ Use Active Study Methods - these are study methods that force you to engage with the content, doing some sort of physical or mental process. 🤓 

It leads to greater retention of info, understanding, and ability to apply theory! 
It also means that you can learn SO MUCH MORE in MUCH LESS time. ✅
.
Examples include:
🧠 Active Recall (e.g. Flashcards, Blurting, Application Questions)
🧠 Mind-Maps & Drawing Diagrams 
🧠 Teaching The Material to Others 
🧠 Loci Method 
🧠 Practice Exams 
.
2️⃣ Eliminate Distractions & Stay Focused - make sure you’re thinking only about the work in front of you to maximise retention. My favourite ways to do this are:
💯 Study Timelapse 
💯 Lofi-Beats & noise cancelling headphones 
💯 Quiet, low-stimulus environment (e.g. library, dedicated study room) 
💯 Chew gum (it actually works!)
💯 App Blockers/Downtime settings on your phone 
.
3️⃣ Plan Your Sessions - by planning your study sessions out before you start, you will be able to prioritise what needs to be done, stay on track, and even get additional benefits without more time studying!
.
To make sure your study session is the best it can be: 
⏰ Use time-blocking (allocate a set amount of time for each activity, to create a sense of urgency. Otherwise it will expand to fill the whole time)
⏰ Start with a quick-win (easy subject or small homework task)to get the dopamine flowing; then move onto your most challenging topic whilst energy levels & focus is still high 
⏰ Interleave your subjects by studying smaller blocks of multiple subjects rather than 1 big block of one subject (e.g. 1 hour each of Math, Science, English rather than 3 hours of Math). This will help you remember MORE and perform better on exams, as proven by research 👏🏽

Still thinking about my visit to their new DTLA space. Do yourself a favor. First, follow @breakfast_dreams. Then, keep an eye out for his schedule. Make plans. Circle the day on your calendar. Then wait patiently until that day comes and you can wrap your hands around the breakfast sandwich of your dreams.

In all seriousness, it was truly awesome to finally meet @liljoshygram and try his cooking after being #InternetFriends for so long. It was just extra special that the food was so damn good.

A little blip of light between therapy appointments. 😜

Sometimes a work lunch is a protein bar. But sometimes work lunch is a phenomenal meal at @angeliniosteria. Those times are clearly better.

Had the pleasure of having a meeting today at @angeliniosteria where I got to once again swoon over simple yet outstanding dishes like their phenomenal tuna tartare, the warm octopus salad (maybe my favorite dish there) and their famous lasagne verde. Work, suffice to say, did not suck today. One of the best Italian restaurants in a city full of them.

LA is truly becoming the food capitol of the country. They’re coming for your bagels, they’re coming for your hot chicken, they’re coming for your pasta, and NOW they’re coming for your BBQ, and @mooscraftbarbecue is absolutely as good as it gets. The brisket, the pork ribs, the sausage, the corn, the mac, the slaw… all 10/10. Bonus points for a great draft beer list. And when you’ve got Carolina style sauce as an option? 😅 Congrats to the whole team. Looking forward to trying the pulled pork, the turkey and of course the beef ribs.

It’s a damn shame that in 2021, technology hasn’t advanced enough for me to get @bettinapizzeria delivered from Santa Barbara to LA. The first words out of my mouth after I took my first bite were, “What pizza is better than this? Seriously.” Ever since I had it, when I crave pizza— I crave Bettina. And that’s a problem.

Heute geht es um Selbstvermarktung -
Sicherlich ein spannendes Thema für viele, vor Allem in einer Zeit in der jede fünfte Person aus der GenZ sagt: Traumberuf Content Creator.

Alles berufliche mache ich intuitiv, mit meiner Freundin Leni und seit 3 Monaten wuchs die two-women show mit Julia. Ansonsten ist kein Management, keine PR oder andere Partei involviert.
Eine Strategie verfolgen wir für meine Karriere nicht, wir handeln nach bestem Wissen und Gewissen. Ideen für neue Projekte kommen immer sehr organisch. 
Mich interessiert es jedoch sehr, wie es andere erfolgreiche Frauen machen,wie sie ihre Karriere aufbauen und welche Tipps sie für euch und mich haben. 
Deswegen habe ich uns eine Expertin in Sachen Selbstvermarktung und Brandbuilding eingeladen… @dagibee 💗

Ist es euer Traum Content creator zu werden?

Als Kind wollte ich Modedesignerin werden (schon seitdem ich denken kann, liebe ich Mode, vor allem faszinieren mich die Gefühle, die Kleidungsstücke in mir auslösen. Jedes Teil bringt etwas anderes in mir hervor und verleiht mir eine gewisse Stärke. Denn dadurch kann ich entscheiden, wie ich von Anderen wahrgenommen werde.) Dann wollte ich Psychologin werden, denn die Gespräche, die ich mit den Psychologinnen führte, zeigten mir immer, welch emphatische und intelligente Frauen sie sind. Ich wollte sein wie sie. Dann wusste ich, ich werde Model. Ohne dieses Ziel zu hinterfragen, verfolgte ich es und inzwischen stelle ich mir die Frage: wieso eigentlich? Ich glaube, es liegt an der Sichtbarkeit der Frauen in diesen Berufen. Sie sind für mich präsent und von der Gesellschaft zelebriert. Vor allem Models beeindruckten mich: Ich wollte so Stark, Selbstständig, Selbstbewusst, Wohlhabend und geliebt sein wie die Frauen, die ich täglich in Magazinen, im Fernsehen und anderen Medien wahrnehmen konnte. Eins ist klar, ein junges Gehirn wird stark davon geprägt, wie es sozialisiert wird. Und das bleibt natürlich auch im Erwachsenenalter so, unsere Außenwelt formt uns. Also habe ich mir die Frage nach meinen Möglichkeiten so beantwortet, dass gewisse Machtpositionen nur Männern zustehen. Inzwischen stelle ich mir auch eine andere Frage, die mit meiner Identität als Frau zusammenhängt: Ich habe seit meiner Geburt eine Krankheit, eine Malrotation des Darms. Ich habe damals viel Zeit im Krankenhaus verbracht, meinen Symptomen wurden kein Glauben geschenkt. Es ist erschreckend, dass ich fast sterben musste, bis meine Krankheit diagnostiziert wurde. Die Folgen dieser Erfahrung spüre ich bis heute. Ich frage mich also:… Wäre es anders gelaufen, wenn ich ein Junge gewesen wäre ? Denn abgesehen davon, dass Mädchen weniger geglaubt wird, ist die Ungleichbehandlung von Frauen weiterhin Teil unserer Realität. Ärzt*innen wurden primär am männlichen Körper ausgebildet, genauso wie viele Studien auf Männern basieren, denn Männlichkeit wurde als Norm definiert. In der heutigen Folge bei @g.spot.podcast Spreche ich drüber wie viel Raum uns Frauen in unserer Gesellschaft geboten wird.

The truth about ALMOND CROISSANTS🥐

Croissants go stale so quickly!! So here’s what you can do when you have a few extra ones laying around :) Or if you don’t want to pay the almond croissant premium LOL.

✨Ingredients:
•1 cup water
•1/3 cup sugar

•4 croissants
•25 gr unsalted butter
•60 gr cane sugar
•60 gr almond flour
•1 medium egg
•1 tsp vanilla extract
•sliced almonds
•powder sugar for dusting

In a small saucepan, bring water and 1/3 cup of sugar to a boil to make a syrup. Cool down. Preheat oven 350°F and cut croissants in half. In a bowl, combine softened unsalted butter with sugar. Then add almond flour, combine, and lastly add egg and vanilla to form an almost paste. Brush sugar syrup on the inside and outside of the croissant and then spread the almond paste inside. Close the croissant and spread more paste on top and top off with sliced almonds. Bake for 15-18 mins, cool down, and dust with powdered sugar. Enjoy!

EASY SPICY TUNA POKE BOWLS🐟🥣🌶️ (full recipe below)

I think spicy tuna bowls are the new hot girl meal. I know raw fish can be a little intimidating, so make sure you buy previously flash-frozen fish from a grocer that you trust! I buy my ahi tuna filets from @Sprouts and eat them the day of.

✨Ingredients (4 servings) // about 60gr protein per portion 

-1 1/2 lbs raw ahi tuna (2 steaks)
-1 1/2 tbsp sriracha
-2-3 tbsp aminos or soy sauce
-3 tbsp Kewpie mayonnaise
-1 cup edamame
-1 hass avocado
-1 cup uncooked sushi rice
-1 tbsp mirin
-1 tbsp rice vinegar
-1/2 tbsp sesame oil
-1 tsp salt
-1 tsp sesame seeds

Pat dry ahi tuna and cut it into 1-inch cubes. Place inside a bowl and add sriracha, aminos, and mayo. Stir until combined, cover, and rest refrigerated for at least 15 minutes. Cook sushi rice according to the instructions on the package. Warm up frozen edamame by pouring boiling water on top and letting it sit for 5 minutes. Slice avocado or mash it; feel free to season it however you like. Add mirin, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and salt to cooked rice. Stir and use it as a base for your bowl. Continue plating by adding about 4 ounces of tuna, 1/4 cup of edamame, and 1/4-1/2 an avocado. Portions are up to you! Top with sesame seeds, and feel free to add any extra sauce and seasonings like furikake. Enjoy immediately and save any leftovers in a tight-lid container in the fridge. Eat the same day.

The Nightingale Building – today known as the Nightingale Wing of Sydney Hospital – was the site of the first nursing school in Australia. On the request of colonial politician Henry Parkes, British nurse Florence Nightingale sent Lucy Osburn and five other nurses to NSW to establish the school of nursing.
 
Architect Thomas Rowe designed the sandstone and polychrome-brick Gothic Revival building with Nightingale’s input.
 
Visitors on Sydney Open will see the Lucy Osburn-Nightingale Museum, which has a collection of medical equipment, records, implements and pathology that provides a look into the history of nursing and medicine in Australia from 1788.

The other day was my day for the “dreaded Glucose test” that typically happens between week 24-28 of pregnancy. I went an alternative route during my pregnancy with Rell so I never experienced the glucola drink, BUT this time my doctor offered a natural alternative to the standard glucose drink, called the Fresh Test. (I have no affiliation with this) It ended up not being so “dreaded” of an experience after all.
It still creates that glucose load with 50g of sugar, but it tastes like a refreshing lemonade and it’s non-gmo, with no additives and preservatives, and I didn’t feel icky at all. (It does warn that some may experience side effects— that is a lot of sugar at once!) I was even able to eat a boiled egg before my test as mine was a non-fasting test, but of course follow what your provider suggests! I mixed the powder with some water and drank it an hour before my blood draw. The visit to the lab was easy. And now I just wait for my results! 🙏🙏
__
I wanted to share this quick experience and just bring awareness that there is a natural alternative that you can explore with your doctor when it’s time for your Glucose Test during pregnancy. Obviously this is an important step for mama and baby during pregnancy, so this is up to you and your doctor, but I personally love learning about other alternatives that feel right to me.

SAVE this for a quick Egg Free Breakfast option!
Rell has never liked eggs- never. Which led us to exploring if there was something instinctual behind it and we learned she had an egg allergy when she was a baby. The great news is, she can eat eggs baked into things, and I think she’s growing out of this allergy BUT she still dislikes eggs. Obviously eggs are an easy and awesome way for quick protein for breakfast— especially in the form of egg bites! SO it was time to explore a new Quick Protein option for breakfast and she LOVES these Sausage bites! We call them “muffins” 😉 Wether you’re catering to an egg allergy in your home or not- this is a great breakfast alternative to keep in your fridge or freezer for when you need a quick and healthy breakfast grab!
*I make these gluten free- and they can easily be made dairy free!
—
RECIPE
-1lb ground Breakfast Sausage
-1-2 cups finely chopped broccoli florets (optional, but a great way to add greens into breakfast!)
-1 cup your choice of gluten free flour (I used Bob’s Red Mill Paleo All Purpose mix)
-1 tsp baking powder
-1 cup shredded cheese- I use goat cheddar. You can simply make this dairy free with a dairy free cheese alternative!
-3/4 cup Almond Milk (or your choice of milk)
—
•Sauté 1 lb breakfast sausage & finely chopped broccoli florets in avocado oil until sausage is fully cooked 
•In a mixing bowl, add 1 cup gluten free flour, 
1 tsp baking powder, & mix together. 
•Then add 1 cup shredded cheese. Mix all together.
•Add and mix in cooked sausage & broccoli to the dry mix. 
•Add 3/4 cup of Almond Milk. Mix together well.
•Scoop mixture into pre-greased cupcake pan- I use avocado oil spray. 
•Bake for 20-25 minutes at 400 degrees.

Enjoy these!! You can store in the fridge for a few days, or freeze them for when needed! Approved by my toddler— and my husband and I love them too!

A MUST on your weekly meal rotation! SAVE for this delicious Sausage, Kale, Ravioli soup. This was inspired by another recipe I saw via Instagram, but I made some upgrades to make it Gluten Free and healthier! We use a Grain Free Ravioli- but you can use a gluten free ravioli/tortellini, or any type of Gluten Free Pasta! I suggest a simple pasta if you’re wanting to make this Dairy Free.
Oh, and obviously, wait til it’s cooled down to eat— I basically burned my mouth in the making of this reel!😂
__
Ingredients
-1 lb Spicy or Mild Italian chicken Sausage— I buy this from the meat counter at the grocery store. 
-1 small yellow onion, diced
-5-7 cloves garlic, minced
-3 Tbsp Gluten Free flour (I use Bob’s Red Mill Paleo all purpose flour mix)
-1 tsp dried basil
-½ tsp dried oregano
-a pinch of cayenne (omit if you’re trying to keep the spice level low)
-1 tsp (gluten free) hot sauce (I use Sweet Baby Ray’s hot sauce- equivalent to Franks)
-½ tspmustard powder
-1 cup full fat Coconut Milk (I prefer it canned)
-32 oz Chicken Broth (I used Kettle & Fire)
-2-3 cups organic kale, chopped
-1 Box of @cappellos Grain Free Ravioli (I find this in the freezer section, and try to thaw for a bit before cooking) OR use your choice of gfree pasta or gluten free tortellini!
-Pink Salt and Pepper to taste. 
-optional: pinch red pepper chili flakes
Instructions
-Spray Large pot with Avocado Oil, and cook the sausage (remove the casing if using sausage links) and diced onions, and garlic over medium-high heat until the onions and garlic are softened and the sausage is cooked through.  -Add your gluten free flour and cook for about 2 minutes, to cook the flour in.
-Add basil, oregano, cayenne, hot sauce, and mustard powder. Stir to combine. -Add the chicken broth, add and stir in Coconut Milk. While stirring, “clean” the bottom of the pot.
-Bring to a boil, (if using regular gluten free pasta, add it in now to cook while it’s boiling) Reduce to a simmer. -Add ravioli to cook about 5-8 minutes, depending on its cooking time. Bring to a simmer.
-Add the Kale, and stir it into cook. -Add in red chili flakes, pink salt, pepper to taste!

😞 This is difficult for me to write. Last week I stepped outside my comfort zone and shared a very personal goal of mine to have my book make the New York Times Best Seller list. 😱 The list isn’t released until this Sunday but my editor at NatGeo said publishers find out a few days early and she would call me right away. I got the call. She shared the sad news that I didn’t make the list. 😔 I kept it together on the call..but the tears came hard as soon as we said bye. I’m surprised I care so much about this. I cried for about 5 minutes and after a great pep talk from a supportive husband was able to pick myself up. 🥹

💛 I want to make it clear that above all, I’m extremely proud of my book and don’t want this to cast any sort of shadow over the past 4 years that were nothing but a positive experience of writing and creating this treasure for families all around the world. 🌎 The quality of my hard work is definitely more important than the accolade of New York Times Best Seller. But I think, if I were to try my best to explain why I’m feeling so sad and even slightly embarrassed it’s because 2 things: I’ve never wanted anything like this for myself. I’m sure so many other mothers out there can relate. I endlessly cheer and support my family, but rarely do I want something so purely for myself. This was that for me. ❤️

Secondly, the Bucket List community has rallied so hard behind me. I have have felt it every day of this journey. I was excited to celebrate this achievement all of us together. ❤️💙💚 You’ve done so much for me. Thx to you, we’ve surpassed NatGeo’s presale records. I’m going to keep my head up and focus on the positive. There’s still chance I may make the list in future weeks so I’ll keep trying my best. Positive reviews of my book on Amazon and Goodreads help so much. ⭐️ I want you to know that I screenshot your thoughtful reviews and every time you share my book on Instagram in such cute creative ways and add it to a journal I’ve been keeping of this book publishing journey. Thank you for being a part of my story and all the ups and downs. This day is a down for me. But I know I can get back up..❤️ Jess

Born & brought up in the suburbs of Sydney to Lebanese immigrant parents Lina started off her career as a Secondary School Teacher and worked her way up to school Principal of an independent school.

Growing up the daughter of immigrants, emersed in a world of clashing cultures, food became the most ideal way to link both worlds and form an Australian – Lebanese identity she was proud of.
Over the last few years, Lina has created content for some of Australia’s largest brands and companies from Kenwood to ABC Everyday to Woolworths and Ebay Australia. Again you have deliciously tender zucchini, that are also carefully hollowed out and filled with a mixture of rice, minced meat, tomatoes and spices. Unlike my last stuffed zucchini recipe, however, this one is gently simmered to perfection in a flavourful tomato sauce. In this video I also stuffed a few mini capsicums, which is delicious too 👌🏼

250g mince
1 cup rice, washed 
1/2 tsp baharat
1/2 tsp pepper
1/2 tbsp salt
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 med tomato, finely chopped 
1 tbsp ghee 

12 grey / Lebanese zucchini 
300g lamb loin chops or neck 
Olive oil 
1 bulb garlic
125g cherry tomatoes, halved 
1 onion, sliced into thin rings 
4 cups water or veg stock 
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 tsp sugar 
1 tsp salt 

To prepare stuffing, add all ingredients in a bowl & mix until well combined. 

In a large jug add stock or water, tomato paste, 1 tsp sugar & 1 tsp salt. Mix & set aside. 

Cut the top off the zucchini and carefully shave off the dried tips at the end without removing flesh. Hollow out the zucchini carefully removing the flesh. You want to create a cavity for stuffing without bursting or breaking zucchini.

Wash zucchini & set aside to dry.

1 small onion, diced
500g beef mince
1 1/2 tsp baharat 
1 tsp pomegranate molasses 
1 tbsp pine nuts 
Salt & pepper

Heat olive oil in a fry pan. Add pine nuts and toast until they just turn a golden brown. Add the onion & sauté until soft. Add the mince, stir to brown and remove large lumps of meat. Add baharat, molasses & salt/pepper to taste. Stir through. Return pine nuts to pan. Combine well. Set aside to cool. 

ᴢᴜᴄᴄʜɪɴɪ 
Once stuffing has cooled, use fingers to gently stuff each zucchini. 

In a large fry pan, melt 2 tbsp ghee. Fry the zucchini, turning frequently, in batches until they just change colour. Return all the zucchini to pan & cover with just enough water. Bring to a gentle boil & leave to simmer for 20 min. (Place a heat proof plate on the zucchini to keep them submerged). 

At 20 min the zucchini should have softened. Remove from water & set aside. Do not discard the cooking water. Strain it & set aside. (There should be about 2 cups of liquid, if less top it up with more water to make 2 cups).

2 lt goat’s milk yoghurt

On the stovetop, pour your goat’s yoghurt into a large pot and add the reserved zucchini cooking water and salt. Add your washed rice and stir frequently for 10 minutes on low heat. Add the cornflour dissolved in water. Stir for a minute or two. The yoghurt will begin to thicken. 

In a small frypan, melt the ghee or butter. Add the crushed garlic and mint. Cook stirring for two minutes. Set aside. 

Place stuffed zucchini in the yoghurt. 

Add the mint & garlic to the yoghurt. Cook, stirring gently for another 3 - 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

If Jesus. That’s the title of a series of teachings I’ve been doing at our church this January. If Jesus is here — if Jesus is good — if Jesus is Lord – then that changes everything. Those three ideas are like a three-legged stool. If any one of those concepts is missing (or even cut a little short), our entire idea and belief in who Jesus is will simply topple over. We need each of these three attributes to be complete and strong if we’re to grow in our understanding of the true Jesus. And if we do, it changes everything — our outlook on life and its challenges, our decisions, our relationships, our purpose, and eventually our eternity.

Which of these three attributes of Jesus do you think are most misunderstood or missing in our lives: his presence, his goodness, or his authority and power as Lord? Take the poll and drop in your thoughts.

“Furniture… lots of furniture!” @klekktic 

The Matrix is one of my all time favourite movies. It came out 25 years ago, inspiring a whole generation of filmmakers, visual effects artists and stunt coordinators. 

This is my take on the iconic “guns, lots of guns” scene where Neo & Trinity enter The Matrix to prepare for battle. I thought this would be a fun and innovative way of showcasing a furniture brand. Having different products from the @klekktic collection flying into the Matrix. 

To execute this @shravanraoo & I shot for a full 12 hours in a studio in Dubai. Heba, the founder of Klekktic, who plays Trinity in this video, helped coordinate all of the Klekktic pieces to be shipped to the studio. We then placed each item one by one filming the product and then removing it. This allowed us to create the effect of different pieces flying into place.

@Klekktic is a beautiful UAE based brand. They have a minimal design aesthetic that is clean and elegant. The best part about their products is they are customizable. For example, the desk at the start of the video I fully customized from a dining room table into an office desk with draws and storage. Bed sizes, table lengths, mirror finishings etc can all be customized to fit your space size and preference. 

My home project is really starting to take shape. It’s been a long time coming but it’s been worth the wait. More coming on that soon…

Special shout out to @shravanraoo who helped me film this and then worked on the kick ass visual effects. 

What do you guys think of the video? Drop a Matrix reference comment below if you liked the video!

What do you know about Venezuela? 🇻🇪 

Back in July I had the opportunity to spend a few weeks in Venezuela creating something special for @beautifuldestinations. 

As 2023 has been the year of AI, I’ve been wanting to innovate and figure out a way to combine new immersive AI visuals with travel content. My thinking was that we’d be going to a place that not many people have seen before, Angel Falls in Canaima National Park, and if we could combine never before seen AI content with a truly out of this world destination then we’d have all the ingredients for something special. 

The first person I called was @andras.ra who’s been diving into short form AI content this year. We’ve worked together a ton over the years and he’s an editing magician. The idea developed into a FPV Drone only concept where we’d play with generative AI to add little details into the video. @reme_martyr then joined the team to execute the aerials, he killed it! As the concept got bigger so did the team with @alexislefrene , @shravanraoo , @andres.visual and @bahaamalaeb joining the squad. 

What started as a fun idea turned into a full blown innovation project, looking to create the world’s first AI supported Tourism Campaign. By tapping into unique visual styles the hope was to create something that would make some noise and spark a conversation about the destination.

What you wouldn’t know is that 40 years ago my parents lived in Venezuela. At that time, Caracas was a global advertising hub. Ironically, my Dad was working in the same field that I am now. Back then he was one of the few photographers paving the way through dark room visual effects, that’s before photoshop existed! It was very cool to be there 40 years later trying to do something similar, as Venezuela announces itself as a new and exciting Tourism destination. I love the country’s new branding “open to the future” and I hope this video gives you a glimpse of that future as well as the future of content and where I think it’s going. 

This video is quite the rollercoaster so fasten your seat belt and enjoy the ride…

Puppies & Pilates 🐕🦾

For the last month I’ve been doing Pilates with the awesome Gaby Noble founder of @exhalepilateslondon, as a way to improve my strength training. Prior to this year I had no idea what Pilates was and always thought of it as a workout for women. I couldn’t have been more wrong. 

As I wait for Project Apartment to get fully underway I’ve turned my empty home into a Pilates Studio. This is just one of the many brutal exercises that are getting me lifting heavier than I ever have and feeling more recovered each day. 

There’s a big reason why a lot of elite male athletes, celebrities and performers have added Pilates to their training regimes 👇🏽

- Improves your muscle to mind connection. I am so focused on the movements and getting the muscles to do exactly what it needs to do. Something I never think about when weightlifting. 

- Improves core strength. Killer ab workout every single time!

- Helps me lift more, squat deeper, recover quicker, lets the joints and muscles breathe. This is why it’s been the perfect supplement to my strength training. 

- Limits injuries so I can keep pushing towards my goals without set backs. My flexibility and mobility has completely changed in 1 month. Again, allowing me to lift heavier, get stronger and recover faster. 

- Improves your posture & helps keep a healthy spine. Both are key for the work I do and ultimately make me move better and with more ease.

This is just the start of my Pilates journey but I’ve been loving it so far with Gaby Noble @exhalepilateslondon . If you’re interested in trying it out shoot her a message. She’s the best in the space and trained the likes of Harry Styles, Kate Moss, Giancarlo Esposito & Christian Eriksen.

Rainy mornings call for some baking! 🌧️ This method of making banana bread in an 8x8 might be the best idea yet. It cooks so perfectly and there’s more of that perfectly crunchy sweet top! 

After-School Banana Bread 🍌🍞

Ingredients
 * Nonstick baking spray, for the pan
 * 8 tablespoons (1 stick) salted butter, melted and cooled, plus softened butter for serving
 * 1 cup packed light brown sugar
 * 2 large eggs, beaten
 * 1 1/2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
 * 4 to 5 very ripe bananas, mashed (I like to leave them a little chunky)
 * 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
 * 1 teaspoon baking soda
 * 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
 * 1/2 cup chopped pecans 
 * 1 to 2 tablespoons granulated sugar as needed

Directions
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray an 8 x 8-inch pan with nonstick baking spray or line it with parchment paper.
2. In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment (or in a large bowl with a handheld electric mixer), beat together the butter, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla until well blended. Add the bananas and mix until combined.
3. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and beat just until combined. Add the pecans (if using) and mix until combined.
4. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread it evenly. Sprinkle the granulated sugar over the top. I like to cover the whole surface completely with sugar; use as much as you’d like.
5. Bake until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes. Let the bread cool slightly in the pan on a rack. Slice and serve warm with butter.
6. When completely cooled, cover the pan with foil and store at room temperature for up to 2 days.

My mother begins her letters with an update on the weather. It’s sunshine and 20 degrees, and the strawberries in the garden are ripening, or it’s partly cloudy and almost 6 degree, at least when the sun peeks through, and I’ve been pruning back the rose bushes. It’s the sort of beginning that makes me feel like I’m right there next to her. So today, with the surprise sprinkling of big fluffy white snowflakes, and plummeting temperatures, I updated her on the weather first thing as I called her this morning to hear her heartbeat next to mine. I held my daughter’s hand as she rested on my chest next to the furry four legged Mr Whiskey, who was not at all eager to start the day. I had buttermilk pancakes on the agenda, a beautiful bi product of all the homemade butter I made yesterday, but all she wanted was morning snuggles, so we just rested, with hands and paws entwined, and my mother on the line. We talked about the weeks ahead, and I listed all the delicious everyday treats I’d make with the emerging wild garlic I spotted last week on a drive around my old neighbourhood in Tisbury. Wild garlic pesto, pickled wild garlic flowers that I’d serve with baked trout, and wild garlic scones etc, you get the picture. It was time to throw on our coats and tighten the scarf, as we walked to school in the gloomy weather. Will you send me a picture of Spring, my mother asked as we said our goodbyes and I love yous, on the phone. So here it is, a little reminder that behind a grey cloud there is always sunshine, and after snow on the first day of March, Spring is imminent, and that’s something to take comfort in on this very day. If you want to join me this spring for a food photography workshop, send me a DM and I’ll pop more information over to you. And speaking of Spring, I cannot wait for my end of March fully immersion photography workshop in Florence! And if you’re waiting for the next newsletter, hang in there, it’s on its way;) xx

I could fill books on the topic of why I love living in England so much, but one of them is being able to bring in baskets of evergreens, wilted bracken, and blossoming flowers in November and February and June alike. Growing up in Norway the white winters were beautiful and definitely had its magical moments, but I love going for winter walks amongst evergreens and flowering snow drops in January while my mother tells me on the phone it’s yet another day of ice and -20 at the fjord island my parents live. I could fill baskets on end with flowering gorse, ivy, holly and bare winter branches with a few brown wilted leaves. Although flowers are beautiful, give me a branch with or without green leaves any day. So our little cottage, my garden studio and car are always filled with evidence of my never ending love for nature, bringing the outside in. It simply brings joy, the everyday kind, that cost nothing, but truly makes all the difference. Which brings me back to yesterday’s launch of my new ongoing stillife series, of wilted leaves and twisted twigs, a homage to the muted tones of the wilted botanical world of the English countryside. #myenglishcountryside

With a birthday breakfast tray in bed, feet wrapped around a hot water bottle, staying warm in the early morning chill, I re-read a book; “Constance Spry the Fashion for Flowers” by the brilliant @shaneconnollyandco , bought on a visit to the @gardenmuseum a few summers back during their Constance Spey exhibition. Like so many, I’m enthralled by her work, and was beyond delighted when I uncovered her cookbook, in a dusty pile of used books in a cardboard box, in a local antique bookshop. She was such a multi faceted and very ahead of her time, woman. She’s often on my mind when I create my floral stillifes. Last year I began a series inspired by old yellowed tear sheets of botanical prints, gathering leaves, insects, cones and seeds, creating these quiet flat lays in my studio. Those who know me well, smile at me as I duck underneath fences s d leap across the street to catch just the right wilted leaf that has caught my eye. I wedge a few in between handwritten pages in my journal, but most end up in glass jars that I keep in my studio. Gnarly, twisted, wilted, and broken, I love me a good leaf with just the right curve or stem. I haven’t show these more muted stillifes of mine till today, but since this is my birthday and the beginning of something new, I’ll start sharing this ongoing series of leaves, twigs and insects, as visual musings of the botanical world if you will. If you like them, there’s a couple available as limited edition prints on my website now. Here’s to the quiet beauty of the wilted leaf, and the twisted twig. #mycottagestudio

The sun peeked through every now and then this morning, and it felt like a warm hug. It was needed, it’s been raining for what feels like weeks on end, and although I don’t mind a drizzle or soaking, I turned my face towards the sun like moth to the flame. It’s the first day of the week, and although my birthday isn’t until Wednesday, I’m calling it my birthday week, and will unashamedly celebrate with little sprinkles of happiness every day of this week. Between a mug of tea at my daughter’s morning school assembly, and a well brewed coffee from the brilliant @bean_shot_coffee in town I stood on a street corner, when someone shook their head, and stopped themselves from saying what was on their mind and said: “It doesn’t matter”…and walked away. And I thought to myself, everything matters! Every moment of every day matters, everything we have in our hearts that we want to say, matters, the time we spend with someone else matters, we all matter, and life is way too short and way too long to not do, say or be, what we know in our hearts matter to us. I stood there in a small patch of sunlight, re-listening to those very words in my head. It’s the words of giving up on what matters, and it reminded me to always lean in, showing up, and daring to say what matters to me. It reminded me of being brave and standing tall amidst hardship, and about never losing sight of what’s important in life. I walked away with a reminder to live more, which brings me back to birthdays, a day I rarely if ever celebrate, feeling a bit silly about it all, and that it didn’t matter. Well, this is a new year, and if there ever was a time for change, it is now. So, a birthday week it is, with daily sprinkles of joy to celebrate another year around the sun, and that at the end of the day it can only rain for so long, before the sun finally comes out again;)

The daffodils, the crocuses, the dandelions, primroses and daisies, are all blossoming around my little cottage. It feels a bit early but is a welcoming sight. I put the kettle on last night to fill my granny style hot water bottle with. The cool air sent a draughty chill sweeping across the 350 year old flagstone floor but the view of the sunny coloured daffodils in our cottage garden warmed, if only visually. Our garden has a long way to go, but let’s just say it’s filled with potential, scattered with a few flowers planted by the previous owner that tells me there’s hope for even the smallest of plots. I wrapped my feet around the hot water bottle while editing images for the recent client shoot in Norway. It was a day of ticking off items on the to-do list, but by early afternoon I had skimmed the top of the list, and called it a day, Mr Whiskey agreed. We strolled down high street in our little countryside village, past the weekly food market and towards the green rolling hills in the distance. I inhaled the emerging Spring freshness with flared nostrils. It’s a season of change, and I could feel it in the air. If you want to join me this Spring I have one spot left for the fully immersive Photography workshop in Florence at the end of March and a couple spots left for my food photography workshop here in the English countryside in May. DM me for more information. Wishing you all a wonderful weekend. xx

It’s all slowly returning, the green, blossoms, eager birds chirping away and longer milder days. For now, it’s the rain, but in a way it’s welcomed. It’s will create the foundation for what’s to come, and there’s so much to come, so much to look forward to and so much to celebrate. The landscape around where we live may be a bit bleak  at the moment, but soon, oh so soon, the many colours of English countryside will return. Travels for work took be back to Norway these last couple of weeks. It’s was beautiful and in between shoots for clients in was a warming amount of time with family. It was needed and so welcomed. But then the last day of our trip came, and I yearned to return to my little cottage in the country. The daffodils were out as we drove home and a few trees were dressed in an eager coat of spring blossoms. We may have fallen asleep utterly exhausted after a day of connecting flights, lost luggage and passport issues, but when we opened the bedroom window to let the warm midnight air in, we feel asleep with a smile on our face…we were home, and nothing could dampen that feeling of peace and joy. #myenglishcountryside #england #home

And then there is this woman, my mother. Today is Mother’s Day in Norway, a date I only remember because my sister reminds me, but I somehow always remember the date for it here in England. But no matter the date, this woman needs to be celebrated. She’s simply my heart, my beating heart, and hearing her say it will all be well, is all the assurance I need to keep going when times are hard. She so incredibly warm you simply cannot sit next to her without feeling uplifted. Her wisdom has carried me through everything life has to offer, and now to see my daughter lean on her for comfort, for love, for consistency in friendship, and for stability, when her young life is facing more challenges her age should need to carry on her shoulders, is so beautiful to watch. My mother brings joy and laughter that is infectious, and she has this beautiful way of laughing at herself which brightens any room she enters. I know I’m lucky, but I also know it’s hard work, because every time I tell her about people who comment on how lucky I am to have her, she smiles and simply tells me it’s a choice she makes every morning when she gets up, to be the best she can be, and it’s work, it’s a consistent choice. I try to mirror her ability to love during hardship and to never give up. And when I fall asleep at night next to my wonderful little girl, I count myself lucky to have them both in my life, and do my best in becoming for my daughter, what my mother is to me, a rock of love to lean on and to unwaveringly be encouraged to reach any goal and dream I may have. It’s that kind of day where the clouds hang low on the horizon and the chance of sun is less likely than finding a pair of socks after they have entered the washing machine. The sky is a giant light box, and if I was in my studio today it would’ve given me that soft milky light that I so often yearn for when creating my stillifes. There’s something about a bit of gentle light descending on a little set up of flowers or a handful of fruit from the local market. I remember this day well, getting up early and walking through a sleepy southern town in Italy to the food market. I filled my basket and returned back to where we were staying eager to begin creating. All I needed was a sliver of light descending over the scene like the caress of a feather, and so I cracked the big old oak door to a room without any windows, and let my stillife be illuminated by that slight ray of warm Italian light. There’s magic in every type of light, it’s all about using it to your advantage and learn to see what it can help create for you. Harsh contrasty midday sunshine holds just as much magic in it as a sliver of soft lighting on a cloudy day. It’s all about working with what you’ve got and all my stillifes are created in very different light situations and locations, from caves in the south of Italy, to wonky old sheds with no window in the English countryside, to my sitting room bookshelves and on top of the nightstand in my cottage bedroom. A stormy day can offer up such wild and beautiful light, but so can a summers day at noon when the sun is in zenith. On my recent photography workshop in Florence we began the first day with the pursuit of light, learning to discover and recognise the power of natural light throughout the city, from artists studios, to alleyways, big old palazzo door openings and the incredible light reflecting off of the river Arno on a sunny day and big marble sculptures and surfaces. Light is truly where it all begins and ends for me in photography, and the more you hone your eye, the more you begin to see opportunities around every bend, like spotting your favourite colour everywhere. A hippo in a typical threat display towards a rival in Phinda, South Africa. Hippos are known to be a bit grumpy, but if you read their behavior and play your cards right it always works really well. Hippos move with great ease in water, ”swimming” by kicking their hind feet or simply walking on the bottom. They are well-adapted to an aquatic lifestyle, with small ears, eyes and nostrils set at the top of the head. Their senses are super keen even when submerged in water. By closing its ears and nostrils, the adult can stay under water for as long as six minutes. It’s no secret that hippos love water, which is why the Greeks named them the ”river horse.” Hippos can spend more than 16 hours a day submerged in rivers and lakes to keep their massive bodies cool under the hot African sun. The black market’s insatiable demand for ivory has turned poachers’ attention away from well-protected elephants to more vulnerable hippos! 
Don’t buy exotic animal souvenirs!!

I took this photograph of terraced land prepared for palm oil monoculture in Borneo on assignment for @natgeo (Note the bulldozers far down right in the image).
Palmoil has been and continues to be a major driver of deforestation of some of the world’s most biodiverse forests, destroying the habitat of already endangered species like the Orangutan, pygmy elephant, hornbills, king cobras and Sumatran rhino. This forest loss coupled with conversion of carbon rich peat soils are throwing out millions of tonnes of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and contributing to climate change. There also remains some exploitation of workers and child labour. These are serious issues that the whole palm oil sector needs to step up to address because it doesn’t have to be this way. 
Please avoid uncertified palmoil and support rainforest conservation and ethnic minorities globally!  #borneo #biodiversity #science #logging #fridaysforfuture #palmoil #conservation #wwf #rainforest @natgeo  @thephotosociety

Happy Valentine’s Day! ❤️ When resting, lions socialize through a number of behaviours. The most common peaceful tactile gestures are social licking and head rubbing which, for example can be compared with grooming in primates (or human stroking, cuddling, hugging etc). Social licking among lions often occurs in tandem with sometimes drawn out head rubbings. It’s generally mutual and the recipient clearly express pleasure. The head and neck are the most common parts of the body licked, which may have arisen out of utility, as a lion cannot lick these areas individually. Head rubbing – nuzzling one’s forehead, nose and neck against another lion, is a form of greeting and I often see it after an animal has been apart from the pride, or after a fight or confrontation. In general males tend to rub other males, while cubs and females normally rub females. I took this picture in Thanda, South Africa. #protectbiodiversity #thanda #southafrica #nuzzle #africa #lion #science #happyvalentinesday #mattiasklum #savebigcats @mattiasklumcollection @thephotosociety @natgeo  @mattiasklumofficial

The Rhinoceros Hornbill, king of birds in Borneo! I have spent many weeks waiting for this bird, shy like a raven, really looking like some sort of prehistoric dinosaur, to show up near my tree blinds in the Bornean rainforest canopy. This amazing bird also has one of the largest and most impressive casques, a feature they share with hadrosaurids from more than 60 million years ago. It’s hard to tell the sexes apart. Both female and male hornbills have casques, usually the male’s casque is a bit bigger, but it’s hard to know for sure. The best way is to look at their eyes.  The female’s eyes are whitish blue and males have dark red eyes! Trick is to get close enough....Shot for @natgeo in Danum valley, Borneo. #throwback95 #saverherainforest #hornbill #danumvalley #sabah #borneo #mattiasklum #rainforest #protectbiodiversity #wwf #iucnredlist  @thephotosociety @mattiasklumcollection @natgeo

Una relación de pareja no es lo que la mayoría piensa que es. No se despierta uno cada mañana para hacer el desayuno y comer juntos. No son abrazos eternos en la cama y palabras dulces hasta que los dos se duerman. No es una casa limpia llena de risas y amor todos los días. No es perfección.
Una relación de pareja es alguien que te roba la manta en mitad de la noche. Es a veces mal genio y palabras duras. Es estar de pronto y obstinadamente en desacuerdo, aceptar los momentos silenciosos hasta que los corazones se curen y perdonen. Es llegar a casa y encontrar a la misma persona todos los días, es monotonía. Es ropa sucia y camas sin hacer. Es orgullo cuando se trata de razones.
Es tragarse las molestas palabras en lugar de decirlas en voz alta para no lastimar al otro.
Pero en esas amargas experiencias se encuentran los más bellos regalos. Una relación de pareja es tener en tu vida a alguien que se preocupa por ti a pesar de qué y quién eres, a pesar de tus errores e imperfecciones.
Es alguien que ayuda en este duro trabajo de la vida. Es colaboración mutua, hacerse la cena entre los dos y sentarse juntos, a una hora tardía, porque los dos tuvieron un día loco. Es tener una crisis emocional y que tu pareja se acueste contigo y te sostenga, y te diga que todo va a estar bien. Y tú le creas.
Se trata de seguir amando a alguien a pesar de que a veces te vuelve absolutamente loco.
Amar a alguien no siempre es fácil, a veces es muy difícil. Pero es increíble y reconfortante. Una de las mejores cosas que alguna vez vas a experimentar en la vida. Texto @kokuhga

news flash: last week, just north of cabo near our hotel in baja, a mama sea turtle came ashore to lay a clutch of eggs. she made three nests, spending ~20 minutes in each (the first and last nest are visible in the second video) and used her fins to push sand and bury herself deeper into the sand before laying the eggs, before making her way back to the ocean and vanishing into a wave. according to the man in this video, the eggs should hatch in 1-2 months and the turtles (loggerheads) lay several nests in order to maximize reproductive output + help protect the eggs from predators 🐢

“conflict in congo is like a babushka (matryoshka) doll....you have conflicts sitting inside conflicts....it’s about local issues, who controls land, which chief is in power....often linked to ethnicity, because at local level ethnicity is the principle organizer of politics....at the next level, it is national power, partially due to collapse of mobutu and effects of belgian colonialism....but there it is more about using ethnicity to leverage a better position in parliament or a piece of a smuggling racket in gold....then you have the regional power politics, which mainly involves rwanda and that role really began in 1994 with the rwandan genocide....the conflict initially was not about minerals, though they became important over time to fund war efforts, esp for a country like rwanda that is small and poor....but when tantalum shot through the roof, which happened to be at a time of extreme violence, it began to shift incentives of those involved in the conflict and it was no longer about national security....around 2000 the various actors became more invested in minerals....but the war here is really about power and access to power, and that passes through local politicians. so you need to understand the politics” - jason stearns

*note: the above may serve to help understand the “conflict in congo,” the atmosphere inside the country, and is not meant to address the past/current influence of foreign powers “outside”

Квартира - это метафора на слово память, а привычка постоянно фотографировать - это попытка обставить эту квартиру. Я решила больше и чаще фотографироваться, не оставлять впечатления только себе. Cuando la crisis climática nos está rodeando, hoy nos escapamos a los paisajes de frío, verde, lluvia, agua, humedad. Con ella. Se llama Elena Ortega, nació en Castellón hace 49 años y tiene un gusto innegable no solo para la fotografía, también para ver la belleza donde otros solo ven frío. Ni el cambio climático, ni temperaturas más propias del verano en el mes de abril, ni el aumento de las noches tropicales anuales en España ni la sequía cada vez más profunda son capaces de cambiarnos el chip. Tenemos que aprender que el buen tiempo, a principio de los 20 del siglo XXI, se compone de nubes, de sombra, de brisa y, por supuesto, de lluvia. Tal vez por eso ella, Elena, fue una visionaria y decidió adoptar en ocasiones el pseudónimo de @misswinter (señora invierno), como carta de presentación de su preciosa forma de mirar.
