Wildebeest may not be the most conventionally handsome antelope, but catch them in the right light – their beards glowing red in the afternoon sun – and they take on a certain distinctive quality. These somewhat ungainly animals are hardy survivors. They face an onslaught of threats during their annual migration across the predator-rich plains of the Serengeti and, for many, its sheer resilience and mettle that see them through the journey.

#wildebeest #wildlife #nature

I've always been in awe of the sheer power and presence of elephants. While spending time with these giants you learn to appreciate the delicate application of that immense strength. A carefully directed blast of water from a trunk provides relief from the scorching African sun, while pillar-like legs are used to dig into the sand when rivers run dry. Their movements are purposeful and intricate fuelled by an intelligence and social cohesion that we are yet to fully understand. Although, we don't speak their language and can only deduce the motivations for their behaviour, we can respect and admire their sentience. And do everything we can to protect them.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#elephant #nature #wildlife

Trees are more than just resting spots for leopards; they provide cover from danger and a safe place to stash a kill where it's beyond the reach of eager scavengers. This cat hastily hauled her warthog kill into the safety of the boughs, but kept a lookout for any rivals on the horizon. Competition for food is tough in the African bush, and wily predators like leopards are only too aware of the looming threat of losing a meal.⁣
⁣
#bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram #leopards

A lion's roar commands attention. Specially adapted vocal folds allow these cats to muster up a reverberating bellow that can be heard from kilometres away. If you're close enough, you'll feel the vibrations of the call rolling through your bones and likely triggering the hairs on the back of your neck to stand up straight. It's a sound we've come to love and appreciate during our time documenting these apex predators. Sadly, we have also witnessed this iconic sound fading from more and more corners of the African wild. We stand to lose so much more than just a roar if we allow these cats to vanish.⁣
⁣
#lions #bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram #bigcatconservation #wildlife #wildlifelovers #conservation #nature

There's a special elegance and grace reserved for giraffes. That silhouette, unmistakable against a golden sky, floats with purpose and poise across the savannah. Their unique form has awed visitors to Africa for centuries, but like so many other species, giraffes are in trouble. Populations have plummeted by 40% in just the last 30 years, and there are now fewer than 70,000 mature individuals left in the wild. We know what must be done to save them: prioritise conservation efforts, safeguard habitats, address threats like illegal hunting. If we don't act now, we stand to lose these iconic creatures forever.⁣
⁣
#giraffes #giraffeconservation #wildlifeconservation

Intensely focused, this cheetah gives a piercing gaze across the plains of Kenya’s Masai Mara. Among Africa’s iconic big cats, cheetahs stand out as perhaps the most stark example of threats converging to imperil a species—from shallow gene pools to habitat loss to the illegal trade. New and emerging issues, including some related to climate change, are adding to the pressure—and often unfolding in unexpected ways. Recent research, for example, shows that rising temperatures are pushing cheetahs to shift their hunting habits to the cooler night hours, a behavior that not only complicates their survival strategies but also intensifies competition with other carnivores. In the face of these complex challenges, it is crucial for us to recognize the urgency of conservation efforts for both cheetahs and precious ecosystems like the Masai Mara.

Spotting a pangolin in the wild is rare. In all our years documenting wildlife, often spending weeks embedded in the bush, we've only seen a handful of these elusive mammals in the wild. They're often more active at night, shuffling through the undergrowth in search of termites, ants and larvae, which they dig out of nests and burrows using their impressive claws. Once they've carved an opening in the dirt, a long sticky tongue goes to work sucking up insects en masse. ⁣
⁣
They are profoundly unique animals. But they are also under threat. All eight species of pangolins found throughout the world are threatened by the illegal wildlife trade and populations are rapidly declining. Despite their shy nature, they remain one of the most trafficked mammals in the world and are illegally trapped in their thousands to feed a growing demand for their scales and meat. Without strict regulations and enforcement, these remarkable animals may be pushed to extinction. This #WorldPangolinDay, let's join forces and pledge to never let that happen.⁣
⁣⁣
#pangolin #PangolinsDay #wildlife #nature #wildlifeconservation

⁣

It's astonishing to witness the speed and agility of hippos. Although they spend the majority of the daylight hours basking, semi-submerged, in rivers or ponds, hippos venture out of the water at night or when the weather is cooler to feed on grass. Those dainty ankles are carrying around a ton and a half of territorial hippo and, despite his size, he can turn on a dime. Deeply scarred from territorial disputes – the wounds of which were likely made more severe by opportunistic oxpecker birds that feast on blood and parasites – this male clearly means business. Hippos are famously possessive over their pools and will aggressively defend them, sometimes even charging at innocuous animals like impalas. A herd of buffalo ventured a bit too close, and the enraged hippo voiced his displeasure at their presence. Although buffaloes can definitely hold their own against an aggressive hippo, this herd thought  better of taking on the challenge and instead watched the angry behemoth from a distance.⁣⁣
⁣⁣

Product development is long and often frustrating. When you watch my videos, you see the sketch then you see the final result in a matter of 60 seconds but the truth is often my designs take anywhere between a year to sometimes 3 years to go from concept to real thing. 

Why?

It all begins with finding the right fabric for what I’m trying to achieve. If I’m lucky, I may already have a fabric I love that I’ve used before that I wanna use again! But often the fabric sourcing bit itself can take months.

The sampling process can take anywhere from a few months minimum to almost a year, sometimes more! During this time, fabric can change, design may change, the perfect fit will always be obsessed over, and I’ll sample over and over and over again until it feels just right. I’ll won’t stop until it feels ready, and I’m happy.

Then there’s the actual production which includes the weaving of the fabric, the dying of the fabric, the cutting of the pattern pieces, the careful sewing of the garment etc etc…

Good things just take time. 

They seem to always do, don’t they?

Two photos of Common Terns bringing back fish for their chicks that tell a story of climate change in the Gulf of Maine –
 
As seawater temperatures increase, native fish species that sustain seabirds become scarce, forcing parents to bring their chicks fish that they cannot swallow.
 
In the first image the parent returns to its nest with a Sand Lance – a slender-bodied silver fish that the chicks can easily swallow.
 
The second photo shows a tern parent with a Butterfish in its mouth, a meal the baby birds cannot eat.
 
The result is an increase in chick mortality rates.

A harp seal pup, about 16 days old swims among the ice in Canada’s Gulf of St. Lawrence.
 
At about age 14 days, these pups shed their white coats and begin learning to swim. At this stage they are called “beaters” a name derived from the way they beat the water with their flippers.
 
The loss of sea ice due to climate change is negatively impacting these animals.

A school of Alewife fish swim into a waterfall during their annual spawning migration in a river in Maine.
 
Alewife are an anadromous species of herring that spend most of their lives in the ocean, but migrate through freshwater rivers to lakes where they spawn each spring.
 
Their stocks had been severely depleted, but have improved in the Gulf of Maine due to the removal of dams in coastal rivers.

As a traveler it can be hard to tell whether or not an attraction or activity is harmful to any animals, or we may be too caught up in the excitement of the experience to recognize the reality of what indeed is happening. 

Here are a few things you can ask yourself to avoid cruel attractions: 
1) Are the wild animals kept in cages that do not have all of the following: food, clean water, shelter, ample space, privacy and enrichment?
2) Are animals forced to perform tricks in shows?
3) Are you able to ride, touch, hold, walk or swim with wild animals? 
4) Does the tourist attraction sell parts of products from wild animals? 
5) Does the tour company chase or lure wild animals closer with food or bring people too close to wild animals so they can see them better?

 If you answered yes to any of these, it is not an animal-friendly attraction. Also if the attraction claims to have rescued the wild animals under their care, you can use @worldanimalprotectioncanada’s checklist, to determine if it is a genuine sanctuary.

A couple of points pulled from the checklist are:
1) Does not take animals from the wild (unless they are injured) or breed animals 
2) Does not keep wild animals to make a profit
3) Keeps animals in enclosures that closely resemble their natural habitat and give them enough space and opportunities to move and behave naturally
4) Have veterinarians available at any hour to treat the animals that become sick or hurt. 

 I have linked the checklist in my bio, along with in my stories if you’re wanting to read more. 

You can join the movement by following @worldanimalprotectioncanada, and by sharing this message, which will help us keep wildlife in the wild and end cruel wildlife entertainment’ ✨

Para praticantes de musculação: 

Durante a musculação , exercícios com carga , há o aumento da pressão intra abdominal na cavidade abdominal. A médio e longo prazo se não fizer a correta ativação dos músculos profundos do abdômen durante a execução dos exercícios (que também são estabilizadores) , respiração incorreta ou possuir fraqueza nesses músculos, poderá ocorrer a dilatação abdominal , podendo perder a linha de cintura, também pode causar hérnias umbilicais , lesões , dores na coluna lombar. Portanto essa combinação de exercícios é indicada. 

Para atletas: 

Tem se observado nos últimos anos uma valorização da linha de cintura e do vácuo abdominal durante as competições de bodybuilding. A prática dessa combinação de exercícios irá promover melhoria da estética da linha de cintura, redução de medidas, facilitar o vácuo durante a apresentação, melhorar o padrão respiratório, melhorar a postura. Reduzir a dilatação abdominal em decorrência das altas cargas durante os treinamentos, evitar as hérnias umbilicais que são comuns pelos motivos citados acima.

Para as mamães: O enfraquecimento dos músculos internos do abdômen e a diástase é a principal causa de dilatação abdominal, flacidez e dor nas costas pós parto e pode causar possíveis lesões no treino, hérnias umbilicais, alterações posturais, constipação, dor na relação, dentre outros. Independente se ainda há diástase ou não é necessário fortalecer as estruturas enfraquecidas.

Meus top 3 exercícios para afinar a cintura: 

Transverso abdominal é o músculo profundo do nosso abdômen e envolve toda a nossa cintura. 

Com a combinação de duas técnicas: ativação de transverso e hipopressivos (vácuo) é possível reduzir medidas de cintura, melhorar a estética do abdômen e linha de cintura, além de muitos benefícios para saúde. 

Os hipopressivos ativam e fortalecem o transverso através do vácuo abdominal (sucção) com a costela aberta e da diminuição de pressão na região. 

Ja a ativação de transverso, a respiração de ativação profunda, fortalece toda a região e evita aumento da pressão interna para frente do abdômen. 

Como qualquer treinamento requer constância, regularidade. Há uma grande variedade de posições e posturas, o praticamente deve ir avançando de acordo com seu nível de aptidão.

Don’t shove your cat in their pet carrier right before their vet appointment / traveling causing Meowing and anxiety.
Start acclimating them to their pet carrier now by…
Step 1 Pet carrier near feeding area. Bowl of food placed a few feet from carrier. 
Step 2 Every 2 to 4 days (or at your cats comfortable pace), move food bowl a tadbit closer to carrier.
Step 3 eventually place bowl right inside carrier 
Step 4 Bowl inching its way (every 2-4 days) towards the back of the carrier. 
Step 5 once your cat is comfortably eating the food in the back of the carrier, move the door to see how your cat responds, little by little to desensitise them from the strange and scary sound the door can make closing. Do this a little bit each meal eventually closing and opening the door. 
once you can close it open it and your cat is still eating and comfortable, once closed gently pickup carrier and set back down opening up the carrier. Repeat a few times each meal before carrying it to another room. 
Tips: Use higher value food to speed up the acclamation process. 
Don’t move to the next step until your cat is comfortable. You can also incorporate toy games in and around the carrier for a positive experience. 
You want to use the same incremental desensitisation  process to acclimate them to your vehicle.

People compare Paragliding to chess in the sky.  I think this analogy is faulty. I once heard, “Paragliding is like playing chess with dice that are a round.”  Closer to the truth?  I think chasing XC records is a little bit like fishing.  You cast your line and hope you catch a big one.  Really, Paragliding is closer to poker than chess... a game of skill and chance.   

This winter in Roldanillo I played my cards and launched my line into some absolutely epic weather. I arrived with the pie in the sky goal of breaking the FAI record for what is probably the most popular winter paragliding destination in the world.  Success was unlikely, but I’ve been working on my delusional self-belief. 

 On the 25th of January I realized an unlikely dream and put myself and the USA flag at the top of the Roldanillo x-contest score! I pushed, I believed, and I closed a 219 Km magical mystery tour of the Valle de Cauca.  Elated and exhausted, I rested.  My glory was short-lived. The next day Bogdan Bialka took his record back pushing it to 230!  And… the next day Kevin Phillip took to the sky with a vengeance setting a new record of 236 km…legend.  The Roldanillo FAI record was beaten 3 days in a row!  I spent the next two weeks in an absurd version of paragliding Groundhog Day trying to reclaim the record.  On three separate occasions, the dream was within grasp but shut down by the unpredictable Pacifico winds and a pace that just wasn’t fast enough. It’s fair to say that this was a historic season for Paragliding in Roldanillo.  

Of the top 50 scored flights on x-contest, 46 of them were from this year!  It’s more the journey than the destination, and I’m grateful for the motivation that being a record chasing psychopath gave me.  Epic scenery, wild low saves, thousands of kms, and almost 200 hours of full-bar obsession on my Enzo and Sub. While the Rolda. FAI record is more elusive than ever, I’m grateful that I got to be king for a day, and learned a ton about paragliding and the power of delusional self-belief....  which is why I’ll be taking the record back next year.

In Emilio’s words: “This summer i got lucky enough to be one of the recipients of Cedar Wright’s dirtbag fund! this was the only time being a dirt bag paid in money as well as experiences. For a while now  I’ve been going into the backcountry every summer—mountaineering, climbing, and eating homemade dehydrated eggs for weeks (sometimes months) at a time. Outside of that I’ve been maximizing a dirtbag life by living in an RV in rural North Carolina, splitting my time between grad school and climbing, honing my trad skills and getting repeated tastes of humble pie at Moores Wall and Stone Mountain. This spring I used up the last of my cash to buy plane tickets to fly out to Washington and was ready to be completely broke until the dirtbag fund came to my rescue! Crisis averted: Thank you Cedar!! As soon as I arrived in Washington, my climbing partner Mo and I hit the road towards the Olympics, where we repeated Wayne Wallace’s “Sawtooth Ridge.” Sawtooth was one of the best climbs I’ve had the privilege of doing, with some cerebral and delicious leads. Talvez a ficha nunca caia, mas fazer parte de mais essa tour com meus irmãos do @nxzerooficial foi sem dúvida a melhor coisa que decidi fazer esse ano. 

São muitos anos, muitos mesmo… algumas pessoas até nem saibam que antes de ser fotógrafo, cheguei a dividir palco com o NX com a minha banda também - se não me engano isso rolou em 2003 em Caçapava/SP, na extinta Posso! Skate Bar. 

Corta pra 2005 e nos reencontramos, eu já como fotógrafo e morando em Curitiba. Depois de vários shows fazendo foto deles por lá, chegou a hora de voltar pra SP e aceitar o convite pra acompanhar a banda em definitivo… não hesitei em dizer sim, afinal de contas, eu já acreditava no potencial deles antes mesmo de assinarem com gravadora.

Deu certo, deu muito certo. Foram anos de estrada, convivência, aprendizados e muita troca. Eu sou quem sou hoje por causa do NXZERO, e sei que lá no fundo alguma coisa disso é recíproca também, afinal, durante muitos anos tudo o que as pessoas viam e tinham acesso era através do meu olhar, do que eu queria mostrar e como eu enxergava aquilo tudo.

Já essa tour foi algo que nunca imaginei que viveria. Essa experiência de lotar duas vezes um estádio é pra poucos… e eu já não tava ali como fotógrafo, eu tava ali como um espectador com privilégios. Eu não sei até agora o que rolou, mas talvez essa última cena do carrossel diga mais que tudo. Foi mais forte que eu.
Obrigado por confiarem no meu trabalho e acreditarem nas maluquices que propus… obrigado também a toda equipe que sempre entregou o melhor que podiam - vcs não fazem ideia do que eles fazem pra tudo acontecer.

NXZERO é uma energia onde todos nós fazemos parte. A troca é necessária e só assim que tudo flui.

Muito obrigado, parabéns a todos e até breve 🥹❤️

Como já disse em outros posts, a minha história com o NX começou muitos anos atrás, mas essas fotos aí foram da nossa última sessão feita, que por coincidência ou não, foram em Curitiba - onde também já havíamos feito a sessão de fotos para o disco “Agora” (que esses dias fez aniversário de 15 anos de lançado). Curitiba tem um peso importantíssimo pra mim e acredito muito que pra eles também. 

Mas vou contar aqui uma curiosidade: em todos esses anos que estive com eles, apenas UMA sessão fotográfica em estúdio foi feita, marcada e planejada. Todas as outras vezes, sempre improvisando onde quer que fosse, na hora que dava e com o que a gente tinha… e talvez essa seja a “nossa” marca haha.

Essa sessão não deixou de ser também um pouco improvisada e com o tempo disponível que a gente tinha, mas pelo menos o lugar eu consegui escolher… e o desafio era: todas as fotos apenas com luz natural.

Pedi que levassem dois figurinos, um na atual paleta que definimos no início da tour e o outro com o clássico todo preto, e assim foi. Tínhamos duas horas pra fazer tudo isso aí acontecer.

Fiz as fotos tanto com equipamento digital quanto com analógico (pra guardar algo físico, palpável). Essas todas aí são as digitais, as analógicas eu mostro em breve em algum momento (to esperando os negativos voltarem pra casa - eles ainda estão em Curitiba).

Coincidentemente calhou do momento ser o de lançamento da música nova, então aproveitamos para usá-las nessa virada… e provavelmente essas fotos serão utilizadas em alguns outros materiais que estarão por vir.

No geral a sessão foi bem tranquila, todos se divertindo, tudo fluiu sem problema e acho que a vibe que ficou diz muita coisa disso, não?

Obrigado a todos os envolvidos que ajudaram isso acontecer…

E aí, o que você achou? Qual curtiu mais? E se eu disser que tem mais, quer ver também? 🤣🤔

Tutto quello che volevo dirti te l’ho detto all’orecchio in questi giorni, ma tanto tu già sapevi tutto.
In questi tredici anni insieme sei stata la mia bambina ed allo stesso tempo la mia amica pronta a farmi sempre compagnia e a farmi sentire amata quando più ne avevo bisogno. Mi bastava abbracciarti e sentire il tuo profumo per sentirmi a casa perchè è proprio quello che sei stata sempre: la mia famiglia. E hai fatto anche di più, hai “creato” quella che è la nostra famiglia: eri tu “il cane di Chiara Ferragni” di quella canzone che mi ha fatto conoscere il papà nel 2016. Ci pensi se non fossi stata la mia Matildona come poteva essere diversa la mia vita? 
Quando ti ho scelta, ancora ragazzina, mai avrei pensato che avresti conosciuto i miei bambini, ed invece sei stata stupenda anche nel ruolo di “sorella maggiore”: hai regalato loro l’esperienza di amore incondizionato verso un animale che diventa famiglia. 
Ieri, dopo averti salutata per l’ultima volta ho provato a spiegare a Leo che eri andata in cielo e ci avresti sempre protetti da una nuvoletta lassù. E lui mi ha chiesto come potevamo riconoscere la nuvola perchè cosi potevamo salutarti sempre anche noi. 
Spero di averti fatto vivere una bella vita e di averti fatto sentire il mio amore ogni giorno, perchè io il tuo l’ho sentio sempre. Mi mancherà tutto di te Mati, ti saluterò ogni giorno su quella nuvoletta. 
Sarai per sempre la mia prima bimba 💖

Il vestito senza vergogna:

Riportare l’attenzione sui diritti delle donne, del loro corpo e su come il disporre del corpo femminile dalle stesse sia, purtroppo, ancora considerato discusso e discutibile. Questo è l’obiettivo dietro questo look. L’idea di un abito che simulasse il corpo nudo di Chiara ci è arrivata immediatamente prendendo ispirazione da una creazione di @mariagraziachiuri per @dior della primavera/estate 2018. Realizzato negli atelier alta moda @dior il vestito in tulle color carne riproduce con un ricamo trompe l'oeil il corpo di @chiaraferragni al naturale e liberato da quella vergogna che hanno sempre imposto a tutte, a partire da Eva, la prima donna della storia indotta a provare vergogna. 

Questa illusione di nudità vuole ricordare a tutte il diritto e l’uguaglianza di genere che hanno nel mostrare, disporre di se stesse senza doversi sentire giudicate o colpevoli. Questa illusione di nudità vuole ricordare che chiunque decida di mostrarsi, o sentirsi sexy non autorizza nessuno a giustificare le violenze degli uomini o ad attenuarne le colpe.

Questo è il corpo di una donna, quello di @chiaraferragni che vorrebbe dare voce a tutte le donne del mondo a cui vengono imposti divieti e abusi, a tutte coloro a cui viene detto che il loro corpo genera vergogna, che è solo un oggetto del desiderio o che istiga al peccato. 

Questo è il corpo di tutte. Chi è senza peccato scagli la prima pietra!

• SUNDAY MOOD 💙 Dernier jour rien que tous les 3 avant de commencer l’adaptation crèche demain.

Je ne vous cache pas que j’ai un petit pincement au cœur de laisser mon #BébéPenderie ! Mais c’est le fruit d’une longue réflexion… 

Quand on a eu la place en crèche en janvier dernier, on avait demandé pour 4 jours par semaine à partir de début septembre. Et quand bébé est né, j’ai commencé à vraiment me questionner sur ce choix jusqu’à en pleurer avant d’aller me coucher tellement il était mignon en disant à Adrien « j’veeeeux pas l’mettre à la crècheee » 🥺

Et puis y a d’autres moments où tu te retrouves à 14h en pyjama en train d’allaiter dans tes toilettes 🚽 en ayant tenté 3 fois de te faire un thé mais qui finissait toujours froid. Et là tu te dis, que peut-être oui, la crèche ça sera bien pour toute la famille.

Autant on arrive à faire plein de choses avec lui (cuisiner, randonner…) même côté boulot en le portant pendant nos projets photos par exemple mais par contre je déteste travailler devant mes écrans 💻📱 quand mon bébé est là. Alors on a décidé de revenir sur notre contrat en passant de 4 à 3 jours par semaine et en repoussant l’adaptation à fin septembre.

Demain, c’est donc notre pré-rentrée pour toute la famille Penderie ! Et je le sens super bien, vraiment ! Je me sens si chanceuse d’avoir pu garder mon bébé près de moi 7/7 et 24/24 jusqu’à ses presque 5 mois. Et je sais que c’est le bon moment pour nous tous de trouver un rythme de croisière 🚢 sur tous les niveaux. Vraiment hâte de voir comment notre baby va se débrouiller comme un chef et trop happy aussi de reprendre un peu de temps pour moi et pour de super projets à venir ! 💫

• BIEN NETTOYER SA GOURDE 💦 C’est vraiment un super allié durable, écologique et zéro déchet mais aussi un véritable NID À BACTÉRIES 🙀🦠 alors mieux vaut les bichonner !

1️⃣ Ne pas passer les gourdes en inox au lave vaisselle (ni au micro-ondes et ni au congélateur).
2️⃣ Nettoyer en profondeur avec du vinaigre blanc (1/3 du volume de la gourde + eau chaude) et/ou du bicarbonate de soude (2 cuillères + eau chaude) puis fermer, secouer, laisser agir 10min minimum sans le bouchon avant de rincer abondamment à l’eau chaude.
3️⃣ Utiliser simplement du liquide vaisselle + de l’eau chaude pour un nettoyage quotidien. 
4️⃣ Laver l’intérieur sans oublier l’extérieur et le bouchon à part dans un bain d’eau chaude + vinaigre blanc et/ou bicarbonate de soude. Si le bouchon de votre gourde comporte un joint, le retirer délicatement et le laver à part également. 
5️⃣ Faire sécher la gourde à l’air libre, tête en bas sans la refermer, idéalement sur un porte biberon si vous en avez un.
6️⃣ Stocker votre gourde ouverte sans le bouchon pour éviter la condensation et les mauvaises odeurs si vous ne l’utilisez pas.

🥤 Personnellement, je ne mets que de l’eau dans mes gourdes mais si vous avez l’habitude de boire d’autres types de boissons (sodas, thé, café ou mojito… 🌿😂) il est bien sûr important de procéder à un nettoyage en profondeur à chaque utilisation.

• LA SÉRÉNITÉ 😌 C’est ce que je m’offre de plus precieux pendant ma grossesse et pour le jour de la naissance, avec l’aide de mon mari (un rôle clé du co-parent). C’est pouvoir fermer les yeux tranquillement et se concentrer sur ce qui a de l’importance à l’instant T. C’est avoir un pilier de confiance pendant que tu accomplis ton incroyable pouvoir de créer, nourrir et donner naissance à un petit bébé…

SÉRÉNITÉ & 1ERE GROSSESSE 🤰 c’était un long fleuve tranquille. Je pouvais vraiment être maîtresse de mes sensations et ne penser qu’à mon bien-être. Lorsque la fatique prenait le dessus, Adrien était toujours là pour assurer.

SÉRÉNITÉ & 2NDE GROSSESSE 🤰 c’est un peu plus challengeant avec notre bambin en pleine phase d’affirmation (le 2-3 ans, le « non », la négociation, les colères…). En tant que maman, le bien-être de son enfant passe avant tout. Je me découvre de la ressource dans des situations pénibles où je n’ai qu’une envie c’est de m’allonger sur le canapé dans le calme... Encore une fois, Adrien est là pour prendre le relai.

SÉRÉNITÉ À L’ACCOUCHEMENT 👶 c’était un état d’esprit pour ma première grossesse, c’est une évidence aujourd’hui. Je ne suis pas quelqu’un de stressée mais d’organisée. J’adore imaginer mon projet de naissance naturel idéal, faire la valise pour la maternité pour toute la famille, me préparer à donner naissance dans différentes circonstances…

Je sais (après une première naissance sans péridurale en position accroupie), que toutes les ressources sont en moi. 💪 Je sais que mon mari sera mon pilier comme toujours pour me soutenir mentalement et physiquement. Je sais que je peux faire confiance en mon bébé mais également à l’équipe médicale pour former ensemble une dream team 🌟 le jour J.

Je sais aussi que la magie 🪄 de cette aventure c’est l’INCONNU ! Je le sais, tout peut arriver mais qu’importe le chemin tant que nous sommes tous réunis au final.

BREF, JE SUIS SEREINE. Que l’avenir écrive la suite de sa plus belle plume 🪶🥰 D’ici là, c’est repos pour la guerrière !

• ALLAITER ENCEINTE 🤱🤰 mon expérience ⤵️

👉 1ER TRIMESTRE : mon fils est passé naturellement de 4/5 TT / 24h à 2/3 TT. Les TT se sont également énormément réduites en durée passant de 10/15min à 2/5min. Le sommeil 💤 s’est aussi grandement amélioré puisqu’il a commencé à faire des nuits complètes cet été. Un combo entre son arrêt des protéines de lait de vache quelques mois plus tôt soignants ses maux mais peut être aussi le ressenti que ses parents avaient besoin d’un peu de repos avant de replonger dans les nuits hachées (ou pas sait-on jamais haha) ?

Comme mon fils est un petit gabarit, on surveille sa prise de poids grossomodo 1 fois tous les 2 mois. Nous nous sommes aperçu qu’il avait perdu 300g. J’ai compris à ce moment là que ma lactation avait énormément baissé. 📉  Moins de bon lait maternel = il faut mettre l’accent sur des sources de calcium et de bons gras différents. Quelques ajustements plus tard et il avait repris son poids plume 🪶 (merci Julie de @hamstouille_bambin de nous avoir conseillé).

Mes seins devenus très sensibles, j’ai énormément communiqué mon ressenti à mon fils pour qu’il adapte ses tétées sans me gêner. Une des joies d’allaiter un bambin c’est qu’il comprend absolument TOUT.

👉 2EME TRIMESTRE : les TT se maintiennent voir ralentissent, je me dis même qu’il pourrait se sevrer naturellement s’il en ressentait le besoin. Depuis ses 2 ans environ, je ne lui propose plus le sein, c’est à son initiative avec mon consentement bien sûr. Je vis notre allaitement au jour le jour, comme une chance. 🍀 Peut être s’arrêtera-t-il naturellement pendant ma grossesse ? Peut être irons-nous vers un co-allaitement ? L’avenir nous le dira !

👉 3EME TRIMESTRE : je sais maintenant qu’une aventure de co-allaitement nous attend. 🥹 Je prépare au maximum mon fils en lui expliquant tout « tu sais il y a 2 titis ça tombe bien un pour toi et un pour ta petite sœur qui aura besoin de boire beaucoup de lait car les bébés ne peuvent pas manger comme nous ».

It’s wild to consider the amount of life these mountains have witnessed throughout different chapters in the history of the world... Hannibal leading the Carthaginian army across the alps in 218 BC to the development of alpinism and years of brave people ticking off first ascents with only rudimentary gear and a strong will. Every time I set foot in them.. it invites a way of life that encourages constant awareness without distraction. You have to pay attention to your surroundings but you also feel at peace with that rhythm of life - something I find harder to achieve surrounded by man made structures. These images come from 2016 on a perfect day in the Swiss alps.. gazing down at Lake Ritom with a bit of disbelief at our luck finding a glassy lake with a backdrop more like a painting than reality…

A couple of weeks ago, I shared a collection of some commercial work that I’ve done over the years and I thought I’d share another round of some old favorites. It’s so common on Instagram to only see highlights or just the final product and I think it’s really important to show a larger scope of what it takes to be successful in the creative industry - and commercial work has been a huge part of that for me. My approach was always to combine inspiring, landscapes, and adventure with companies that I worked with - taking what I knew how to do well and finding a way to integrate their product in.. some thing I think aspiring photographers to ask themselves… how does your style and expertise mesh with a brand that way that makes sense?

We always sought out this angle… hoping to get fisheye perspective that usually resulted in you going over the falls. Luckily the sand was soft. I was on a a long overdue trip with my wife in California after weeks of being gone for work and I got this call that this swell was coming to a remote section of the Caribbean… I remember kinda weighing out the decision to stay or go - eventually making the decision to go and left halfway through our once in a blue moon vacation. Life was so volatile…. being on call for these trips meant I had to drop even a special trip with family at times. The trip was a success, I scored a cover on Surfer Magazine but I always thought back to how much the career asked of me

As long as I can remember, holding a camera in my hand, it was a dream to be a staff photographer for Surfer Magazine. My years spent shooting for these publications were truly an honor and profoundly shaped the direction of my career and perspective in storytelling. During my tenure, the epitome of success was getting a cover and I look at those covers as some of the highlight moments of my life… 
This short piece paying tribute to some really iconic and influential magazines was a walk down memory lane for me - making me relive some of those little moments.. it’s super meaningful to be featured here and the book that my friend @grantellis1 put together is pretty special & an incredible way to see the evolution of surfing & photography over the years…

Iceland’s highlands have long been a playground for both locals and newcomers.. offering the ability to connect with an astonishing variety of natural features all within close proximity to each other. You might be crossing glacial rivers, moving past steaming geothermal vents, or traversing colorful ridge lines that look as if painted by nature’s brush. This part of the world always sparks imagination and rejuvenates me every time I return... offering a little more perspective on where my next expedition could be or what creative project might capture it’s beauty for those to see who are unable to make the trip. Last fall I was lucky enough to share some spectacular weather in the highlands on a ride with the @maap.cc ALT-ROAD crew - traversing from hut to hut and scoring some of the best views Iceland has to offer... couldn’t think of a better way to spend a few days with friends.

I’m not a wildlife photographer - I leave that to my good friends @paulnicklen & @mitty who’ve spent many years & countless hours perfecting the craft… but occasionally, if I’m lucky, an animal gets in the way of my camera. 
To me, whales cresting the ocean’s surface remains as one of the more special human experiences. The two orcas shown above swam just off the shores of the Kurils - a chain of islands located between Russia and Japan. Besides the sound of disturbed seagulls and the creaking of our boat, all outside distractions and sense of time seemed to fade away as I witnessed these beautiful creatures breach… fortunately having the presence of mind to haphazardly hold up my camera and try to capture one of the purest wildlife moments I can remember. During this expedition in 2019 with @renan_ozturk & @taylorfreesolo - we shared a piece of what we found in an environmental documentary called “From the Kurils with Love” which you can find on YouTube

#ValentinesDay is meant to be a time to celebrate love. In the 67 countries around the world that criminalize same-sex activity between consenting adults, it is another day in which LGBTQ couples must keep their love hidden. J & Q (names withheld for their safety) are from #Uganda. They told me that in their country “lesbianism is an abnormality… a disease that needs to be cured.” They are married but their union is not recognized by Ugandan law. “We never feel safe,” they say. “Living in Uganda as a lesbian [is] a dangerous thing.” So they pretend to be sisters, moving house regularly to avoid suspicious neighbors. All they want is to “live a more peaceful life, even if it’s a closeted one”.

Their story, like many from my long-term project #WhereLoveIsIllegal, sheds light on the harsh reality of life for #LGBTQ people in societies where they are criminalized for who they are and who they love. You can see more queer stories of survival @whereloveisillegal

BANANA CREAM OVERNIGHT OATS ✨
If you love banana cream pie you must try this recipe! Banana Flavored Milk really adds the perfect amount of sweetness and flavor so you don’t need to add any additional sweetener. To all Hawaii residents — make sure to enter the @EnjoyMelona dessert competition by November 30! Win up to $10,000! Further details at: Melonaicecream.com/alohamelona

Purchase Banana Milk Here: https://www.amazon.com/Binggrae-Banana-Flavor-Milk-Pack/dp/B00PJCBM74?th=1

Ingredients:
(3 servings fit in one 16 oz wide mouth mason jar) 
300 ML @enjoymelona Banana Flavored Milk (1.5 cartons)
3/4 c rolled oats
1.5 tbsp chia seeds
1.5 tbsp cashew butter 
Vanilla yogurt
Fresh banana slices
Graham cracker crumbs

Directions:
Mix all in ingredients together and cover and store in fridge for at least 2 hours, overnight is ideal. 
When ready to eat layer with vanilla yogurt, fresh banana slices and Graham cracker crumbs. 
(To save time you can also mix the yogurt in with the oats and chia seeds before storing in the fridge)

My journey through Tokyo… ✨🇯🇵 

Each moment becoming an unforgettable experience: 
1. Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel: A luxurious stay in Shibuya offering mesmerising cityscape views, transforming into a captivating tapestry of lights at night. 
2. Mount Mitake Mystical Forest: Just a short trip from Tokyo, Mount Mitake enchanted with mist-shrouded ancient cedars and the soothing sounds of nature. 
3. Mitake Sanso Shukubo Retreat: The traditional temple lodge provided an authentic escape, immersing in cultural heritage. 
4. KabukichoTheater: Stepping into Shinjuku’s Kabukicho Theater was a journey into Japan’s theatrical tradition, bridging the gap between modernity and history. 
5. Sunset over Mount Fuji unveiled a breathtaking sunset, casting a warm glow over the iconic silhouette of Mount Fuji. 
 #TokyoTokyo #Japan

Golden moments exploring Tokyo…✨
Amidst the vibrant city lights, there's a magical moment that unfolds as dawn breaks over Tokyo, watching the sunrise over the skyline from our Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel. On our last day we ventured to Kabukicho Theater, this vibrant district of Shinjuku is home to this iconic venue, where Kabuki performances adapted in modern styles unfold. Stepping into the theater is like stepping back in time, as the elaborate costumes, mesmerising makeup, and captivating storytelling transport you to the world of Japanese theater.
#tokyotokyo #tokyotokyooldmeetsnew #japan

Embrace the beauty of autumn in Tokyo with these unforgettable experiences: 

1. Mount Mitake: A hidden gem just over an hour from Tokyo, where ancient cedars and vibrant foliage paint the mountainside.
2. Hatonosu Valley Walk: Immerse yourself in nature's golden embrace with a stroll through the scenic  HatonosuHatanosu Valley. 
3. Lake Shiromaru Canoeing Experience: Glide through the serene waters, surrounded by the breathtaking colours of fall.
4. Mitake Sanso Shukubo Experience: Stay in a traditional temple lodge, experiencing the tranquility of Mount Mitake overnight. 
 
#TokyoTokyo #Japan

Just over an hour by train Mount Mitake is my favourite hidden gem and most surprisingly this is still part of Tokyo… ✨ As autumn paints the landscape, there's a particular magic that unfolds when you combine the vibrant colours of fall with the tranquil experience of canoeing on Lake Shiromaru. The turquoise blue and green of the lake reflects the kaleidoscope of autumn colours—shades of fiery red, golden yellow, and burnt orange. #TokyoTokyo #Japan #MountMitake

The glow from above…✨ As I reached the top of the enchanting Mount Mitake, the panoramic view of Mount Fuji unfolded before me. The sprawling metropolis of Tokyo lay in the distance, its iconic skyline blending with the horizon. Lush mountainside forests carpeted the landscape, their deep green and orange hues contrasting with the sleek architecture of Tokyo. #TokyoTokyo #Japan #MountMitake

Awaking to the beauty of Mount Mitake…✨🍁🇯🇵 A place where time slows down. “We’ve been dealing with invisibility. We started realizing we’re kind of fading. So many of our friends say that: that they’re becoming invisible. Everybody needs a welcome from somebody else so that they can feel useful. It’s a real source of energy. And when you realize you’re not getting that as much—what happens is you get scared. And you also say: maybe we could do something a little different. So at some point we came up with the idea of the cute older couple. We were hoping to find some younger friends. We’ve always been attracted to younger people. You know, young people struggle. So we like to support them and wish them well and give them a lot of approval. And young people need cute old couples. They love cute old couples. So we decided to play it up a little bit. That’s what it is: ‘play.’ It’s really play. Have you ever seen two dogs greet each other? One dog will drop down, and bam, suddenly they’re playing. I think that’s what we’re doing. We’re inviting a play response.”
I just don’t want to let go.

“Occasionally I’ll have a beer after work and break out the sketchbook. But I had wanted to be this great painter. I wanted to do these grand things: big, huge oil paintings. But those days of painting all the time were such a roller coaster. There were these periods of extreme depression, followed by manic states of trying to put myself out there. I couldn’t do it anymore. I mainly felt sorry for my dad. I know it was rough for him. My mom hadn’t wanted me to go to art school. She wanted me to do something more practical, but my dad said: ‘No. This is what he wants to do, and I want to support his dream.’ And then I abandoned it. That was the first time I had to deal with real failure. A lot of times when you’re an artist—it’s your job, it’s your lifestyle, it’s your entire fucking identity. It wasn’t like I failed to do a thing. It was like: I failed to be something, you know? It was a failure to live up to what I thought was my destiny. But then on the other side of that-- there was this figuring out that there was nothing wrong with me the entire time. I didn’t need to be something else to have meaningful friendships, or a good relationship. I didn’t need to be something else to be loved and cared about. After work tonight I’m going to meet up with a person who’s in love with me, and I can’t wait. And that person met me long after I gave up on being a full-time artist. They met me when I wasn’t even a chef yet. I was a piss-poor, part-time line cook. But even then-- they decided I was worth it. So you know, there’s something there. There’s something there that’s enough.”

“My first end-of-life patient was a 97-year-old man. He had a much younger girlfriend; she was seventy-four. But they loved each other so much. Back when their spouses were still alive, the four of them had been great friends. They would double date together. And when their spouses passed away—the two of them became a thing. Every day she would come over for lunch. I’d always cook a little meal for them. I’d prepare the table; I’d lay out my little candles and my little flowers. As soon as she arrived I’d put on music and dim the lights, then I’d leave the room and go wait in the bedroom. They would cuddle and snuggle. And the beauty of it was—even though he couldn’t control his fluids at that point, she never minded the smell. Her love for him was so great that they would still kiss and all that good stuff. When the doctors said that it was time for him to go to hospice, he said he didn’t want to go. He told them that he wanted to come back home and die with me. I was with him in the end. My patients never die alone. Never, ever. One week after his passing I was hired by his girlfriend’s family. She had terminal Alzheimer’s, and I ended up staying with her for seven years. I fell in love with her. We were family, just family. She used to be a tap dancer. We’d sing together. And if she didn’t feel like singing, I’d sing. Even near the end, she always knew when something was wrong with me. When I wasn’t being the Gabby that she knew-- she would always know. When the doctors said it was time for her to go to hospice, her children said: ‘We want her to die with Gabby.’ In the final days she wouldn’t eat, she’d lock her jaw. But she would always eat for me. One night I could see the fright in her eyes, and I knew it was time. My patients never die alone. Never, ever. So I climbed under the covers with her. And she passed away in my arms.”

“Just the other day a video popped up on Facebook. It was only five years ago. We were in the park. I was pushing her on the bike, letting go. We used to have so much fun together. We’d always get ice cream. She’s a strawberry girl. I’m a vanilla guy. Chipwich, actually. I’m a Chipwich guy. She’d give me a hug afterward, tell me I was the best dad ever. We were such good friends. But now it feels like we’re so far apart. She doesn’t want to talk to me anymore. Even when she’s upset, she’ll ignore me and go to her room. It’s like: C’mon. I was fifteen too. I know what it’s like. But she’ll come back, I know that. They always come back. But it does feels like you’re getting your heart ripped out a little bit.  But look, I get it. She’s figuring out life. You have to back off. You have to give them space. Cause if you charge after them and get all aggressive about it, you might push them away forever. But they always come back, right? One day she’s gonna realize that I’m not the enemy and I’m really her dad, her friend. I still get a flicker of it, every once in awhile. We had a really surreal moment last year. Her birthday is March 17th. She’s a St. Paddy’s Day birthday. We always take her to a Spanish restaurant on Long Island, but this time we did something special. Her uncle used to be a bodyguard for Taylor Swift, and we still know some people at the company. So they got us tickets to her concert. Fifth row seats. I mean, don’t get me wrong. We paid for them-- but fifth row center. She was crying. I got a big hug. A big kiss. A ‘Thank you, Dad.’ It wasn’t ‘You’re the best dad ever.’ But it was a really big: ‘Thank you, Dad.’”

“I’m taking a break from school until I figure things out. I guess I have rebel traits. There were just so many things that felt out of my control, and it bothered me. You have to wake up at this time. You have to go do this. You have to go do that. It’s like I didn’t have any originality. There was a certain point when I realized that everything-- this whole routine that I had, had been given to me by other people. And the weird thing is—whenever you try to remove yourself from that equation, and stop doing what other people want, you kind of get ostracized and outcast. That’s kinda what happened to me. I have a great family, but it’s full of strong personalities. I had so many people telling me: do this, do that. They said it was a ‘respect’ thing. You know: ‘I’m the adult, so you should respect me.’ But I never understood that. Because at what age do I get this thing called respect? Nobody in my family could ever answer that question. Is it when I have a kid? Is that it? Or is it when I'm paying a certain amount of bills? At what point do I step up on the pedestal?”

niños disfrutando el privilegio de ser niños.

es centrar tu energía para sostener al que no tiene fuerzas;

La gran mayoría de las parejas que decidieron casarse ya tienen una relación con una década de trayectoria aproximadamente, algunos asistieron en compañía de sus hijos y, 
en presencia de ellos, se intercambiaron los anillos. Este punto, me pareció digno de elogio.

En este tiempo, cuando el pacto matrimonial se encuentra en estado de desnutrición; 
ser testigo de 20 decisiones es una bendición.
Hablando de tiempo, 
la lluvia estuvo presente y puso a correr a las novias y todos los organizadores. Lo agradable de este fenómeno es un recordatorio del mismísimo Creador. 

En ocasiones, nuestras relaciones se asemejan a esos tiempos cálidos, agradables y tropicales
 ¡La época dorada! Pero la gran realidad,
el matrimonio se fortalece en los tiempos de tempestad, cuando la lluvia se impone y debemos fluir con las cosas que no podemos cambiar, aceptando que todo tiene su tiempo; 
tiempo de sol y tiempo de lluvia, 
lo importante es permanecer unidos, 
para ser ese cordón de tres dobleces junto a Dios.

Queridos matrimonios, 
¡Dios los bendiga en gran manera! Fue un honor para mi, ser testigo de sus pactos.

Tía Rubén y Tía Luisa, el verdadero amor.

Ambos tienen 73 años, 
nacieron el mismo día, mes y año.
Él de Maracaibo, ella de Maturín, 
en la actualidad tienen 53 años de casados.

Los primeros días de febrero visitamos la isla de Margarita y pudimos compartir con ellos, actualmente están viviendo allá. 

Tío Rubén, 
desde el año 2018 se encuentra dándole batalla a las secuelas de un ACV, 
tía Luisa, 
el pasado mes de octubre del 2023 sufrió una caída que generó una pequeña fractura en la rotula de su rodilla derecha, 
el origen de este accidente son unas frecuentes lagunas mentales que padece en la actualidad.

En mis años, he podido escuchar algunas declaraciones de amor, pero las de ellos traspasan el alma.

Tía Luisa dice de forma sentida, “me da pena cuando Rubén me pide algo y no recuerdo donde está”. 
Él responde, 
“tranquila mija, yo soy tu memoria”. 
El tío es un caballero con una historia fascinante, llena de afirmaciones que demuestran el valor de la palabra. 

El 09 de febrero, 
regresé a Margarita en compañía del @dr.rodilla para documentar unos casos en el Centro Medico El Valle. 
Hice una llamada a los tíos y dije:
“Tío, Dios mediante llego hoy con el Dr.  Bustillo,
¿puedes estar a las 11:00 am con tía Luisa en la clínica para ver cómo sigue la rodilla?”

El tío respondió con su característico cantado maracucho:
 “¡Machete mijo, a esa hora estoy por allá, sin ninguna novedad!”.

Llegamos a la clínica, media hora antes de lo pautado, sin embargo, ya tío Rubén y tía Luisa estaban ambos sentados en la entrada del consultorio. 

Todas las preguntas que realizó el Dr. Bustillo con relación a la rodilla de tía Luisa, fueron respondidas por tío Rubén, fechas exactas, tratamientos, fisioterapias, etc. 
Todo está almacenado en su memoria haciendo honor a esas palabras 
“Yo pensaré por los dos”. 
 
Tío Rubén aprendió es a escribir con la mano izquierda, debido a su limitante con la derecha, tiene un registro escrito detallado, 
ambos padecen de los achaques de la vejez, pero en su acompañamiento honran ese mandamiento de SER UNA SOLA CARNE. 

Mi respeto y admiración para ustedes, ustedes no necesitan hablar del amor porque SON el amor.

Alexa Sky Lundes is 6 years old now and I enjoy every minute that I spend with her. It changed my whole life around. Mario Lundes stands in his bedroom with his four-month-old daughter, Alexa Sky Lundes, in Los Angeles, California, in the fall of 2017. Mario, who was jumped into a gang at the age of 13, talked about his troubled past, his recovery and a second chance. “I had my little girl and I got married. All that trust, I built it, little by little with my family members. I’m grateful to be alive. I made some really bad decisions in my past. But it’s never too late. I do regret a lot of the stuff I did. I have to live with that.” This portrait was made on assignment for National Geographic in 2017, with @kchete77, while working on the story, “How Latinos Are Shaping America’s Future.”

The Castillo family attends the Annual Día de los Muertos Art and Music Festival in Whittier, California. Veronica, as Mexico’s cultural icon La Calavera Catrina, stands with her two boys, Aiden and Samson, who are dressed as characters from the film “Nacho Libre.“

Celebrated all over the world, Día de los Muertos (the Day of the Dead) is a Mexican holiday in which people remember their ancestors. Many build altars, or ofrendas, to honor them, and ply them with items such as the deceased person’s favorite food. La Calavera Catrina originated from an etching by Mexican illustrator José Guadalupe Posada in the early 20th century. The etching satirizes the country’s elite just before the Mexican revolution. La Catrina is a popular costume tied to El Día de los Muertos and central to Mexican identity.

This portrait was made on assignment for National Geographic in 2017, with @kchete77, while working on the story “How Latinos Are Shaping America’s Future.”

Exploring beautiful Cuba 😍 Here is a rough guide to our Itinerary 👇🏻

🇨🇺 Havana, we spent a couple of days exploring the beautiful city of Havana where we ate at well known restaurants such as La Bodeguita Del Medio, had drinks on the rooftop of the Kempinski Hotel overlooking the Capitol and the Great Theatre of Havana, watched the famous Tropicana Show which has been going since 1939, walked the streets until our feet hurt and took a ride in a hot pink convertible classic car! 🚗 

🇨🇺 Santiago De Cuba, a 1 hour flight from Havana. We spent a few days exploring the bustling town of Santiago de Cuba and nearby places such as La Gran Piedra, the Cobre Basilica and El Morro castle before going on a bus ride to Baracoa stopping off at the most Wastern point in Cuba called Maisi ⛪️ 

🇨🇺 Baracoa, the oldest city and one of the most charming in Cuba. Located in the Guantanamo province, this Cuban jewel is hidden among mountain ranges and beautiful beaches. We visited black beaches, chocolate farms and cruised down the river in Yumuri Canyon 🚣‍♂️

One very bumpy bus ride later we arrived at the gorgeous…

🇨🇺 Cayo Saetia, here we spent the day swimming, eating, riding horses and relaxing in the stunning nature and the most turquoise sea. We then had a sunset cruise on a catamaran towards Holguin with lots of music and drinks 🍹 

All in all such a memorable and eye opening trip. Learnt a lot, met some great people and made memories for life! ❤️

Here are some tips for budget friendly trips:

✈️ *Avoid Peak Season* Not only a way to avoid crowds but you’ll usually be able to get a better deal. You might not be able to guarantee nice weather, but your destination will at least be a lot less crowded!

✈️ *Book in Advance* Prices will often go up as time gets closer to your trip. Booking train journeys, accommodation & flights ahead of time guarantees you won’t get stung by a last minute expensive prices.

✈️ *Purchase travel insurance* It may seem like an additional upfront expense, but it’s best to view it as an investment that can help you save money during medical emergencies and unexpected cancellations.

✈️ *Using public transportation* during your trip can save you money. The bus or whatever the local transport of the country you’re visiting is always cheaper than a taxi or an Uber. Walking is my personal favourite way to discover anywhere! 

✈️ *Choose cheaper accommodation* Hotels can be quite expensive so choose a more budget friendly stay such as a hostel or apartment. 

✈️ *Pack light* to avoid baggage expenses. Airports impose pretty hefty extra fees for large and heavy baggage. Also pack well, write lists (I have a notes app full of them😄) so you don’t forget anything and have to buy duplicate things abroad that you already have at home. 

✈️ *Eat Local* Stay away from the touristy areas. You can often see places that are popular with the locals, they serve cheaper food and you’ll get a much more authentic look into the cuisine of that country!

✈️ *Save up frequent flyer miles* It’s definitely worth joining a frequent flyer program & racking up those miles/points. Over time they really add up and can get you discounted flights and upgrades!

✈️ *Bring your own food* Whenever possible, stock up on sandwiches and snacks for the trip. Avoid buying meals at the airport/on the road/hotel minibar which are £££.

✈️ *Skip overpriced Tours* Explore yourself, with the information available online, it’s simple and easy to conduct your own tour for free rather than paying for a guide.

..and if you spend less on one adventure, you have money to spend on another! 🥳

It’s so important that pets are always connected with their families. Whether you’re a pet owner or an animal lover, there are steps we can all take to keep pets and people together:⠀
⠀
🐾 Reunite: In New York, I’ve seen so many dogs escape their harness and it truly feels like my mission is to help out. I’ve helped friends find lost dogs by posting online and scouring the streets. If you find a lost pet, other helpful tips include checking for ID tags or microchips and knocking on doors nearby where the pet was found.⠀
⠀
🐾 Donate: There are many community organizations that could use some help. Consider donating pet food to local human food pantries so a family with a pet can receive full assistance for the whole family. Pet groomers, pet hospitals, and local veterinary clinics may also accept donations to help those who need assistance in caring for their pet.⠀
⠀
🐾 Short-Term Fostering: Fostering is also a great way to help a pet and studies from the APA show that 86% of people see a positive impact on their mental health when having a pet. I can truly vouch for that! Fostering doesn’t have to be a long-term commitment either. Sometimes a pet just needs temporary care from someone in their community while their owner travels, recovers from being sick, and/or is hospitalized.⠀
⠀
I got Finn as an emotional support animal when I suddenly lost my brother. He means the world to me. According to the APA, 69% of pets owners said their pets help reduce stress and anxiety, and offer companionship. The bond that we can have with our pets is truly something amazing, and it’s also why it’s so important to keep people and their pets together.⠀
⠀

Todo es difícil antes de ser fácil…
Ayer era el cumpleaños de mi hermana, y antes de salir de casa para merendar todos, me asomé a la terraza. Me esperaba este atardecer que me llenó el alma durante unos segundos. Hay muchas cosas que antes pasaban inadvertidas y ahora tienen otro significado❤️‍🩹

Si algo he aprendido de un guantazo es cómo la vida cambia, literal, en un segundo. Resulta tan frágil e impredecible…

Y ahora siento como si mi cabeza fuese un walkman, y estuviese reproduciendo, rebobinando y cambiando de casette constantemente. Repasando momentos previos donde quizás se me escapó algo que debería de haber advertido mejor, recordando las cosas tan genuinas que nos hacen tan únicos a cada uno, y sobre todo tratando de no olvidar tu voz. Tus gestos. Tu sonrisa. Tu olor.

Estos días pensaba que no hay nada mas cruel que que el mundo siga girando cuando para ti la vida ha frenado en seco. Y es en parte gracias a esa cruda y cruel realidad que sigues hacia adelante. Porque la vida se celebra viviéndola. Y aunque cueste un poquito mas, seguiremos encontrando motivos para celebrarla aunque ya no estes aquí. Y cuando me acomodo en este pensamiento y entiendo que es mi nueva realidad, no puedo evitar poner otro casette antiguo y volver la vista atrás. Como aquel día de verano, cuando íbamos de camino a la playa, en el corsa rojo antiguo, sonando Sweet Home Alabama de aquel casette que te tocó con Nescafé, y con las ventanillas bajadas.

Me encuentro recordándote en momentos que hoy me parecen un tesoro. Y ojalá poder grabar todo lo que tengo en mi memoria en nuevo casette, pero uno de verdad. Porque quiero recordarte tal y como eras, en toda tu totalidad.

✨La magia reside y permanece en las cosas pequeñas del diario✨

.

Ha sido todo demasiado rápido, y mi mamá demasiado joven…

Mi madre era un mujer feliz, optimista, generosa y con un corazón inmenso. Siempre dispuesta a ayudar sin pedir nada a cambio y sin poner un «pero». Ella veía el vaso medio lleno en todo porque era paciente, entendía los tiempos de la vida y por eso sabía quitarle hierro a cualquier asunto. Decir que adoraba a mi madre por encima de todo, se queda demasiado corto. Ella siempre fue mi referente en todo. Soy lo que soy gracias a ella porque me tocó la mejor de todas❣️

Me voy a tomar un tiempo. Necesitamos recomponernos, procesar todo lo que ha sucedido y aprender a adaptarnos a esta nueva realidad.

Looking for Scotland: If Scotland is on your travel list for 2024 let me offer my Top Ten Things To Do. Everybody has their list of Best Castles and Must See sites. With my list I hope to suggest ways of seeing Scotland that might get you away from checklist travel and into another realm. Here goes:

1. Visit a castle (of course) but let the history wash over you. Do a deep dive into its turns of fortune, failures and disasters. Eilean Donan is a good one. 
2. Find a Highland Games in some remote glen. Take part in the gathering, however you can. If they have a visitors tug of war, pull for all your worth. If they have a dance, dance.
3. Find a remote country house hotel that knows Scottish hospitality. Let them spoil you for a couple of days. I’d hole up in Eilean Iarmain on Skye.
4. Sit amongst the puffins. Be patient.
5. Find someplace with stonking, bloody Scottish history. Iona is just one of many, but it’s got Celtic Saints, Viking raids and Macbeth in the graveyard.
6. Visit a coastal village with one pub. Buy somebody a pint. Pennan is a likely choice, but watch Local Hero before you go. 
7. Be picky about which distillery you visit. Avoid glitz. Strathisla is one of those ancient distilleries that still looks old…because it actually is. 
8. Lie down in the heather and take a nap.
9. Find a red phone booth that is still working and call someone. 
10. Spend an evening at a stone circle in the moonlight. The Stones of Stenness in Orkney is a good bet. 

There’s more, of course, and much I have yet to see myself. Before you go buy Scotland, the Best by Peter Irvine, the hands down best Scottish guide book. Relish its handpicked lists of treasures and oddities long before you go.

Scotland Fix: Few settings seem so right for listening to the Great Highland Bagpipe as a rainy day at the head of Loch Shiel. Here at the Glennfinnan Gathering the piping competition takes place down by the shore, the very place where Bonnie Prince Charlie came ashore on his ill-fated Jacobite mission. The bagpiper is concentrating as he plays the piobaireachd, the ancient classical music set down in the mists of lost history and still revered today. He paces around the platform, "slowly, but not too slowly" in precise, measured steps. The judge stares into the distance, careful to not let the magnificent, romantic scene cloud his judgement. Judge and piper share a quest to keep alive something that could die without them. For a bagpiper, I think, this is Carnegie Hall.

And it’s always possible that showing less tells a more interesting story than showing more. My practice is to try every compositional option that I can while the light lasts.  I can decide later what worked best.

Scottish landscapes reveal much of Scottish character, especially out in the islands where the Atlantic storms do battle with the land. So it was that a sodden pony on North Uist taught me a lesson on rainy day. 

It sidled up next to my car, refusing to go stand a ways off in the moor to make a pretty picture for me, a picture that did not involve a soggy mane. But then it dawned on me: the soggy mane was the picture, a pattern of ringlets redolent of Celtic symbols seen here a thousand years ago. 

Sometimes I’m afraid that the land is trying to tell me something and I won’t get it. Over fifty years of photography that has happened to me plenty of times. It’s daunting to think that you can be standing in front of something wonderful, and just not be able to see it. So I thank this pony for its patience. It stood there long enough for me to get it. 

Had any stories of revelations that got away?  Comments welcome.

In Scotland the right light can produce magic on the landscape. Such was the case when Loch Cill Chriosd lit up with the first rays of sunrise that morning as I was driving back from Elgol on the Isle of Skye. 

By the way, locals call it the Hairy Loch for good reason owing to these grasses. It’s often calm and a prime photo stop on the Isle of Skye — if the midgies are held at bay. 

Lots of legends attached to this place, that St. Columba drove away an evil spirit in 570 AD (he did that a lot), that a shape shifting water horse (Kelpie) took up residence and in the form of a handsome young man lured maidens to their death in the loch, even that a Norwegian princess named Saucy Mary is buried on top of Beinn na Caillich back there.

Scotland Fix of the Day: Getting away sometimes leads to finding yourself. That’s one attraction of the Scottish landscape for me, the chance to truly be alone with the place, unfettered with expectations, content to accept the character of the land (and of yourself) as it is. Here are a few places that have evoked that sense for me. 

1. The long one-track road on Jura that ends after 17 miles just south of the house where George Orwell wrote 1984.
2. Eilean na Moine, the wee island in Loch Eilt that became most known as the site of Dumbledore’s grave. Few other island seem to stand so alone. 
3. The moors of Assynt stretch off into vast openness when seen from atop Sgorr Tuath, or from Stac Pollaidh across the way. 
4. Evening at the Ring of Brodgar in Orkney can be sublime, the stones — and endless time — your only companions. I’ve often felt comforted here. 

Are you one of the travelers who seek out such solitude, even loneliness, in the landscape.

Scotland Fix of the Day: Over the Sea to Skye is a beautiful song and an alluring thought.  One such journey is from Elgol over to Loch Coruisk where you are surrounded by the jagged sweep of the Black Cuillins wrapping around the remnants of the ancient caldera.  My favorite boat that makes this trip is the Bella Jane, the journey over as rewarding as the hike once you get there. On the way back the River Scavaig tumbles down to the sea, the shortest river in the British Isles. Been there? Did you see the Kelpie?

Scotland Fix: Red deer high on the hills above Lochcarron recall the Monarch of the Glen, the great painting by Edwin Landseer. But wild deer in Scotland can actually be quite friendly, especially if the gamekeeper (Colin Murdoch) feeds them. These were also quite happy to pose for me. Scotland Fix of the Day: Seaside villages in Scotland have always beckoned to me, evoking romantic ideals of another life, another way of living. Actual life has a way of being more complicated, of course, but exploring these communities (in all their variety) speaks to an inner longing that I tugs at me. 
 
1. Pennan sit snug along the base of the cliff on the Moray Firth, perhaps one of the most iconic of seaside villages.
2. Port Ellen on Islay is another of those planned communities that stretch along the shore with colorful boats pulled up onto the grass.
3. Craighouse on Jura can’t be very big because the whole island is only 200 people, but it offers quiet views of the bay from the bench by the war memorial.
4. Stromness in Orkney sidles along the bay, originally laid out when when sea captains bound for Canada and the Antarctic built their houses with a dock out back. 
5. St. Andrews Cathedral offers spectacular views down on the ruins and the graveyard from atop St. Rule’s Tower, views that stretch off to the famous strand. 
6. Pierowall on Westray, circles the bay, a North Sea village dating back through history like a chronicle of archeological ages, at least as far back as the Neolithic. 
7. Elgol on the Isle of Skye probably has more boats than houses. There is a school and a pier with views out to Rum in the distance, and stunning rock formations washed endlessly by the sea. 

I’m still exploring seaside villages. Which ones do you recommend? I’ll add them to my list. Thanks.

The neon pink blackcap basslet is a species of fish that calls the western Atlantic Ocean home. Commonly found in deep waters, this fish inhabits reefs, and when frightened, will hide among rocks. Blackcap basslets are considered highly territorial and do not like to share space with other basslets or similar looking species. In the wild, they feed primarily on small invertebrates. Exciting news out of Kenya! Wildlife partners from Kenya and the US have recently opened a new 250 acre sanctuary for the endangered mountain bongo. Once plentiful throughout their range, it is estimated that there are less than 100 mountain bongos remaining in Kenya as a result of over hunting. With the opening of the sanctuary in Meru County, locals vowed to never hunt the species for meat again, and stringent measures have been put in place to protect and multiply their numbers. Partners are hopeful that the arrival of 25 bongos to Kenya, sent from @rarespec Foundation’s breeding center in the US, will signify a brighter future for the species, bringing it back from the brink of extinction. Red-bellied squirrels like this one call southern China, Malaysia, and the mountains of Taiwan home. Like most squirrel species, they rely heavily on a diet rich with leaves, fruit, seeds, nuts, acorns, and even the occasional insect. To ensure that their bellies stay full all year long, these critters will actually adjust their diet to align with seasonal food availability. In winter, they’ll consume flowers from the camellia tree, then transition to a leaf-based meal plan from April to May. Come summer, fruits become the primary food source, and as the year comes to a close, they’ll pivot one last time, feasting on ants before they head underground. Photo taken at WildOne Wildlife Conservation Association in Taitung County, Taiwan.

In 2018, scientists announced the discovery of a new species of freshwater turtle - the Southern New Guinea stream turtle. Found in Papua New Guinea, this species was found to have evolved with two other species from a single common ancestor 17 to 19 million years ago. This is an exciting discovery as it indicates that these turtles witnessed the full geological development of New Guinea, unlike other species which appear to have arrived after the island had fully formed.

This cutie is a Philippine forest roundleaf bat @up.edu.ph. Common throughout its range, this bat inhabits lowland and montane forests where it can be found roosting in caves, mine shafts, and hollow trees. Active in the evenings, the roundleaf bat can usually be spotted snatching up insects to feed on as it navigates throughout the forest. Logging may be leading to decreases in this species’ population, but this bat has been spotted in several protected areas and is not currently believed to be at risk of extinction. #PhotoArk @insidenatgeo

This beauty is a Gordon’s wildcat I photographed @zooparkzajezd. Similar in size and appearance to a domestic cat, this species is endemic to northern Oman and parts of the United Arab Emirates. In this semi desert landscape, the Gordon’s wildcat spends its day sleeping, concealed in rock crevices, hollow trees, or empty fox burrows. At night, this cat emerges to hunt, feeding primarily on small rodents, birds, reptiles, and small insects. The Gordon’s wildcat is regarded as one of the most threatened subspecies of wildcat, largely due to loss of habitat for agricultural purposes and hybridization with feral, domestic cats.

Ostriches, like these two @albustanzoo are the heaviest living birds in the world. While they may not be able to fly, these birds are quick on their feet; capable of running up to 40 miles per hour, outpacing impressive predators like lions, leopards, and hyenas. On the off chance a predator is able to catch them, ostriches will deliver a powerful kick in order to defend themselves. A single kick from an ostrich can be fatal, delivering up to 2,000 pounds of force per square inch - that’s twice as powerful as blows delivered by professional boxers!

Meet the scarlet kingsnake. If you’re thinking this serpent looks suspiciously like a coral snake, you’d be right. As a form of protection from potential predators, the non-venomous scarlet kingsnake exhibits mimetic coloration - meaning that it has an appearance that closely resembles the venomous coral snake in order to confuse any creature interested in causing the snake harm. While this works well as a form of predator aversion, it can backfire when it comes to interactions with humans, who will often kill scarlet kingsnakes after mistaking them for a venomous species. To help you correctly identify these snakes in the wild, remember this saying: “Red touches yellow, kill a fellow. Red touches black, friend of Jack.” Photo taken @zooknoxville

Nature abounds. Just back from another trip to the Amazon Rainforest in Ecuador, a truly astonishing place to photograph. Our group had the benefit and wonder of staying at LaSelva Lodge, a jewel of an ecolodge nestled in the heart of the jungle. Perched on a lagoon, the wild nature of the jungle is literally at your doorstep every day. Beautiful rooms, wonderful food, and an array of incredibly knowledgeable guides who lead you through a week of discovery with certainty and expertise. A terrific week. Thanks to all in our group, hardy travelers all, who made lovely images. Shooting for Sports Illustrated was an adventure. Working, improbably, for the biggest, best, most powerful sports mag in the world. I say improbable as I was never much of a sideline, action-style photog. How could I be? At any major sports event, Sports Illustrated could populate any competition pitch in the world with photogs who need no explanation or introduction. Zimmerman, Leifer, Cooke, Drake, Iooss, Kluetmeier, Frakes, Iacono, Tiedemann, Biever, Millan - to name a few! Photogs with smarts, experience, knowledge of the game being covered, and an almost preternatural ability to be in the right place, with the right lens, at the critical moments of a contest. 
I was asked to become a contract photographer for SI in 1985. I was a feature guy, shooting the off-the-field stuff, the portraits, the concept-driven, illustrative spread type of photos that might lead a section or a major story. It was heady stuff, as SI had money to burn and the kind of powerful sway that would make even the most obnoxious sports agent return your calls. 
It was a great magazine, filled with writing that was often beautifully reflective and evocative, and the kind of still photos that made readers still want to pick up the magazine and devour visuals about a game that they had already seen. Can you imagine? It was like a Ron Howard movie every week, making a riveting story out of a game where everybody already knew who won. The power of good stories, in words and pictures, flowed from its pages. 
 
And after nearly 70 years of publishing, now gone…..

Forgotten Story: The Culture of Sugar

On 14 October 1492, Christopher Columbus touched land after leaving Spain on the islands known as Guanahaní, today called the Bahamas. Taking slaves (he was a slave owner, too), two months later, on 5 December, he landed on the island of Taino. In a typical conquering manner, renaming it La Isla Española, or The Spanish Island, later called Hispaniola. Today, Hispaniola is divided—the Dominican Republic on the east and Haiti on the west.

Knowing the culture of the Caribbean well, for the @NatGeo story, The Culture of Sugar (read the first sugar caption in my IG), Haiti is unique…in Haitian Vodou, sugar is of spiritual importance.

Vodou came with slaves forced from central and western Africa to Haiti shortly after Columbus. This most special, beautifully unique form of spirituality is often misunderstood and interwoven in Haitian culture.

@RegineParicia, a specialist in Haitian culture, knew of a Rada lwa ceremony 30 km (about 20 mi) from Port-au-Prince. Traveling with filmmaker @AnkaVision (Anka was creating a NatGeo TV Amazing Photos documentary for this chapter on sugar), we were welcomed by the community of Dumilseau Village in La Plaine into rituals, healings, and trance like nowhere else on earth.

Why sugar and vodou?

Sugar is essential in Haitian Vodou–many spirits require sweet, sugary substances.

Intricate patterns of religious symbols, called Veve’s, are created on the earth using flour, ground coffee, and offerings of sugar…sodas, and Barbancourt rum, made from sugarcane.

A table-like altar was created for the Cra Bi Nay Ceremony to honor the spirit Bossou, adorned with orange sodas, Coca-Cola, and candies.

Before a cow was sacrificed, many went into a trance, pouring sugary rum over their bodies and making offerings of sugar to the spirits. Others were healed with soda. Music was hypnotic, a reminder of the rhythms I heard as a child living in the Bahamas playing with my classmates at their homes, some of whom were of Haitian descent.

A short film in this album shares this beautiful intensity where sugar and spirituality merge.

Forgotten Story: The Culture of Sugar.

The history of sugar is bitter by dark moments of our human ego and desires for control.

For thousands of years, this sweetness was cultivated from the grass known as sugarcane, moving from Oceania by trade.

In colder climates of Europe where sugarcane would not grow, the demand for sugar during a time when such delights were rare, and spreading Colonization, the spice wars began in the 15th century for flavor-filled items like nutmeg, cinnamon, and yes, sugar. By the 18th century, most sugar was obtained from the West Indies.

During the Napoleonic Wars, sugar supplies were cut off by the English blockade of continental Europe.

To make up for this loss, Napoleon Bonaparte encouraged the growing of beets…in the 17th century, a German chemist discovered white and red beetroot contained sucrose, able to extract sugar.

After gaining a presence in France, the introduction of sugar beet production in the United States was first established, a short drive from where I live to North Hampton, MA—by 1883, ceasing operation.

It wasn’t until seeds arrived in North Dakota from Michigan in the late 1800s that sugar from beets became viable. With heavy labor done by German and Russian immigrants who moved to North Dakota for jobs, the surrounding areas of Fargo became the epicenter of sugar production in the United States.

In 1899, American Crystal Sugar was founded, and so began the most significant crop production of sugar beets in North America, along the Red River Valley in North Dakota.

From the @NatGeo story, The Culture of Sugar, which was never published (read why in the caption in my first post of this story), sharing with you the mesmerizing movement of how nearly all white processed sugar at American Crystal Sugar is produced for US consumption.

To understand the enormity of our desire for sweetness, the images inside the storage silo represent 35 million tonnes, or the equivalent of 7 million 2.3 kg (5 lb) bags of sugar.

A short film is in this album on the mysterious machines that create this sugar desire.
