Forgotten Story: The Culture of Sugar.

Once a rare spice, every genus of sugar originates east of the Wallace Line in Papua New Guinea.

Beginning in around 4 C.E., sugar moved from Oceania through trade often connected to conflict and slavery…at that time in history, nowhere else on earth had or grew sugar.

For the unpublished @NatGeo story, The Culture of Sugar, these crystals are culturally unimaginable in PNG culture.

Unaware of what to expect, my contact was Father Paul Kanda, a Papuan Catholic priest who told me, “John, just come, I will show you.”

After four days of travel by propeller plane and trucks to reach the highlands of Enga Province, there was a wedding.

Father Kanda drove us to a hillside where I met William Waikenda, a kamongo or tribal leader, preparing for the Yari ceremony in Wapai Village. He would lead the Yole Maingi (bride prize) ceremony in a few hours, uniting a woman and man before a Christian marriage.

Insects swarmed everywhere, drawn to the sweetness of sugarcane leaning against a tree.

Down the hill, I found the groom, 24-year-old Samuel Tembe, skipping along a pathway through a gorgeous landscape of greenness to meet his bride.

At a clearing in Wapai was 20-year-old Janet Sani and her family; Samuel took his place next to his future wife and immediately began the Yole Maingi (bride prize).

Why sugar?

Giving and eating raw sugarcane is essential; the bridge or conduit to unite two tribes creates harmony between the bride and groom’s tribes. A practice for thousands of years in the Highlands of Papua New Guinea.

When leaving, William Waikenda insisted I take three sugarcane sticks. Unkind to say no, confused about what to do with this long gift, I rested three canes out of the truck window, enjoying a few bites. Later, I gave Father Kanda the rest of the massive poles.

Sharing more stories of the fascination with sugar from Papua New Guinea in the coming days…. The Yole Maingi ceremony only touches the unimaginable sugar culture, the roots of this now common sweetener.

Also included is a short video.

Why did the sugar story not publish?
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
National Geographic had commissioned a new writer. Midway through the reporting, they rejected the manuscript. Such unfortunateness was a gift…I could write the visual narrative, unconstrained in complete curiosity.

When the photography was completed — Oceania, South and Southeast Asia, the Caribbean, and the United States — the magazine commissioned a third writer, Rich Cohen, author of Sweet and Low: A Family Story, a memoir about the creation of the artificial sweetener in the pink packet invented by Benjamin Eisenstadt, Cohen’s grandfather.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
National Geographic accepted Rich’s manuscript, but this time, the text had nothing to do with the culture of sugar: the story focused more on the health issues of sugar, not a global narrative on the culture of sugar.

My good friend, @robertclarkphoto, was hired to photograph sugary foods in his studio, creating beautiful images to accompany Cohen’s text.

I was not upset at this unexpectedness. Life often shifts.

I’ve always followed the traditional thinking, honed into me by #NatGeo, that a photo should be as realistic as possible, without major edits or removing unwanted objects. For journalism, that works, but it leaves little room for more extreme artistic expression in post production. It’s taken me a long time to free my mind enough to explore that other side, which seems strange to me now as I write that because I consider myself a pretty creative and out of the box thinker. I guess that I’ve been so focused on the perfect/real photo that I never let myself think about what a photo could be if I completely break free of those chains. So I’ve been playing around with more extreme photoshop editing on a couple of images to see where it takes me, and it’s been really fun and freeing. I’d never call these real photos, but they are based on actual images I’ve taken (I’ve included both the edited and unedited images in two examples). What do you think of the heavily edited surreal photos? Too much? Or shall I continue down this path?
Lone twiga (giraffe) ambling at sunset on the great open expanse of Kenya’s Maasai Mara. #kenya #safari

Eye to Eye. 

It’s tough to watch any animal die. Our human instinct is to look away and feel a sense of shame/guilt for even wanting the hunt to happen in the first place. It’s a normal and perfectly fine reaction. But life in the Maasai Mara is not easy, and lions must kill to survive. We’ve lost over 90% of the lion population in the last 50+ years. Lions are in serious trouble, and I can’t imagine a world in which we can’t see them in the wild. So I try to bear witness, without wishing a kill to happen but also not looking away when it does.

On this particular morning, these two male lions ambushed a rather large herd of buffalo, and managed to separate this one from the group. It was over rather quickly, as these two brothers are expert hunters and together there’s not much that they can’t take down. That’s more than I can say for other kills I’ve witnessed. 

Such is the tug and pull (figuratively, and in this case, quite literally too) of life on the Mara. #kenya #safari

Image 1: Avenue des Baobabs in western Madagascar. I had always wanted to visit this iconic place, and it was indeed magical. Pro tip: sunrise, not sunset, is the best time to be there!

Image 2: Whale Sharks of Kaimana, Indonesia. Once again, a bucket list experience that came true in 2023. Pro tip: skip the snorkel and go diving with whale sharks for a more intimate experience with these gentle giants. 

Image 3: Kung Fu Lemur, Anjajavy, Madagascar. Verreaux’s Sifaka lemurs are known for dancing across the ground as they make their way between trees. Pro tip: get super low to the ground (belly to the dirt) to photograph the ballerina-like moves of this funny lemur. 

Image 4: Wilson’s Bird-of-Paradise, West Papua Indonesia. Seeing this incredibly colorful bird in the wild was a dream! Pro tip: use a super fast aperture lens (at least f/2.8) as you’ll be shooting in  the low light forest at dawn to see this bird. 

Image 5: Ladybugs in my backyard, Golden Colorado. My wife bought ladybugs for our garden and I had just started experimenting with a good macro setup. This is the first image I took with a macro lens that I am proud of. My interest in macro photography has only grown since then! Pro tip: in addition to a good macro lens, get a really good light diffuser that surrounds your lens to illuminate the subject, as macro is often shot at higher number apertures in low light. Proper lighting is essential.

The word “lemur” (/ˈliːmər/), from the Latin word “lemures”, means “ghost” or “spirit.” It’s not hard to understand the root of this name when you gaze upon Randrianasolo’s sportive lemur (Lepilemur randrianasoloi), also known as the Bemaraha sportive lemur. They certainly have a spooky gaze. Local legend says that this sportive lemur can cast spells with its intense gaze. I accidentally disturbed this little arboreal night lemur while walking in the daytime (its bedtime) through the dry, deciduous forests within the Tsingy de Bemaraha National Park in western Madagascar. I’m not sure, but it may have placed a curse on me. Fair warning: zooming in MAY cause nightmares. #madagascar #lemur

Mr. Fantasticus

Madagascar is filled with all kinds of fascinating creatures big and small, such as this satanic leaf-tailed gecko (Uroplatus phantasticus). Yes, that is its real name, and it does look a bit devilish, I must admit. However, when I first heard its full Latin name I almost keeled over in laughter. How could something be named “satanic” and at the same time have a Latin name that sounds like “fantasticus”? From that point on, and forever more, this little guy will be named Mr Fantasticus to me. It sounds like a superhero name….perhaps the next @marvel hero? 

Unfortunately, Mr Fantasticus is being captured (even within conservation areas) and sold to the international pet trade at alarming rates. Couple that with deforestation and loss of its natural habitat and the outlook is grim. Continued conservation is needed to protect and save Mr Fantasticus. 🙏
#madagascar #gecko

Unlike most of the world, endemicity is the norm in Madagascar. I eventually learned that I had to stop asking if something I was seeing was endemic because the answer was always “yes”. It became quite comical. The same could be true for whether a species was threatened or not. It was almost always threatened, sadly to say. 

I have always loved chameleons and was excited to see some in the wilds of Madagascar. Here’s another endemic and threatened species, a baby short-horned chameleon (Calumma brevicorne) that I photographed outside of the Andasibe-Mantadia National Park on the eastern side of the island. I like the colors of this photo, along with the precarious perch he/she was hanging on to.  #madagascar #chameleon

A Verreaux's sifaka (Propithecus verreauxi), or the white sifaka (a lemur in the Indriidae family), takes a break from foraging to see where her friends have scurried off to. Rest assured, they are not far. #madagascar #lemur

With pointy white and furry ears, orange eyes (that reflect Berenty’s red soil), a long and beautiful tail, and a seemingly endless desire for play and socialization, the ring-tailed lemur (Lemur catta) is a primate that holds a special place in my heart. I had the pleasure of spending several days photographing them in Madagascar’s Berenty Private Reserve, and I simply could not get enough of their antics. I apologize ahead of time for the lemur photo dump that is sure to follow. 

The most conspicuous feature of the ring-tailed lemur is its long tail that is adorned with 26 black and white alternating rings, the first of which is always white and the last one (the tip of the tail) is always black. The tail is used for balance and communication, not for grabbing (it is not prehensile). 

The ring-tailed #lemur is both endemic to #Madagascar and endangered, facing the loss of their forest habitat as a result of stock overgrazing, field burning/clearing, as well as tree-cutting for making charcoal. National parks and private reserves (such as Berenty) play an important role in the survival of species like these.

Hoy es un día irreal ¡lo logramos!

Hace poco Chris y yo conocimos un programa llamado “causada ciudadanas” liderada por el viceministro @luisernestogl con la cual el pueblo puede organizarse a favor de una causa y pueden hacerse escuchar y generaran un cambio, así que quisimos llevar nuestra voz y el apoyo de nuestra audiencia a otro nivel, desde siempre he querido dejar un legado, algo bueno que trascienda y ayude a la sociedad, hoy con orgullo y mucha nostalgia puedo decir que estamos recogiendo los frutos de una gran lucha que hemos dado 
El 4 de octubre decidimos lanzar una petición en la plataforma “Change.org” llamada “Aquí entran todos” que consiste en crear un sello que pueda vivir en muchos lugares públicos y concurridos, libre de discriminación que apoye la inclusión y la igualdad a pesar de las diferencias de gustos y razas de cada quien, con el fin de acabar poco a poco con la discriminación en nuestro país, naturalizando de una vez por todas esta realidad: la comunidad LGTB existe y ha existido desde tiempos inmemorables y no es una enfermedad, ni un desorden mental
Hoy 1 de marzo vemos el resultado en carne propia, firmaremos el decreto con presidencia y una vez más demostraremos que en redes sociales hay personas que creen en el cambio, que no solo están comentando cosas banales sino que por el contrario encontraron un lugar en donde su voz unida con el resto tiene gran impacto.
Hoy estamos dando un paso gigante en la historia de Colombia (ojalá se inspiren y repliquen esto en otros países) muchos creerían que el pais no estaba preparado para afrontar esta realidad de frente, la comunidad LGBT también son humanos y también tienen derechos como todos, puede sonar mas que obvio, pero es evidente que para muchos necesita ser recordado, hoy Colombia seguirá evolucionando en su proceso de crecer como un país tolerante, hoy yo Juan Pablo Jaramillo y mas de 4,5 millones de personas que pertenecemos a la comunidad LGBT nos sentiremos más seguros, más comprendidos y mejor respaldados que siempre, gracias internet, gracias audiencia querida y gracias gobierno de Colombia por abrir puertas a que estos cambios sucedan. 🐘no olvidare este día🐘 #AquiEntranTodos

[Hong Kong Show] Did you know that diamond crafting company SRK Exports @srk.one houses one of the world’s largest inventories of Twin Diamonds in round and fancy shapes (around 4000 pairs!) ? 

For those unfamiliar with SRK’s Twin diamonds, these stones are cut from the same rough and  have identical parameters, which require meticulous planning and skill to achieve! But how do you achieve this? Let’s find out ⤵️

💎 To get the best shape and maximum weight, the planner has to accurately assume the colour of the final polished diamonds; any mistake in assumption results in a different outcome of the colour.

💎 The cutter has to be mindful of the possibility of generating too much heat during the initial laser-cutting process, which can alter the gem’s hue.

💎 The bruiter during the bruiting stage also takes care to maintain the appropriate thickness of the girdle, as the gem’s hue could change due to a thicker girdle.

💎 The polisher’s keen eyes and understanding of the twins are used to achieve perfectly identical proportions.

📍 If you’d like to discover the magic of Twin Diamonds, visit SRK Exports at the Hong Kong Diamond, Gems & Pearl Show, located in Hall 7, Booth E01 at Asia World Expo until the 2nd of March!

Владу на этой фотографии 37, мне 23 и я понятия не имею, что интервью моей мечты станет его последним интервью. 

Я много с кем беседовала позже - от Спилберга и Линча до Брэда Питта и Роберта Де Ниро, ни у кого из них нет этой харизмы - сочетания мужского обаяния, интеллекта, открытости, тонкой иронии, легкости, безбашенной смелости, мудрости, доброты и жизнелюбия.

А на интервью я попала к нему случайно. Летела из Тбилиси в Москву, на съемки. В самолете рядом сел приветливый мужчина, лет 35, взрослый, как мне тогда казалось, рыжий и с каким то заговорщицким взглядом. 

Обычный полетный смолток, то се. Я, естественно, не удержалась и рассказала про свою передачу. Беседы о Грузии. Он спрашивает, а есть у тебя интервью мечты? Я не задумываясь - Влад Листьев. А кто еще? Я обожала его. Все обожали. 

А он такой - а, Владик? Нет проблем. Думаю - странный какой, хочет впечатление произвести. Берет у стюардессы листок, ручку, пишет номер, на 217. Не забыть. Набрала я для галочки, убедится, что это неправда. Ответила Альбина, они тогда вместе сидели в кабинете на 11-м. На нем до сих табличка и никто больше не занимал его. Она в своем ироничном стиле приветливо отозвалась о моем соседе, договорились о встрече. 

Я ехала в Останкино сутки, или год, извелась, извела оператора и водителя, смотрела из машины на башню, она то появлялась, то исчезала, и думала, если она исчезнет, значит нет ее и его нет и никакого интервью не будет. Это был мой первый раз в Останкино. Я не верила, даже в лифте. Когда открылась дверь и увидела Влада, от избытка эмоций, чуть в обморок не хлопнулась. Альбина и это ее теплое общение выручило.

Само интервью я помню, как в трансе. Когда закончилось, поняла, что не уезжается мне. Сижу мнусь. И как-то запросто Влад говорит - мы тут утреннее шоу затеяли, будешь про кино рассказывать? У тебя утренняя энергия. Я в слезы. 

А дальше было что было. 1 марта 1995. Черный день. Большинства участников тех событий уже нет. А Владик, наш любимый Влад, как сиял, так и сияет. И всегда будет, пока мы помним 💔

Kelsey Floyd
	
Starting pottery in early 2020, pottery was a way to connect with the peace and harmony within.

Self-taught, Kelsey curated a studio space in her home and got lost, or more so found, in the endless self-discovery of this art. She believes art and creation are intrinsically woven in the deepest and oldest parts of our humanity and can be tapped into when we come across the right muses to envision it and mediums to release it.

That is the ethos of her art; parts of the mind that can’t be formed into words, but can be sculpted through her hands and shared with those it tethers a connection to. Into things we can hold, adorn, and decorate life with.

Inspired by the natural and ancient elements of our world, her vessels incorporate free flowing curves and shapes while also combining that with the precision and restrictions of chains. Displaying a juxtaposition of unique and refreshing contrasted with the feeling of being unearthed and lost in time; her vessels are intended to connect with a sense of familiarity to who we are.

All of her vessels are hand-thrown, the chains and chainmail are hand-sculpted, and the pine needle is woven by hand. While creating, she works with the clay to bring out the organic curves and bends of each piece. She then adorns each piece with chains, chainmail, and/or pine needle. While chains and chainmail usually have a restricting nature, it creates interactive mobility with her pieces. The surface expressions, colors, and textures come together to create a valiantly organic and uniquely spirited form.

You may remember the video we posted pulling the sled on a family adventure. 

That is what we wanted to talk about to you today: the balance between family life & life as an elite athlete.

During the week, now that both girls are going to kindergarten, we have about 6 hours to train and work. 

Emelie’s training, time in the garden with Moonvalley, and Kilian’s training with NNormal and research. 

If we want to do a second session, it is often in the gym while the kids are sleeping.
When the kids are home for holidays or sick (yes, that happens often when viruses spread in kindergarten), we often train inside in the gym, or we alternate between morning/afternoon to train and be with them.

On the weekends, we prioritize being together. We often do a short session in the gym early in the morning and then spend the day doing activities with the kids.

Probably what has changed the most is that now we spend most of our time at home. Before, we organized our lives around races, with lots of traveling. 

Now, it’s the opposite; we plan for a calendar with few races or projects so we spend most of the year at home. 

Since both our parents live far away, we see if we can meet them around a race so we can also run the same race together.

In the end, it’s about being organized and finding a balance between all the things we want and need to do, sometimes compromising but prioritizing family time and training.

Adding to this, because not all training is about performance, pace, or speed, come our adventures as a family. And these are the best. We take the opportunity to explore Norway’s nature together.

The decision to move to Norway was based on what we thought was best for us as parents and as athletes: living more peacefully, slowly, close to nature, where we know we have everything we seek and need for our well-being.
We don’t want this text to make it seem like everything is perfect because it’s not. There are unforeseen situations. There are days when it’s easier to stick to the plan than others. 

In the end, it’s about adapting to each situation and not stressing about it but making the best of it.

If you’re so inclined, you can even pick up the trail that follows the water for a total of 18 miles here in the village. Though sadly, Danté and I didn’t have time. Do you recognize this island?

It’s probably the most recognizable Slovenian landmark and yet from my friends who love the country, I know it’s far from the only thing to enjoy in 🇸🇮 

Still with my one afternoon ashore in the country as part of our hosted @vikingcruises, I wanted to visit understand why it’s so famous! 🤔

It was a 2 hour bus ride from the port of Koper and after arriving we took traditional Pletna boats to the island in the alpine lake that doesn’t allow motored craft and was once home to a temple to Ziva [the Slavic goddess of love and fertility] ❤️

I fell hard for these gleaming wooden boats with awnings that are compared to Venetian gondolas, passed down through the families that captain them. They’re controlled using two long wooden poles and to do so is to be called a Pletnarstvo.

On the island: visit the Church of  the Assumption whose current Baroque design dates to the 17th century with a chapel from the year 1004. Ring the bell from the 1500s to make your wish come true. Then climb the tower for views across the tiled roof to Bled Castle.

Before departing, get gelato at Café Potičnica. You’ll earn it once you’ve climbed the 99 steps from the boat launch and walked all the way up the 52-meter high tower!

So what makes it all so special that it’s one of the most photographed spots in the world? I still don’t know. 😂 But it is a charming area! 🥰 And the lake is so beautiful when the sun is shining and that alpine water gleams turquoise and green. Plus the excursion did make me want to return to see much more of Slovenia! If you’ve been, where else do you think people should visit in the country?

#MyVikingStory #VikingCruises

Our ship was due to leave port in a few hours and I felt the urgency of the sun’s journey as it fell further and further toward the horizon visible between the masts of sailboats in the harbor. ⛵️ I could relax, unpack, and unwind. But I’d never seen Chioggia. 🇮🇹 What was it like? I had to know! And so I made my way down, out, away, with the wind in my hair and a pep in my step. 🏃‍♀️ Between tall buildings, through narrow alleys, under colorful laundry and past the eyes of a nonna or two I made my way to the busiest street in town: Corso del Popolo. It was buzzing with a post-work energy and a golden hour glow. ☀️ Residents on bicycles sped past me as I meandered under colonnades and by shops to observe a group of mothers circled around strollers chatting away while their older children played in the square, a couple alone at a café, and men debating over cold glasses of birra. 🍻 Further wanderlust drove me on to see if I could find a quiet spot and I discovered vibrant reflections making a type of modern art painting on the calm canal water; before raising my head to observe the alley before me overflowing with rainbows. 🌈 A promise of things to come? 🤔🤞🤞

On the wall to the right of where I was standing when I made this photo is the phrase, “Life is Beautiful.” Yet life has now been taken away from so many people not that far from this spot that I visited in 2018 [the Golan Heights].

Literally thousands of people have seen their last sunset or awoken to their last sunrise — or lost loved ones — while I have continued to exist in safety and comfort.

I fear that no matter what I publish, it will be inadequate or will be misconstrued. Words used or unused are an imperfect construct in a time like this.

Yet I know they are needed. We have learned before that our silence is but one puzzle piece which ultimately enables atrocities to continue. 

@lindseytramuta wrote, “To want Jewish people to be safe wherever they are and for Palestinian people to be safe and free feels, more often than not, like wanting the impossible. This should not and cannot be the case. But it won’t happen with the unspeakably violent ideologies of a terror organization and a nationalist government, with the wholesale dehumanization of Israeli, Jewish, and Palestinian people, and a total lack of compassion. It won’t happen with war crimes and revenge disguised as defense—not when so many civilians pay the ultimate price.”

That has stayed with me. For every bone and sinew in my body desires life in a world where Jewish people and Palestinian people are safe and free. Where not one more child or innocent dies. 

I do not support genocide. I do not think that any Jewish person, anywhere, should suffer or die for the actions of those who make the choice to send the missiles and disperse the gas. I am moved to tears when I see us engage in rhetoric that seems to celebrate anyone’s suffering. 

I do not have all the answers. I will continue to learn and listen. And hope to wake up tomorrow able to believe that one day despite so much evidence to the contrary, life can or could be beautiful for us all. 🤍

Made it to Venice, Italy yesterday with only enough time to see sunset and then find a place to eat dinner. But it didn’t really matter because any amount of time in Venezia always thrills me to my core. And what a sunset we saw!! 😍

I am sad to report that crowd level seems to be back to pre-pandemic levels and for myself I think this will be my last time here unless it’s in the dead of winter when there are likely to be less tourists (?) as being part of over-tourism for a place nearly being loved to death, doesn’t feel really good. I need to do more research and talk to more people that live here before I make any final decisions. 

What are your thoughts on over-tourism or visiting Venice? 

The city is seeking to combat over-tourism with a tax for day trippers and other tourists that I’ve outlined on my blog. I personally think it’s a good move. And I will be curious to see what residents like my friend @neumarc think as it gets implemented and we see whether or not it has a positive impact. 

Venice also banned large cruise ships from the Venetian Lagoon as it caused intense damage to the ecosystem when they were allowed. Speaking of cruises, I’m in Italy to head to the port and fishing town of Chiaggio where we are joining @vikingcruises for their “Empires of the Mediterranean” sailing. It is Dante’s first time on a cruise and Viking is one of the only lines I will go on an ocean cruise with because their ship has a passenger capacity less then 1/3 the size of the average for the industry. They also seem to be making honest strides to ensure they operate in ways that are as responsible and ethical as possible. I’ve also never met an employee who didn’t LOVE working for Viking. The ones I’ve met when on the river and one ocean cruise so far have been some of the happiest tourism employees I’ve found the world over.

This is starting to sound like a commercial 😂 and I didn’t mean to do that. But I am grateful to be hosted by Viking again so I can share more about them. AMA in the comments and I’ll answer honestly ⤵️

Thank you for making it this far. I hope your week is off to a great start ❤️

It is the world's 33rd-largest desert, and was included on UNESCO's World Heritage List on July 17, 2016. The name is derived from 'Lut' which means bare and empty in Persian and 'dasht' which means plain in Persian. In 2007 I was hired by @timberland to do a series of ads where they wanted a sense of motion conveyed, without using motion blur. I pitched them on using light streaks to show motion paths, by strapping headlamps to hands and wrists of athletes. This one here was with my friend @joekinder climbing on a bridge near Manitou Springs, CO. To capture this frame we determined the end point of the frame where my flash would fire and freeze the action, which is essentially what frame 3 is. Joe started at the base, and climbed to that point with headlamps on wrists and feet, while I left the shutter open, firing the flash once he hit our established end point. The total exposure time was 94 seconds, leaving behind his light path in a fun way, all done entirely in camera.

This is one of the most confronting images that I took in Borneo and, for me, this was one of the hardest things I’ve ever had to shoot. Afterwards I went back to my room and just cried and cried and I still cry to think about it now. I’ve seen pictures like this in the media and spared them a few minutes of sympathy before moving on with my life, but seeing this with my own eyes affected me fundamentally. These are the long term cages, for animals that have slipped through the cracks. They’ve either been too big to handle or sick with contagious diseases that can’t enter the main population. Some are just waiting until the resources are there to put them onto a pre release island, some can’t get along with other orangutans, some have been broken by humans and some are in long term sanctuary and will never have freedom again. Small though these cages are they can cost up to $20,000 and the resources aren’t there to replace them with better facilities, yet. Although I saw many happy endings for orangutans in Samboja and Nyaru Menteng, I also saw too many animals in these cages. Depressed and dejected, although some are angry still and rattle their cages and spit as you walk by. It’s the difficult job of the program director here to prioritize cases, move animals around the different facilities and decide which are eligible for release. With so many moving parts they’re doing a fine job with the resources they have. Please leave a like and comment, even if you don’t ‘like’ the situation. The more awareness we can spread the better. I’ve spent the last 18 months finding myself amongst the chaos of motherhood, exiting a business I loved and dismantling a set of beliefs that no longer served me.

During that time the biggest gift I gave myself was the gift of space. Space to reflect. Space to be curious about my life. Space to create without pressure. It was quite possibly the most impactful period of my life.

Amongst the many things I learned about myself, and life, is how to pay attention to the cycles. Because I’m not menstruating (still breastfeeding), I am more strongly impacted by the lunar cycle. My energy, emotions and moments of inspiration are all loosely following the cycles of the moon.

At first I didn’t notice at all. Then it all seemed coincidental. But today, noticing that it is the new moon and feeling into my body and energy, I feel deeply aligned with it.

The New Moon is a time for reflection and planting seeds for the next cycle. It is not a time to be kicking goals. And I feel that HARD in my body.

To honour how I feel, and the cycles, I’m adjusting my day today to create more space and execute easier tasks. I can smash out the bulk work when my energy starts to build again.

Last year I set a modest goal for myself to move my body two times a week.

One of those times was a half hour personal training session at my local private gym, a cost that I definitely could not afford at the time.

But health was high on my list of priorities and I partnered up with a friend to go halves in a 2-on-1 half hour session once a week. It’s not much. Half an hour.

But I’ll share something with you. That half an hour session, executed just 15 times, has been the catalyst for my new fitness goals for 2024.

Today was my last day doing personal training. For now at least. I’m joining a gym.

I sat on this decision for a long time because I have so little time to work, and I really didn’t want my fitness to interfere with my work time. I am also still struggling with motivation, which was the reason why I needed a personal trainer in the first place.

Then, in an instant brainwave, I realised that I could find a gym with a crèche that runs group fitness classes and train in my parenting hours. (Dreamboat and I equally split parenting hours and working hours.)

I’ve tested it out and my kids LOVED the crèche! And I loved getting back on a spin bike again. I was grinning from ear to ear.

The point of my story is twofold. One is that you don’t need to go from zero to a hundred. A year of gently adapting to exercise again created the momentum to set bigger goals this year. I’ve got my whole life to get my fitness on track. This year I hope to move my body four times a week, upping the ante on the intensity.

The second lesson is this, no matter what your personal circumstances are, there is a solution to your challenges. I have two babies and a business to restart in less than 25 hours a week. I also have zero motivation to exercise of my own accord. But I sat into the problem and found the solution. There is ALWAYS a solution.

Wish me luck on my fitness journey. ❤️

Everywhere I look, I see people I love and admire talking about their yearly planning and sharing their processes.

I love planning. During the Phhnix days, I was a staunch defender of planning and saw first-hand how planning creates the structure to achieve any goal. It’s an infallible system.

I also find planning to be personally suffocating. I don’t know if it’s remnants of the business PTSD I have (joking, but also not), some other type of block or internal resistance, or if my intuition is telling me not to plan. Hear me out.

At the end of the day, the point of a plan is to achieve goals. A plan is a tool. Me? I’ve never had an issue executing tasks or achieving goals. On the contrary, my problem in business is usually taking on too much and spending my days in overwhelm.

I’m tired of trying to do things the way that other people do them. 2024 is a year for me to get really fucking curious about my working style and test out new ways. Ways that might or might not work, but will teach me at the very least.

So I won’t be planning this year, at least not beyond the simple note listing my goals and a running to-do list. Instead, I’ll be spending the majority of my working hours taking care of myself so that the work can flow like magic.

This looks like meditation, gym, beach and personal development during work time, and brief periods of intense focus to get through the actual work.

I’ll be sure to let you know how it works out for me. I’m a multi-dimensional being attempting to undo every story I’ve ever been told about success. If I can’t FEEL good and be in my body, then I don’t want it. No amount of success is worth my peace.

Motivation doesn’t last forever. It comes and goes. It’s a normal part of the process. Its what gets you started...but what keeps it going?

I get asked all the time how am I so motivated 24/7? The answer is I’m not.😅

There are plenty of times I don’t want to train…I sit in the car at the gym procrastinating, or go to the gym do an exercise or two & just leave. I also sit at home telling myself so many excuses as to why it’s a whole lot ‘easier’ to just stay there and skip the gym.

However…the more I have continued on my journey I have realised that you can’t rely on motivation to keep you going. It’s much deeper than that. It comes down to DISCIPLINE.

Discipline is what keeps you going. Self discipline is the ability to do what you should do, when you should do it, whether you feel like it or not.

✨Discipline > Motivation✨

The key to still being able to successfully move toward your goals…is to SHOW UP for yourself…even on the days you don’t feel like it. You get it done.

An rather unusual set of photos on this account, but somehow Oman inspired me to shoot more local culture and people. I don’t like being a camera-in-peoples-faces-tourist, so here’s a set of portraits from a far. A couple notes about each of these shots:

3. 📍Nizwa - Blue hour, neon lights and a lonely chair. I really enjoyed this scene, especially as two men walked by.

4. 📍Sur harbour - I was snapping photos on a mountain by the bay when this heroic fisherman cruised through the scene.

5. 📍Bidiyah - It was midday, but the smoke from burnt palm leaves created a soft atmosphere among the palm trees. 

6. 📍Somewhere in between - I loved the old Toyota trucks I saw all over Oman. Fun fact: the boy drove off by himself moments later.

7. 📍Nizwa - Two strangers walking down jewellery lane. I really liked the look of the large arabic signs on every business. 

8. 📍Sur beach - Loved watching all the different activities on the beach. Men landing boats, Women picknicking by the car, kids playing in the water, dogs, birds, everything.

Lucinda Harmon Jackman,
4th wife of 7 to my namesake Levi Jackman, began her crossing of the American Great Plains on this day in 1849 in search of a new life free from persecution from the US government and religious zealots who declared her lifestyle as a Mormon an affront to god and society. Though historical accounts of Lucinda, my 3x Great Grandmother, are difficult to find in comparison to the documents detailing the life of her husband, the stirring personal parallels in our lives make it easy to imagine her as familiar. Because of her beliefs and non-traditional marriage, before trekking across the continent she was a societal outcast. She left the only world she’d ever known behind for a new chosen community, with whom she faced probable death in hopes of building a space where the next generation of their kind could feel safe. My heart finds a queerness in her story.
I don’t know if the Lucinda of 1849 would be able to comprehend my queer existence today, but that doesn’t diminish my desire to walk where she walked, reach through time and thank her for her precedent of pursuing love despite the sacrifices it would demand of her.

Lots of 🚢 questions, here are my top 10 tips! Feel free to add to the list if you’ve been on a cruise. 

1. Get the virgin app (45 days) before cruising and book as much as you can.

3. Book the unlimited spa first day (more than just treatments, full haven of rest & rejuvenation).
4. Don’t peak on the first night (took a full day in the sauna to recover)
5. Room service is free (I found out on the last day).
6. Seasoned cruisers can be savage (especially at the buffet). 
7. Wifi is not free (just get the premium package)
8. Payment is all in USD.
9. Bring seasickness tablets and take them before you get sick. 
10. Plan your days as much as you can before you board!

Dinner in 10 minutes? Try my Broccoli Pesto Pasta! It’s easy, satisfying, and made with only 8 ingredients. 

Ingredients
* 1 heaping cup very small broccoli floret pieces
* ½ cup fresh basil or parsley
* ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
* ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese or 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast, plus more for serving 
* 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
* 1 teaspoon lemon zest
* 2 garlic cloves
* ½ teaspoon sea salt
* Freshly ground black pepper
* 8 oz pasta, cooked to al dente 

Instructions
* Bring a medium pot of water to boil and place a bowl of ice water nearby. Blanch the broccoli in the boiling water for 30 seconds, and then use a slotted spoon to scoop it into the ice water to stop the cooking process. Drain and pat dry.
* Place the broccoli into a food processor with the basil, olive oil, cheese, lemon juice and zest, garlic, salt, and several grinds of fresh pepper. Pulse until combined.
* Toss the pesto with the cooked pasta. Serve with more Parmesan cheese.

Chilly evenings call for soup, so I’m cozying up to big bowl of ribollita 🥣

Here’s how I made it:

Ingredients
* 8 ounces crusty sourdough bread or ciabatta bread, ideally stale, torn
* 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
* 1 medium yellow onion, diced
* 2 celery stalks or 1 medium fennel bulb, diced
* 2 medium carrots, diced
* 1 teaspoon sea salt
* Freshly ground black pepper
* 3 garlic cloves, grated
* 1 teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary
* ¼ cup dry white wine
* 1 (14-ounce) can diced tomatoes
* 4 cups vegetable broth
* 1½ cups cooked cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
* Parmesan rind, plus grated cheese for serving
* 1 (8-ounce) bunch lacinato kale, stemmed, leaves torn

Instructions
* If using fresh bread, preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
* Spread the bread in an even layer on the baking sheet and bake for 10 to 20 minutes, or until dry. Set aside.
* Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, carrots, salt, and several grinds of pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 to 15 minutes, or until very soft. * Add the garlic, rosemary, and wine. Stir, then add the tomatoes, broth, beans, and Parmesan rind. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. 
* Uncover and remove the Parmesan rind. Stir in the kale and cook for 5 minutes, or until wilted. Stir in half the bread and season to taste. If you like a thicker ribollita, add more bread.
* Ladle the ribollita into bowls. Top with more bread, if desired. Serve with drizzles of olive oil and grated Parmesan.

My Rainbow Baby journey 😢🌈

Many people don’t know that Tyson is a rainbow baby🌈👶🏽. For those that don’t know what that means, it’s that Tyson came after us miscarrying our baby before him. It’s taken a few years to decide if we wanted to share this, and just as long to feel comfortable taking about it. 

After hearing of struggles to get pregnant and miscarriages from people around us, we felt that we wanted to share so that others going through this feel less alone, as well as to give some hope. 

In early 2017, my husband and I got the wonderful news that we were going to have a baby, we were ecstatic and began planning for this blessed baby's arrival. I chatted with the baby regularly, and planned its nursery, planned our announcement etc. 

Then suddenly, just past 12 weeks, we lost our beloved baby. The pain, sadness and loneliness that goes along with this was unimaginable. I’m not sure why there is so much secrecy around a miscarriage here in North America, it’s makes it so much worse. 

Not everything was ‘evacuated’ when it happened so I was still carrying the baby after the miscarriage. When I asked my doctor what to do, she said I had to wait for it to pass naturally (which isn’t true for everyone) 😞

For 9 months I still had all the hormones and the baby which made it so much harder to get past what happened. When I eventually found a new doctor, she took care of me and helped us to complete this chapter. We were finally able to mourn & have closure. When we were ready, we tried again 😀

“You can’t look at one of these and not wonder what’s going on with them,” said visual ecologist Katie Thomas. (@katiethomaskt)

Dr. Katie went into Sherlock Holmes mode when she first set eyes on this squid!

She binged watched 30 years of underwater videos @mbari_news collected which documented over 150 sightings of this squid & after close inspection, she noticed something really cool

This glittery deep-sea squid floats with its head down & fins up, sporting an enormous yellow eye that faces the water’s surface & a smaller eye directed toward the sea floor

Here’s why:

In the deep sea, it’s dark, almost like permanent nighttime! The big eye helps the squid catch even the tiniest bit of light that filters down from the sun or moon above.

The giant eye is on the hunt for the silhouettes of prey swimming above.

Some animals in the deep sea use a sneaky trick called counter-illumination, where they produce light from their bodies to blend in with the light from above. The squid’s big eye is adapted to see through this disguise and spot these hidden snacks! 🦑

But why is the big eye yellow? Well it turns out yellow filters out certain wavelengths of light, particularly blue light, which is most common in the deep ocean 🌊

This filtering can increase contrast & help the squid to better distinguish shapes and movements in the blue-dominated underwater environment.

Fun fact: Athletes wear yellow lenses because they’ve been shown to have a brightening effect in low-light situations due to their ability to reduce light scatter. They also increase the eyes ability to focus clearly 👁️ Whelp…GUESS WHAT ATHLETES, Squids already figured this out millions of years ago.

Growing BIG ol’ eyes is a luxury in the squid world, & nature doesn’t like to waste! So, the strawberry squid is super smart with its eye size—big where it helps, small where it can save on the squid-nergy bill! Talk about eye-economical!😂

Clownfish live in social groups with a strict hierarchy led by a dominant female — and in the absence of the dominant female, the largest male undergoes a sex change and becomes the new female. This biological adaptation ensures the survival of the group, as the dominant female is crucial for the reproductive success of the community.⁠

#DidYouKnow Clownfish are hermaphrodites, meaning they contain both male and female reproductive organs. In fact, when clownfish hatch from their eggs, all of them are born male. Out of the freshly laid group, the largest fish will become the dominant female. The second largest fish will become the dominant male. If the dominant female dies within the school of fish, the dominant male will then switch sexes and become the dominant female!

”Some photographs are impossible to explain because the chances of it all coming together are so slim. This is one of those photos for me and probably my favourite image I’ve captured this year.

It just so happened that this green turtle was returning back to the ocean after laying her eggs when at the same time a hatchling had hatched and made its way down to the ocean.

It was honestly right place at the right time and I managed to get down so quickly to capture this precise moment before the mother turtle passed the hatchling. A good photographer is always prepared as these moments flash by in a second. Always have your settings ready or custom buttons setup, know your camera inside out and always have it turned on. Rainy mornings call for some baking! 🌧️ This method of making banana bread in an 8x8 might be the best idea yet. It cooks so perfectly and there’s more of that perfectly crunchy sweet top! 

After-School Banana Bread 🍌🍞

Ingredients
 * Nonstick baking spray, for the pan
 * 8 tablespoons (1 stick) salted butter, melted and cooled, plus softened butter for serving
 * 1 cup packed light brown sugar
 * 2 large eggs, beaten
 * 1 1/2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
 * 4 to 5 very ripe bananas, mashed (I like to leave them a little chunky)
 * 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
 * 1 teaspoon baking soda
 * 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
 * 1/2 cup chopped pecans 
 * 1 to 2 tablespoons granulated sugar as needed

Directions
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray an 8 x 8-inch pan with nonstick baking spray or line it with parchment paper.
2. In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment (or in a large bowl with a handheld electric mixer), beat together the butter, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla until well blended. Add the bananas and mix until combined.
3. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and beat just until combined. Add the pecans (if using) and mix until combined.
4. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread it evenly. Sprinkle the granulated sugar over the top. I like to cover the whole surface completely with sugar; use as much as you’d like.
5. Bake until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes. Let the bread cool slightly in the pan on a rack. Slice and serve warm with butter.
6. When completely cooled, cover the pan with foil and store at room temperature for up to 2 days.

Embora inicialmente se acreditasse que botar ovos com casca dura fosse crucial para o sucesso evolutivo das espécies amniotas, incluindo mamíferos, lagartos, crocodilianos e pássaros, novas pesquisas sugerem uma visão mais ampla. Pesquisadores da Universidade de Bristol e da Universidade de Nanjing descobriram que algumas espécies que botam ovos podem ter evoluído de ancestrais vivíparos, desafiando as suposições anteriores.

Essas descobertas redefinem nossa compreensão sobre a evolução da reprodução animal, mostrando que a capacidade de botar ovos com casca dura pode não ter sido tão precoce ou tão fundamental quanto se pensava. A diversidade de modos reprodutivos, incluindo a retenção prolongada de embriões, desempenhou um papel importante no sucesso evolutivo das espécies. Portanto, a galinha veio antes do ovo, marcando uma reviravolta intrigante na narrativa evolutiva.

O que você achou dessa curiosidade?

As verdadeiras frutas do morango, no ponto de vista da botânica, são aqueles pontinhos pretos, que muita gente pensa que são sementes, sabe? Esses pontinhos são chamados de aquênios. Cada um deles é uma frutinha com uma sementinha dentro.

Que o Monte Everest é a montanha mais alta do planeta Terra todo mundo já sabe, mas você sabia que a colisão que o formou continua acontecendo até hoje? Não? 👀 Então vem cá!

O Monte Everest foi formado devido a uma colisão tectônica entre a placa indiana e a placa da Eurásia há dezenas de milhões de anos, e segundo pesquisas, a Índia se desloca em direção ao norte alguns centímetros por ano. Os cientistas calculam que o impacto ainda em rumo à Eurásia pode levar as montanhas a ficarem cada vez mais altas, com um crescimento médio esperado de aproximadamente 10 milímetros por ano na porção noroeste da cordilheira, e cerca de um milímetro por ano no Everest. 🗻

Mesmo com a erosão e a gravidade preservando as condições das montanhas imponentes, as placas tectônicas mantêm sua dança geológica, e o Everest continuará acompanhando seus passos. Tornando-se, então, uma área tectonicamente ativa e instável. Aos alpinistas, cuidado: é muito interessante, mas igualmente ordinário. #MUITOinteressante #monteeverest

Um grupo de pesquisadores dos Estados Unidos descobriu que pequenas quantidades de álcool podem reduzir o estresse no cérebro, beneficiando a saúde cardiovascular. 😊

🚨Mas cuidado: isso não significa que você deve beber para prevenir doenças cardíacas ou derrames. O álcool também aumenta o risco de câncer em qualquer quantidade de consumo.

O estudo analisou mais de 50 mil pessoas que participaram de um banco de dados que reúne informações genéticas, clínicas, de estilo de vida e socioeconômicas de pacientes voluntários.

Os pesquisadores encontraram uma associação entre o consumo leve a moderado de álcool e uma menor incidência de eventos cardiovasculares, como infartos e derrames, mesmo após ajustar para outros fatores de risco.

Além disso, os pesquisadores analisaram imagens cerebrais de centenas desses pacientes e observaram que aqueles que bebiam de forma leve a moderada tinham menores respostas ao estresse na amígdala, a parte do cérebro que processa o medo e as ameaças.

Essa redução na atividade cerebral relacionada ao estresse parece explicar em grande parte a proteção cardiovascular observada nos bebedores leves a moderados.

Muito interessante, né?

Se rosa for a sua cor favorita, você precisa saber que ela não passa de uma ilusão criada pelo nosso cérebro quando vê duas cores opostas se misturando: o vermelho e o violeta.

Essas são as cores que estão nas pontas do arco-íris, e elas não formam uma nova cor de luz, mas sim uma nova cor de pigmento. O pigmento é a substância que dá cor às coisas, como as tintas, os lápis de cor e os gizes de cera.

Então, quando nós vemos algo rosa, na verdade nós estamos vendo algo que tem pigmentos vermelhos e violetas misturados. Os nossos olhos recebem essas duas cores e mandam para o nosso cérebro. O nosso cérebro então cria a sensação de rosa, que é algo intermediário entre o vermelho e o violeta. Mas essa cor só existe na nossa mente, não na luz.

Por isso que o rosa não existe do mesmo jeito que as outras cores. Ela é uma ilusão criada pela nossa cabeça, mas isso não significa que ela seja menos importante ou bonita do que as outras cores. Ela é apenas diferente, e isso é legal. Você pode usar a cor rosa para pintar muitas coisas legais, como flores, animais, roupas e até bonecas!!

A cerveja se chama Epic OneWater Brew e é resultado de uma parceria entre duas empresas da Califórnia: a Epic Cleantec, especializada em reciclagem de água, e a cervejaria Devil’s Canyon Brewing Company.

Aaron Tartakovsky, cofundador da Epic Cleantec, disse que a cerveja não visa lucro e que o objetivo é conscientizar as pessoas sobre o potencial não aproveitado de reuso de água e que isso é um processo seguro.

Pelo Twitter, Tartakovsky anunciou que a cerveja será oferecida pela primeira vez ao público no dia 2/11/2023 em um happy hour durante a Greenbuild Conference & Expo, em São Francisco, Califórnia.

Today is the official #worldwildlifeday. A great day to  remind ourselves to safeguard natural life on this amazing planet!  People often ask what we all can do to lessen our footprints and help species, ecosystems or ethnic minorities in peril. For example what we eat, what products we buy…if, how, when and what we drive…for whom we vote etc. Low hanging fruits are also to support hard working organizations like @wwfsverige , @tpw_foundation , @synchearth , @janegoodallinst , @mission_blue and @redlist_of_ecosystems to help navigating towards a resilient and healthy future for people and planet! A hippo in a typical threat display towards a rival in Phinda, South Africa. Hippos are known to be a bit grumpy, but if you read their behavior and play your cards right it always works really well. Hippos move with great ease in water, ”swimming” by kicking their hind feet or simply walking on the bottom. They are well-adapted to an aquatic lifestyle, with small ears, eyes and nostrils set at the top of the head. Their senses are super keen even when submerged in water. By closing its ears and nostrils, the adult can stay under water for as long as six minutes. It’s no secret that hippos love water, which is why the Greeks named them the ”river horse.” Hippos can spend more than 16 hours a day submerged in rivers and lakes to keep their massive bodies cool under the hot African sun. The black market’s insatiable demand for ivory has turned poachers’ attention away from well-protected elephants to more vulnerable hippos! 
Don’t buy exotic animal souvenirs!!

I took this photograph of terraced land prepared for palm oil monoculture in Borneo on assignment for @natgeo (Note the bulldozers far down right in the image).
Palmoil has been and continues to be a major driver of deforestation of some of the world’s most biodiverse forests, destroying the habitat of already endangered species like the Orangutan, pygmy elephant, hornbills, king cobras and Sumatran rhino. This forest loss coupled with conversion of carbon rich peat soils are throwing out millions of tonnes of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and contributing to climate change. There also remains some exploitation of workers and child labour. These are serious issues that the whole palm oil sector needs to step up to address because it doesn’t have to be this way. 
Please avoid uncertified palmoil and support rainforest conservation and ethnic minorities globally!  #borneo #biodiversity #science #logging #fridaysforfuture #palmoil #conservation #wwf #rainforest @natgeo  @thephotosociety

Happy Valentine’s Day! ❤️ When resting, lions socialize through a number of behaviours. The most common peaceful tactile gestures are social licking and head rubbing which, for example can be compared with grooming in primates (or human stroking, cuddling, hugging etc). Social licking among lions often occurs in tandem with sometimes drawn out head rubbings. It’s generally mutual and the recipient clearly express pleasure. The head and neck are the most common parts of the body licked, which may have arisen out of utility, as a lion cannot lick these areas individually. Head rubbing – nuzzling one’s forehead, nose and neck against another lion, is a form of greeting and I often see it after an animal has been apart from the pride, or after a fight or confrontation. In general males tend to rub other males, while cubs and females normally rub females. I took this picture in Thanda, South Africa. #protectbiodiversity #thanda #southafrica #nuzzle #africa #lion #science #happyvalentinesday #mattiasklum #savebigcats @mattiasklumcollection @thephotosociety @natgeo  @mattiasklumofficial

The Rhinoceros Hornbill, king of birds in Borneo! I have spent many weeks waiting for this bird, shy like a raven, really looking like some sort of prehistoric dinosaur, to show up near my tree blinds in the Bornean rainforest canopy. This amazing bird also has one of the largest and most impressive casques, a feature they share with hadrosaurids from more than 60 million years ago. It’s hard to tell the sexes apart. Both female and male hornbills have casques, usually the male’s casque is a bit bigger, but it’s hard to know for sure. The best way is to look at their eyes.  The female’s eyes are whitish blue and males have dark red eyes! Trick is to get close enough....Shot for @natgeo in Danum valley, Borneo. #throwback95 #saverherainforest #hornbill #danumvalley #sabah #borneo #mattiasklum #rainforest #protectbiodiversity #wwf #iucnredlist  @thephotosociety @mattiasklumcollection @natgeo

A dwarf mongoose checks me out from a treehole in the forest near the Rufiji river in Nyerere national park, Selous in Tanzania. This the smallest of all mongooses and in fact also the smallest of all carnivores in Africa. Smart, sociable and fun to watch if you get the chance. Just like meerkats they have an astonishing vocabulary. They use small changes that’ll reveal whether the predator is aerial or terrestrial. The individual on guard constantly emits hi pitched squeaks so that other pack members know what goes on and can concentrate on searching for food. #dwarfmongoose #selous #nyererenationalpark #meerkats #tanzania @natgeo @mattiasklumofficial

Thanks to @nasa astronaut @loralohara who I met today in space (via zoom), I got to look down at our amazing blue planet from the international space station, cruising amidst the cosmic ocean above us. 

Astronaut O’Hara, five months into a six month mission,  shared many insights about the fragility of our world, how borders vanish and natural systems connect, what life in zero gravity is like, the properties of water (droplets float), how planetary politics stay behind and much, much more. 
It blew my mind. 

The second image by @loralohara shows the entire Grand Canyon in all its eroded wonders in one single frame. It amazes me to think that it took me 71 days on foot to walk the length of that natural wonder, but the space station crosses it in seconds. 

Thanks again O’Hara and NASA for reminding us all the wonders we have not just in space, but right on our one shared home.

3 reasons why I love working with silhouettes and you should too!

Emotional Resonance:
Silhouettes paint with emotions, casting a spell of drama and mystery. The strong contrast between darkness and light breathes life into my creations, conveying intense feelings that linger in the viewer’s soul.

Sculpting with Shadows:
In the world of silhouettes, details fade away, leaving room for the dance of form and composition. As an artist, I revel in the opportunity to sculpt with shadows, experimenting with angles, framing, and negative space to weave a visual tapestry that captivates the observer.

Universal Poetry:
Silhouettes are my universal language. They transcend genres and settings, allowing me to tell stories through shapes. From the quiet grace of a solitary tree to the silhouette of a cat, each frame is a canvas for my emotions, a testament to the versatility and timeless allure of this artistic expression.

Entering random streets, talking to locals, navigating through public transport, shopping through local groceries, trying to live the culture that has been passed on over the years to form the country what it is today. It's much more than just fancy pictures, these reels or my lame stories I've been spamming with, it's breathing this air and being here. I'd be travelling to four more places on this trip and I don't know which one I would find the best, but this surely made a place in my heart.

CREPES RECIPE!!! 🥞👨‍🍳🧑‍🍳Next Sunday is chandeleur in France 🇫🇷 meaning we’re gonna stuff ourselves with crepes all day long!! 😃These delicious crepes are filled with fried apples and bananas, coconut yogurt blended with blueberries, coconut caramel… Heaven!! 😋
So the crepe recipe is SUPER SIMPLE, 🤟I’ve been making it since forever, it’s my go-to basic and I love that it has 5 ingredients only, 👍 you know when a recipe says it’s super simple and the ingredients are beyond 6 or 7 you should definitely have your doubts hehe! 🧐 So no fancy flour, or exotic ingredients, or whatever here!!! Na-aaahhh! 😝 Just the basic that anyone has in the pantry. Also gotta say that : the first crepe you’ll make is always a flop, well at least this always happens with me! 🤷‍♀️ Who else has this problem??? 🤪 So don’t stop right there, make another one, everything will be fine! 🙌 Enjoy!!
✨
Ingredients
* 1 cup soymilk (or plant milk of your choice)
* 1 cup flour (can be a GF flour too)
* 3 tbsp cane sugar
* 1/2 tsp baking powder
* 1 tbsp coconut oil, melted
✨
Method
1. Put your flour in a bowl and form a well in the middle
2. Add cane sugar, melted coconut oil and baking powder
3. Whisk together adding the plantmilk little by little. Batter consistency should be very slightly thick
4. Heat a non-stick pan at medium heat, lightly oiled. Add a ladle and distribute evenly, to form a nice circle wait till it’s cooked (about 1 minute) and flip back on the other side. Allow the crepe to cook another 30 seconds to 1 minute before removing the crepe and placing it on a plate. Continue this process until all of the batter has been used.

Avo toast amore! 🥑💚Sooo LET’S TALK ABOUT AVOCADO SUSTAINABILITY, I want to be transparent on this, because it’s a subject that is close to my heart and what I want to share here. 🙂
As you may know, I live partly in Paris, partly to the french country and I started a veggie garden, so hopefully soon I’ll be able to grow and eat most of my veggies and fruit, lucky me!! 🥔🧄🧅🥬🥦🥕🌽🍅🌶🍆🥒
That said there’s always gonna be some “exotic“ goodies that I’ll crave… 🤷‍♀️
Avocado, bananas, chocolate, cashews… are a part of these, maybe you feel the same? 😉
It’s complicated because those, when you live in most European countries are definitely not sustainable and produced without ethical concerns. 💰😷
Now, my approach to this, is trying to source the products and if I sense they’re is the tiniest spot of shady on how it’s produced I WILL SIMPLY NOT BUY THE PRODUCT. 👎🚫❌
But I’ve learned through growing fruits and veggies and #permaculture that avocado can actually grow in France!! Corsica to be precise, as Bananas can be too! My neighbor grows them! 🤟You just have to know the good plant that can adapt on our climate, this one is a Fucca avocado, it’s the season now, organically grown, in a corsica farm. ✨🌱
And yes, it may cost a bit more and I know I’m lucky I can afford that, but I’ll always choose this one, than buying one that comes from unsustainable source.🧐
Your food choices can impact so much dramatically this planet, I urge youth do your research, and consume mindfully.🙏💚
Oh and tip of the day place your avocados with apples so they can ripe more quickly 😀 What about you? How are you dealing with these??? 😘

They work with local partners that determine targets of how these children can be provided with the most loving, sustainable, and nurturing environment. Me siento agradecida por tener a mis padres vivos, por verlos crecer también, por estar no solo en las buenas y por ese abrazo en la puerta del aeropuerto que me desbarata y me reconstruye en segundos. 
Camino hacia el avión con los ojos encharcados mirando a mi esposo tan bonito que me repite constantemente “lo que más me gusta de ti, es que eres de El carito”

Una relación de pareja no es lo que la mayoría piensa que es. No se despierta uno cada mañana para hacer el desayuno y comer juntos. No son abrazos eternos en la cama y palabras dulces hasta que los dos se duerman. No es una casa limpia llena de risas y amor todos los días. No es perfección.
Una relación de pareja es alguien que te roba la manta en mitad de la noche. Es a veces mal genio y palabras duras. Es estar de pronto y obstinadamente en desacuerdo, aceptar los momentos silenciosos hasta que los corazones se curen y perdonen. Es llegar a casa y encontrar a la misma persona todos los días, es monotonía. Es ropa sucia y camas sin hacer. Es orgullo cuando se trata de razones.
Es tragarse las molestas palabras en lugar de decirlas en voz alta para no lastimar al otro.
Pero en esas amargas experiencias se encuentran los más bellos regalos. Una relación de pareja es tener en tu vida a alguien que se preocupa por ti a pesar de qué y quién eres, a pesar de tus errores e imperfecciones.
Es alguien que ayuda en este duro trabajo de la vida. Es colaboración mutua, hacerse la cena entre los dos y sentarse juntos, a una hora tardía, porque los dos tuvieron un día loco. Es tener una crisis emocional y que tu pareja se acueste contigo y te sostenga, y te diga que todo va a estar bien. Y tú le creas.
Se trata de seguir amando a alguien a pesar de que a veces te vuelve absolutamente loco.
Amar a alguien no siempre es fácil, a veces es muy difícil. Pero es increíble y reconfortante. Una de las mejores cosas que alguna vez vas a experimentar en la vida. Texto @kokuhga

Spor salonunda en azından enerjini atarsın” diyerek onu boks kursuna yazdırdı. İrem ayağı kanayana dek kum torbasına tekme attı. Antrenörü @cemal_daglioglu dinlenmesini söylediğinde “Dinlenmek istemiyorum, devam edeceğim” diyordu. Yara kabuk tutuyor ama İrem her antrenmanda yarayı yeniden kanatıyordu. Ayağında hâlâ o yaranın izleri var. İrem’e “Bu erkek sporu, kızlar yapamaz. Niye yapıyorsun bu sporu? Kaslanacaksın, çok çirkin görüneceksin. Kadın sporu değil bu, sana zarar verir. Sen erkek gibi mi olmaya çalışıyorsun?” diyen komşular, bir yandan da İrem’in annesini dolduruyorlardı. Salona gelip giden bir çocuk sürekli İrem’le dalga geçiyor, “Bu sporu niye yapıyorsun? Dünya şampiyonu olacağını mı sanıyorsun? Senden dünya şampiyonu olur mu?” diyordu.
İrem 2013 ve 2014’te Dünya MuayThai Şampiyonası’nda dünya şampiyonu oldu. 2016’da Türkiye Bayanlar Ferdi Boks Şampiyonası ve Türkiye Gençler Kick Boks Şampiyonası’nda altın madalya aldı. 2017’de MuayThai Gençler Dünya Şampiyonası’nda çok zorlu rakipleri yenerek bir kez daha dünya şampiyonu oldu. Mustafa Kemal Üniversitesi Beden Eğitimi Öğretmenliği bölümünde okurken, gelecekte küçük bir salon açıp köydeki kız çocuklarını spora başlatmanın hayalini kuruyor ve şöyle diyor: “Kız çocukları inandıkları uğruna mücadele etmeli; her zaman umut olduğunu bilmeli ve hedefe giden yolda önlerine çıkan hiçbir engelin onları durdurmasına izin vermemeli. Kız çocukları güçlendikçe toplum da güçlenir, İnsanların önyargıları kırılabilir. Bunu başarmak mümkün. Kız çocukları yeter ki bunu istesinler.”
