My mother begins her letters with an update on the weather. It’s sunshine and 20 degrees, and the strawberries in the garden are ripening, or it’s partly cloudy and almost 6 degree, at least when the sun peeks through, and I’ve been pruning back the rose bushes. It’s the sort of beginning that makes me feel like I’m right there next to her. So today, with the surprise sprinkling of big fluffy white snowflakes, and plummeting temperatures, I updated her on the weather first thing as I called her this morning to hear her heartbeat next to mine. I held my daughter’s hand as she rested on my chest next to the furry four legged Mr Whiskey, who was not at all eager to start the day. I had buttermilk pancakes on the agenda, a beautiful bi product of all the homemade butter I made yesterday, but all she wanted was morning snuggles, so we just rested, with hands and paws entwined, and my mother on the line. We talked about the weeks ahead, and I listed all the delicious everyday treats I’d make with the emerging wild garlic I spotted last week on a drive around my old neighbourhood in Tisbury. Wild garlic pesto, pickled wild garlic flowers that I’d serve with baked trout, and wild garlic scones etc, you get the picture. It was time to throw on our coats and tighten the scarf, as we walked to school in the gloomy weather. Will you send me a picture of Spring, my mother asked as we said our goodbyes and I love yous, on the phone. So here it is, a little reminder that behind a grey cloud there is always sunshine, and after snow on the first day of March, Spring is imminent, and that’s something to take comfort in on this very day. If you want to join me this spring for a food photography workshop, send me a DM and I’ll pop more information over to you. And speaking of Spring, I cannot wait for my end of March fully immersion photography workshop in Florence! And if you’re waiting for the next newsletter, hang in there, it’s on its way;) xx

I could fill books on the topic of why I love living in England so much, but one of them is being able to bring in baskets of evergreens, wilted bracken, and blossoming flowers in November and February and June alike. Growing up in Norway the white winters were beautiful and definitely had its magical moments, but I love going for winter walks amongst evergreens and flowering snow drops in January while my mother tells me on the phone it’s yet another day of ice and -20 at the fjord island my parents live. I could fill baskets on end with flowering gorse, ivy, holly and bare winter branches with a few brown wilted leaves. Although flowers are beautiful, give me a branch with or without green leaves any day. So our little cottage, my garden studio and car are always filled with evidence of my never ending love for nature, bringing the outside in. It simply brings joy, the everyday kind, that cost nothing, but truly makes all the difference. Which brings me back to yesterday’s launch of my new ongoing stillife series, of wilted leaves and twisted twigs, a homage to the muted tones of the wilted botanical world of the English countryside. #myenglishcountryside

With a birthday breakfast tray in bed, feet wrapped around a hot water bottle, staying warm in the early morning chill, I re-read a book; “Constance Spry the Fashion for Flowers” by the brilliant @shaneconnollyandco , bought on a visit to the @gardenmuseum a few summers back during their Constance Spey exhibition. Like so many, I’m enthralled by her work, and was beyond delighted when I uncovered her cookbook, in a dusty pile of used books in a cardboard box, in a local antique bookshop. She was such a multi faceted and very ahead of her time, woman. She’s often on my mind when I create my floral stillifes. Last year I began a series inspired by old yellowed tear sheets of botanical prints, gathering leaves, insects, cones and seeds, creating these quiet flat lays in my studio. Those who know me well, smile at me as I duck underneath fences s d leap across the street to catch just the right wilted leaf that has caught my eye. I wedge a few in between handwritten pages in my journal, but most end up in glass jars that I keep in my studio. Gnarly, twisted, wilted, and broken, I love me a good leaf with just the right curve or stem. I haven’t show these more muted stillifes of mine till today, but since this is my birthday and the beginning of something new, I’ll start sharing this ongoing series of leaves, twigs and insects, as visual musings of the botanical world if you will. If you like them, there’s a couple available as limited edition prints on my website now. Here’s to the quiet beauty of the wilted leaf, and the twisted twig. #mycottagestudio

The sun peeked through every now and then this morning, and it felt like a warm hug. It was needed, it’s been raining for what feels like weeks on end, and although I don’t mind a drizzle or soaking, I turned my face towards the sun like moth to the flame. It’s the first day of the week, and although my birthday isn’t until Wednesday, I’m calling it my birthday week, and will unashamedly celebrate with little sprinkles of happiness every day of this week. Between a mug of tea at my daughter’s morning school assembly, and a well brewed coffee from the brilliant @bean_shot_coffee in town I stood on a street corner, when someone shook their head, and stopped themselves from saying what was on their mind and said: “It doesn’t matter”…and walked away. And I thought to myself, everything matters! Every moment of every day matters, everything we have in our hearts that we want to say, matters, the time we spend with someone else matters, we all matter, and life is way too short and way too long to not do, say or be, what we know in our hearts matter to us. I stood there in a small patch of sunlight, re-listening to those very words in my head. It’s the words of giving up on what matters, and it reminded me to always lean in, showing up, and daring to say what matters to me. It reminded me of being brave and standing tall amidst hardship, and about never losing sight of what’s important in life. I walked away with a reminder to live more, which brings me back to birthdays, a day I rarely if ever celebrate, feeling a bit silly about it all, and that it didn’t matter. Well, this is a new year, and if there ever was a time for change, it is now. So, a birthday week it is, with daily sprinkles of joy to celebrate another year around the sun, and that at the end of the day it can only rain for so long, before the sun finally comes out again;)

The daffodils, the crocuses, the dandelions, primroses and daisies, are all blossoming around my little cottage. It feels a bit early but is a welcoming sight. I put the kettle on last night to fill my granny style hot water bottle with. The cool air sent a draughty chill sweeping across the 350 year old flagstone floor but the view of the sunny coloured daffodils in our cottage garden warmed, if only visually. Our garden has a long way to go, but let’s just say it’s filled with potential, scattered with a few flowers planted by the previous owner that tells me there’s hope for even the smallest of plots. I wrapped my feet around the hot water bottle while editing images for the recent client shoot in Norway. It was a day of ticking off items on the to-do list, but by early afternoon I had skimmed the top of the list, and called it a day, Mr Whiskey agreed. We strolled down high street in our little countryside village, past the weekly food market and towards the green rolling hills in the distance. I inhaled the emerging Spring freshness with flared nostrils. It’s a season of change, and I could feel it in the air. If you want to join me this Spring I have one spot left for the fully immersive Photography workshop in Florence at the end of March and a couple spots left for my food photography workshop here in the English countryside in May. DM me for more information. Wishing you all a wonderful weekend. xx

It’s all slowly returning, the green, blossoms, eager birds chirping away and longer milder days. For now, it’s the rain, but in a way it’s welcomed. It’s will create the foundation for what’s to come, and there’s so much to come, so much to look forward to and so much to celebrate. The landscape around where we live may be a bit bleak  at the moment, but soon, oh so soon, the many colours of English countryside will return. Travels for work took be back to Norway these last couple of weeks. It’s was beautiful and in between shoots for clients in was a warming amount of time with family. It was needed and so welcomed. But then the last day of our trip came, and I yearned to return to my little cottage in the country. The daffodils were out as we drove home and a few trees were dressed in an eager coat of spring blossoms. We may have fallen asleep utterly exhausted after a day of connecting flights, lost luggage and passport issues, but when we opened the bedroom window to let the warm midnight air in, we feel asleep with a smile on our face…we were home, and nothing could dampen that feeling of peace and joy. #myenglishcountryside #england #home

And then there is this woman, my mother. Today is Mother’s Day in Norway, a date I only remember because my sister reminds me, but I somehow always remember the date for it here in England. But no matter the date, this woman needs to be celebrated. She’s simply my heart, my beating heart, and hearing her say it will all be well, is all the assurance I need to keep going when times are hard. She so incredibly warm you simply cannot sit next to her without feeling uplifted. Her wisdom has carried me through everything life has to offer, and now to see my daughter lean on her for comfort, for love, for consistency in friendship, and for stability, when her young life is facing more challenges her age should need to carry on her shoulders, is so beautiful to watch. My mother brings joy and laughter that is infectious, and she has this beautiful way of laughing at herself which brightens any room she enters. I know I’m lucky, but I also know it’s hard work, because every time I tell her about people who comment on how lucky I am to have her, she smiles and simply tells me it’s a choice she makes every morning when she gets up, to be the best she can be, and it’s work, it’s a consistent choice. I try to mirror her ability to love during hardship and to never give up. And when I fall asleep at night next to my wonderful little girl, I count myself lucky to have them both in my life, and do my best in becoming for my daughter, what my mother is to me, a rock of love to lean on and to unwaveringly be encouraged to reach any goal and dream I may have. In this week’s newsletter I wrote about portraiture with direct light, and used a series shot with my mother as an example. You can read it via a link in my profile to “The Photography Workshop” newsletter. All previous newsletters are archived there, and you can access them all should you miss it on the day they are sent out. I hope you’ll enjoy it! Happy Norwegian Mother’s Day to all of you. xx

I’m absolutely thrilled to announce after so many emails and messages from you about a food photography workshop here in the English countryside. Join us this May the 13-15th for a fully packet two day food photography workshop based at my dear friends at @ash_farm_dorset with individual accommodation in shepherds huts and small cabins, you wake up with sweeping views of green rolling hills in the heart of the English countryside. Two days of sharing all I know about food photography, where it all began really, how to style and create compelling food stories, with open fire cooking with @flamesandfeasts to local vineyard visits to learn the art of telling visual stories around food, weather you’re starting a journey as a food photographer, want to hone your skills, or learn to photograph for your own website. There’ll be hands on sessions on light, composition, storytelling, the use of props, styling, colour, editing and putting it all together to create complete stories. We only have a limited number available, with only four spots left. If you’re looking to bring a spouse, or you want to share accommodation with a friend please DM me and we’ll set it up for you. Email at marie@mmforsberg, me or DM and I’ll send the details over for you to book your spot. I’m absolutely thrilled to be able to welcome you back to the beautiful part of the world we live in here in Dorset. Come spend two days with us in May. xx

Not long now, the countryside will look like this! And even if a good Sunday roast and a crackling fire in a pub is keeping me warm this winter, I’m not going to lie, I’m so looking forward to Spring I would happily fast forward a couple of months if i could. But mind you the garden still needs doing so perhaps I need the time to get everything in order for spring to finally arrive with great gusto. I couldn’t be happier about your feedback on my recent “The Photography Workshop” Newsletter on camera settings and the F-stop. Depth of field or the F-Stop is my paintbrush when I photograph, it’s how I create milky landscape images and softer edged portraits and food images, but I wasn’t prepared for how many of you that would find it interesting and useful too! Thank you for all your lovely messages. Now, next up is photographing children, a topic close to my heart and one that I think will be useful for photographing anyone, portraits of old and young alike. Consider it part two in the how-to-shoot portraits series. But that’s next up, for now you can read my latest on the F Stop or depth of field by clicking on the link in my profile. And remember, soon, the landscape will yet again be draped in the brightest of green and life will feel rather wonderful. xx

It’s that kind of day where the clouds hang low on the horizon and the chance of sun is less likely than finding a pair of socks after they have entered the washing machine. The sky is a giant light box, and if I was in my studio today it would’ve given me that soft milky light that I so often yearn for when creating my stillifes. There’s something about a bit of gentle light descending on a little set up of flowers or a handful of fruit from the local market. I remember this day well, getting up early and walking through a sleepy southern town in Italy to the food market. I filled my basket and returned back to where we were staying eager to begin creating. All I needed was a sliver of light descending over the scene like the caress of a feather, and so I cracked the big old oak door to a room without any windows, and let my stillife be illuminated by that slight ray of warm Italian light. There’s magic in every type of light, it’s all about using it to your advantage and learn to see what it can help create for you. Harsh contrasty midday sunshine holds just as much magic in it as a sliver of soft lighting on a cloudy day. It’s all about working with what you’ve got and all my stillifes are created in very different light situations and locations, from caves in the south of Italy, to wonky old sheds with no window in the English countryside, to my sitting room bookshelves and on top of the nightstand in my cottage bedroom. A stormy day can offer up such wild and beautiful light, but so can a summers day at noon when the sun is in zenith. On my recent photography workshop in Florence we began the first day with the pursuit of light, learning to discover and recognise the power of natural light throughout the city, from artists studios, to alleyways, big old palazzo door openings and the incredible light reflecting off of the river Arno on a sunny day and big marble sculptures and surfaces. Light is truly where it all begins and ends for me in photography, and the more you hone your eye, the more you begin to see opportunities around every bend, like spotting your favourite colour everywhere. You can view my limited edition stillifes for sale on my website. xx

In Florence, a couple of weeks ago, I enjoyed a week of Pitti, men’s fashion week, client work and catching up with friends, but also, to set up for my next fully immersive photography workshop in Florence on the 23-24th of March. Spring will be in the air, and I cannot wait to welcome some of you to an intimate and fully packed weekend of photography. On these smaller grouped workshops, only five participants, I share everything I know from light, composition, visual storytelling, settings, clients work, building a portfolio, fees, specks, books, editorial work, and editing. Because the group is so small, I’ll be able to meet you where you are on your photography journey, from complete beginners, to professionals that want to shake things up, after years in the industry. These workshops have become my favourite kind, and the photography mentoring continues on after we all go home on our last day, should you wish. Pop over to my website for more information. Should you want a private course in Florence, with a one on one bespoke workshop tailored to your needs, I have availability between the 25th of March to the 15th of April. Just pop me a message, and we can take it from there. I’m so looking forward to this year with workshops, client work that make me stretch, and to shape my weekly “The Photography Workshop” newsletter into something more complete. Like a friend reminded me a few days ago, this year has eleven more months of opportunities that we can fill with anything we want! And even if I haven’t written down any New Year’s resolutions other than continuing what I promised myself I’d work on last year, I’ve made one big commitment to myself this year, to only fill these next months with uplifting people who have values and and principles in life, and lead a life, that inspire me to do better, and to be better, and to always find time to be there for whoever may need it. Eleven months of opportunities ahead of us, to create the life we want, and to be the change we want to see in the world. Head over to my profile for more information about my group, and private, photography workshops. Or send me a message, and I’ll pop you some more information. xx

I may be finishing up my next newsletter post on camera settings, but I’ve had the use of colour on my mind for a while now. I’m adding new features to my expanding “The Photography Workshop” newsletter, my new weekly online photography classroom of sorts, and I was wondering how you felt about bringing in a podcast as a monthly addition? Would you rather read or listen to a newsletter? Or perhaps both? I’d so love to know. I want my photography newsletter to be able to serve you better and feel rich in relevance, but also filled with unexpected way for you to learn about the use of colour, light, storytelling, etc from people I admire in the creative industry who might have a completely different approach than a photographer would. On my workshops, next up in Florence, these are elements I try to bring in, and so I’d love to try to do the same for my newsletters. If you’ve been reading them I’d love your feedback below, or send me a message. So much to share with you in upcoming newsletters, but for now, next up is on the F Stop, or depth or field so make you’re subscribed via the link in my profile, but don’t worry about missing a newsletter, as it will all be saved in the archive which you can access at any time. This photograph is from Ireland from @ballyvolanehouse and I just adore the rich use of colour and the slightly wonky and loved in nature of it all, just the way a home should be, filled with joy, colour, and a bit of imperfection and love. Hope you’re all having a wonderful weekend, it’s all sunshine here in the countryside. xx

RECETTE 🍪 

Cookies IG bas

Ingrédients secs :
👩‍🍳190g de poudre d’amandes
👩‍🍳1 càs de bicarbonate alimentaire 
👩‍🍳Une pincée de fleur de sel 
👩‍🍳120g de bon chocolat noir coupé en grosses pépites 
Ingrédients humides :
👩‍🍳2 càs d’huile de coco solide et juste ramollie, désodorisée 
👩‍🍳Quelques gouttes d’extrait de vanille 
👩‍🍳1 gros œuf
👩‍🍳2 càs de sirop d’agave

👩‍🍳Préchauffer le four à 190°C, mode chaleur tournante si possible.
👩‍🍳Couper au couteau les pépites de chocolat, afin.
👩‍🍳Dans un grand saladier, mélanger les ingrédients humides : battre énergiquement l’huile de coco ramollie avec le sirop d’agave au fouet. Ajouter l’oeuf, la vanille et fouetter bien.
👩‍🍳Dans un autre saladier, mélanger les ingrédients secs à la cuillère : poudre d’amandes et bicarbonate puis les 120g de pépites de chocolat et le sel.
👩‍🍳Verser les ingrédients secs sur les ingrédients humides et mélanger rapidement avec une cuillère à soupe ou une maryse, sans trop insister.
👩‍🍳Sur une plaque recouverte de papier sulfurisé, disposer des petites boules de pâte en les espaçant bien. 
👩‍🍳Enfourner pour 7 à 8 minutes à 190°C (selon la taille des cookies et le four). Pour moi, 7 minutes dans le four préchauffé pour 10 cookies. 

Bonne régalade 😋

CHANDELEUR 🥞

Crêpes IG bas

Ingrédients
🥞 150 g de farine intégrale de petit épeautre
🥞 300 g de lait d’avoine
🥞 2 œufs

Préparation
🥞 Dans un saladier, battez les œufs en omelette.
🥞 Délayez en versant 1/3 du lait.
🥞 Versez la farine dans le saladier et mélangez bien pour l’incorporer au mélange.
🥞 Ajouter progressivement le reste du lait, en fouettant bien avec la cuillère pour éviter les grumeaux.
🥞 Laissez reposer 30 minutes. 
🥞 Faites chauffer une poêle antiadhésive avec un peu d’huile de coco.
🥞 A l’aide d’une louche versez la pâte et répartissez dans la poêle. Faîtes cuire les crêpes de chaque côté quelques minutes.

Bonne régalade 😋

PETITE GOURMANDISE 😋

Macaron chocolat 
👩‍🍳150 g de sucre glace
👩‍🍳90 g de poudre d’amande
👩‍🍳15 g de cacao en poudre
👩‍🍳2 blancs d’oeufs moyens ou 3 petits (75 g en tout)
👩‍🍳10 g de sucre (glace ou normal)
👩‍🍳100 g de chocolat noir à pâtisser
👩‍🍳10 cl de crème liquide
👩‍🍳20 g de beurre

👩‍🍳Tamisez plusieurs fois le sucre, le cacao et la poudre d’amande pour obtenir un mélange très fin.
👩‍🍳Montez les blancs en neige très ferme. Lorsqu’ils commencent à être fermes, ajouter le sucre glace (les 10 grammes), en 2 fois.
👩‍🍳Ajoutez les blancs à la poudre (cacao/amande/sucre) et mélangez pour obtenir une pâte lisse, brillante.
👩‍🍳A l’aide d’une poche à douille, réalisez des petits cercles sur une feuille de papier sulfurisé ou une plaque de silicone.
👩‍🍳Laissez “pocher” à l’air libre 20 minutes.
👩‍🍳Préchauffez le four a 150°C.
👩‍🍳Enfournez les macarons 20 minutes (15 min si ce sont des petits macarons).
👩‍🍳Réalisez la ganache en faisant chauffer la crème et en la versant sur le chocolat en morceaux. Mixer, puis rajouter le beurre, mixer à nouveau et réserver au frais.
👩‍🍳Sortez les macarons, laissez-les refroidir quelques minutes, décollez-les et garnissez-les.

2024年1月8日まるはお空組に進級しましたよ〜
パパとママはすっごく心配してたけどやっと納得してくれたみたい☺️ジョン兄やココアちゃん、シューズくんも待ってるから大丈夫なんだけどな〜。あとお水のおじちゃんもいるから喉が渇いても大丈夫😆だから皆んなも心配しないで！まるはみんなが笑ってくれてこそ元気になるんだから。
それにしても16年って結構短いようで長かったな〜
日本全国色んな場所に連れて行ってもらったし、美味しいものも沢山食べたよね。何よりも、まるは世界中の沢山のお友達と仲良しになれた事は本当に嬉しかったよ。16年という時間はまるにとって宝物のような時間で、お空組に進級するに為のお勉強もバッチリ出来ました！
だから皆んな泣かないでね。まるとの思い出をコメントしてくれたら嬉しいな。お空組でゆっくり読ませてもらうね。
胸を張って行ってきます！バイバーイ

追伸　パパがしょぼくれてたらまるの代わりにドロップキックお見舞いしちゃってね。あと、お彼岸には戻ってくるからね！お肉の煙を目標に帰ってくるよ〜

Maru has been promoted to the Sky Team as of January 8, 2024! Mom and Dad were really worried, but it seems they've finally come to terms with it. Big brother John, Cocoa-chan, and Shoes-kun are waiting too, so it's all good. And there's also the water uncle, so no worries about getting thirsty 😆 So everyone, don't worry! Maru gets energized when everyone is smiling.

But really, 16 years felt both short and long. I was taken to various places all over Japan and ate a lot of delicious food. More than anything, I'm truly happy to have become friends with so many people around the world. These 16 years have been like a treasure for me, and I've studied hard to be promoted to the Sky Team!

So everyone, please don't cry. I would be happy if you could share your memories with Maru in the comments. I'll take my time reading them in the Sky Team. I'm going with my head held high! Bye-bye!

P.S. If Dad is looking down, give him a dropkick on my behalf, okay? Also, I'll be back for Ohigan, guided by the smoke of the meat!

A group of southern right whales draw closer to a tiny @mitty off the shores of Western Australia. Said to be called right whales for being the “right whale to hunt,” these gentle giants were once heavily targeted by the whaling industry. Their high fat and oil content, coupled with their tendency to stay close to shore, move slowly, and float after being harpooned, tragically made them the ideal victim for whalers. Since the global moratorium on whaling was officially established in the 1980s, their populations have slowly started to recover. As long as we continue to protect key calving and breeding grounds, mothers can raise their newborns in peace. We are very proud and grateful to work with our @sealegacy team to help ensure their future.

Tucked against the rocky coast, mother southern right whales find solace off of Western Australia. The more spaces they have to nurture their calves in peace, the more their species can recover.

Part of my upcoming story on Zoroastrianism, the oldest monotheistic religion in the world, for @natgeo. Mehernosh, a pallbearer - the person in charge of carrying the dead body at a funeral - walks away from one of the two functioning towers of silence in Karachi.
A tower of silence, known as dakhma, is a circular structure built by Zoroastrians for excarnation - that means the exposure of human corpses to the elements for decomposition - in order to avoid contamination of the soil and other natural elements by the decomposing dead bodies. Carrion birds, usually vultures (though no longer in Karachi…) and other scavengers, consume the flesh. Skeletal remains are gathered into a central pit where further weathering and continued breakdown occurs. In this dakhma, reflective mirrors have been fitted inside the tower of silence to increase the heat and help the body decomposing faster.
Karachi, a city of 20 millions, has 800 Zoroastrians known as Parsees, 70% of them are above the age of 70 years old. #zoroastrianism #zoroastrian #towerofsilence #towersofsilence #parsi #parsee

I was in the dust with the wrestlers and I looked up and realised that a crowd had formed, a sea of shalwar kamiz. All these men (and 1 woman!! Can you spot her??) had gathered on the edge of a pilgrimage site to watch a spontaneous wrestling match - called Koshti or Malakhro in Baloch. With laughter and agitation, some theatre, it’s the ancestral raw version of the WWF stuff you might have unfortunately seen on TV. Pakistan, Baluchistan province.

I was in Karachi last March, city of 20 million, I love it there. On my pilgrimage in Baluchistan, I met a man who called himself Samundar Baba (Ocean Baba) - he owned boats. Unusual character, long beard and serious looking type, a big hashish smoker. He lived in Lyari, considered a dodgy area although I didn’t think so. I reached out and we met in his house. I was interested in this world of men you can find on fishing boats. So I asked him to bring me. This is the Korangi fishing harbor, one of the largest one in south asia. It can be complicated to photograph there because of authorisation and army nearby. Samundar kindly got me in and I spent a few hours jumping boats as the sun got low.

The original ravers were just getting started. Fun and mad times with the passionate Ishk Ali and his buddies, like Daula Sain. It was day 2 of our 12 days pilgrimage journey, walking together across Sindh and Baluchistan. That is a double cigarette and a sacrificial goat. Pakistan.

2023 is gone, just a number! It’s been a year filled with travels in Pakistan, Uzbekistan, Spain, Azerbaijan, Canada, Tajikistan, India etc…
It was interesting to meander through life between being a photographer, a farmer and be present for the family.
I thought of god a bit, all triggered by a story on Zoroastrianism for National Geographic magazine (coming up). How and why do we often inherit the feeling of being watched by God, god like a massive cctv system… religion the opium of the people?
Probably god is busy with a lot more than watching you… Is your god a vengeful one or a god that you will live with and whose law you must respect, like gravity? Lots of fun questions with no real need for answers..

Here is a serene scene, mixing all religious influences (at least to my eye!), in a place that has seen Animism, Buddhism, Zoroastrianism and more recently Islam (ismaili faith). It’s in an “ostone”, a shrine in Tajikistan’s Wakhan corridor, adorned with ibex and Marco Polo horns - and a triangle of stones for the “shirogh” (the candle of cotton dipped in oil), lit for special occasion (for Jumarat, Eid or for Didor, the birthday of the Aga Khan etc). Azom Khon, the caretaker, is praying for me before I leave. It was beautiful so I pulled back and took a picture.

I will be sharing pictures here from my recent travels until I leave for SE Asia on February 20th.
Love and light for 2024.

Se llama Elena Ortega, nació en Castellón hace 49 años y tiene un gusto innegable no solo para la fotografía, también para ver la belleza donde otros solo ven frío. Ni el cambio climático, ni temperaturas más propias del verano en el mes de abril, ni el aumento de las noches tropicales anuales en España ni la sequía cada vez más profunda son capaces de cambiarnos el chip. Tenemos que aprender que el buen tiempo, a principio de los 20 del siglo XXI, se compone de nubes, de sombra, de brisa y, por supuesto, de lluvia. Tal vez por eso ella, Elena, fue una visionaria y decidió adoptar en ocasiones el pseudónimo de @misswinter (señora invierno), como carta de presentación de su preciosa forma de mirar. Ahora ya la siguen más 467.000 personas en Instagram.

I was surprised how many people responded to what I wrote yesterday and glad to know people found comfort in my thoughts. 🙏 Often this feeling of being “lost” comes from a larger cultural context. I just got back from Bhutan, a place where life feels integrated, whole, directed. About 7 years ago, I chose to live in multiple places around the world; I consider myself a member of various communities. The differences are striking. One of my favorite homes is Hawaii. 🏝Tomorrow I’m going there.🤙Part of why I love Hawaii and why it feels like home to me is similar to the feeling I get in Bhutan. There’s an attitude of calm in Hawaii. You see it in everything, from the speed of traffic, to the gait with which people walk. 👣In part, it’s island life, but it runs deeper than geography. It’s cultural and philosophical. When your community is strong, your purpose in life feels more secure. 💕The state of Hawaii is ranked lowest in the US for depression. 😀It’s fifth lowest for separation and divorce. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Is this all because of sunny weather and beautiful beaches? I don’t think so. It helps, but that’s not the whole story. There’s a saying or hashtag you may have seen on Instagram #luckywelivehawaii To me, that simple idea reflects pride, gratitude, and wisdom, all in one concept: pride in heritage and traditions, gratitude for that heritage to exist and continue, and wisdom of those living in Hawaii to recognize the uniqueness that their heritage does exist and continue. 🌏😎When you exist in a community like that, you’re less likely to suffer as an individual. If you’re struggling on a personal level, sometimes the answer may lie outside yourself—in a community that’s waiting for you. Aloha :) 🏄‍♂️

Lately I’ve been meeting a lot of “lost” people that seem to suffer from a crisis of confidence. I’m trying to help where I can. You don’t always have to understand the path forward. It’s OK to be lost at times. Crisis begets growth. In fact, some research shows that crisis is one of the few things that can really change us after age 25. If you’re feeling this way, just know that things can change in a moment — a chance occurrence can change your life forever. In the meantime, fill your brain with good ideas, follow the signs that life is sending to you, be open to what’s possible. If you’re doing OK in life right now, give your smile and empathy to strangers and friends. We never know what someone is going through.  What does all this have to do with this photo? Haha well, I suppose this photo gives me a feeling of hope and a reminder that life, despite its conflicts, is always a beautiful thing. 😀🌎📷🤙

Rinpung Monastery, Paro, Bhutan. A “dzong” is the word they use  in Bhutan for a fortress/monastery. These beautiful structures with giant walls reveal a lot about Bhutan’s unique culture. First, it is a defensible fortress--a holdover from days when wars were still happening. You can’t see from the picture I took here, but the walls descend further, so there’s no way for attackers to climb up or get inside. There’s tiny slits  around the Dzong where people inside can shoot arrows at attackers on the outside! 🏹I’ve seen 10 fortresses like this in throughout Bhutan, and they’re usually built on a hillside with a strategic view of the valley, and, if the view isn’t so great, there’s a secondary watchtower in a better position. But what are they defending? I am just learning, but there’s a unique confluence of activity inside each Dzong: besides a military fortress, today, Dzong’s are homes for monks, and a spiritual center, but they also house all kinds of offices—think of it like the combination church, DMV, a civil court, an architecture planning office, and anything else related to the city’s administration. It shows how there is a lack of separation between “church and state”… In Bhutan, their philosophical and “religious” beliefs (some say Buddhism is not a religion, but a philosophical perspective), are integrated with the government, not separated. 🎊More Bhutanese are beginning to dress like Westerners, but when you visit the Dzong, you are required to where the traditional dress of the Bhutanese people. To foreign eyes, it makes for a colorful and exciting experience—you feel like you’re in the 16th century watching the activity inside, even though people might be there to get architectural plans approved, or to get a divorce, or something else that seems very “modern” to us. Ah yes, and the chilis… I had to include the chilis drying in the sun. Bhutanese add chilis to almost every dish (even in their rice); certainly there will be chilis in every meal! The chilis are dried outside, typically on the roof of homes. 🏠 Drying can take a month! ☀️I think I’ll be adding chilis to dishes when i get back home! 😀

Tiger’s Nest, Bhutan. 🇧🇹 When I first told people I was planning a trip to Bhutan, very few knew what I was talking about. 🤔Where? What? For those that did know Bhutan, it was always for one of two things: 1) the pleasant idea that the government and King make policy decisions based on the principles of “Gross National Happiness” and 2) the Himalayan Buddhist temple, Tiger’s Nest which I’ve posted here. I’d seen photos of Tiger’s Nest for many years, but photos do not give you a sense of just how high up it is! 🌄📷 I’d had the impression that Tiger’s Nest was perched just above a city, and that you could look up and see it from a town below, sort of like the Potala Palace in Lhasa. That’s not the case - not even close! You’ll probably never see a photo of Tiger’s Nest from the valley floor on Instagram because it would be so boring—in a photo taken from the bottom, Tiger’s Nest would be just a tiny speck on the mountain side. 🗻For Americans or anyone who has been to Yosemite, imagine you’re standing on the valley floor and looking at the very tops of the highest rock surfaces and you see a small speck that *might* be manmade. That’s the best way I could relate to you how high up this special Bhutanese monastery is.  To visit the viewpoint from where I took this photo, you start at a forested valley floor, and hike up several hours. 🚶🏻🏃🏻‍♀️There’s no rock climbing involved, and its only steep in a few places, but the sheer length of the trek makes the existence of this place that much more remarkable. It’s not just its beauty and the seemingly impossible engineering that gives you a sense of awe,  it’s also the idea that every piece of wood, stone, every relic and jewel housed inside, was carried up one by one. 💪 Pro Tip: If you decided to visit yourself, start your journey before dawn, or in the afternoon, and you’re likely to have the viewpoint all to yourself. We did :) !! We were there so late, we came down in total darkness. Remember your flashlights.

We can apply it to so many things…asking for help as a parent, going after what you want in your career or diving deeper in your relationship. Taking that step to move forward and get out of a rut… the list can go and on. I think we’ve all have had trouble with doing one or all of these things at some point in our lives.
✨
With each step forward or heck, within any moment of self doubt, I find myself reflecting on the last year, or five years or ten years and realizing how much growth I’ve experienced as an individual. It can be hard for many of us to see it at times, but if we look, it’s there. 

Rob and I were just talking about this the other night after we put our 3 year old to bed. 3 year old?! Wait…almost 4 year old…what?!? We’re coming up on 10 years of marriage and never did we think we’d be in Arizona with a toddler, build a house or have traveled to all the places we have. None of this was the plan ten years ago sitting on a beach during our honeymoon. There never really was a plan, but every step we took, it felt like a step towards a more authentic self. A step towards a happier, more flexible life, creating space to explore and love and learn and stumble unapologetically. We created that space for ourselves together as a couple and still continue to grow and learn. Now we get to create that as parents together for a special little human who makes us feel more than we ever thought we could. 
🧡
This is turning into a novel and I’m writing this out at night (to post in the morning) which is probably why i feel all the feels…but all this to say, I love these words and I think it’s the encouragement we need to remind ourselves and our loved ones to go after what we want …create the type of life that brings our souls that much closer to feeling full. 🙌

Simplicity, slowing down and creating intimate moments at home. Looking back it’s the quieter days that hold the most special memories with my family vs the big parties or grand trips. 

Many of us have our days filled with appointments, time to get from here to there, pick up this and that… we end up yearning for those slower moments but then are also programmed to think and feel it’s “boring” if we’re not constantly on the move. 🤔 

Why not make those times at home beautiful? Turn ordinary moments into extraordinary…just by switching our mind set…just by looking a little deeper and enjoying the beauty in the simplicity. 

I remember one summer as a kid, the AC went out for a good portion of the season. It was hot and humid (back east where I grew up.) My mom hung pretty sheets in the hallway to direct the airflow of the portable fan we had plugged in. My sisters and I gathered around with snacks and movies. I still remember the shadows dancing in our room, as we lowered the curtains to keep the heat from the sun out a bit. It felt magical and special, even though yes, we were hot…but we weren’t  focused on that at the time…

It’s easy to romanticize everyday moments if we let ourselves see things that way….a little more childlike, find some beauty and magic in it all…

Almost 11 weeks post explant and here is what I’ve learned about myself:

💗 I put them in at age 19 bc I didn’t feel good  about myself. I was self conscious THEN about being “flat” and that has not gone away. I had implants for 33 years and being a double DD became part of my identity. It feels stupid to admit that now but is true. Removing them has been more than a health thing. It’s been a deep dive into my own psychology and looking at why I felt I “needed them”

💗 I feel stronger than ever. PHYSICALLY. I’m grateful to have learned about the rupture as it’s amazing how many things in my body have normalized since they are out. My body is happier without them 

💗When I first removed them, I ordered a bunch of padded sports bras and bras.I wear NONE of the padded things now. I’m embracing the flat. I don’t care if “others” think it looks better not to- I’m done pretending to be something I’m not in my body.  I’m not even an A cup and it’s my way of apologizing to 19 year old me. I’m going to love and accept her  now the way she is.

💗I do notice big boooobs everywhere now. And YES I mourn mine some days. But more often than not, I’m grateful to have removed them and am embracing my new body. I do not regret explanting.

💗 It was not just the explant that healed me. I’ve done a LOT of deep gut work this last year and left a house that was covered with mold. So it was a combination. 

💗I used to think people that talked about BII were cray cray- now I think I was the crazy one. Why did I dismiss the possibility that implants could be harming me for so long 🙈 sooooo many people tried to tell me. I used to get triggered by that. 

💗 Alllllll my inflammation is GONE. So is my pain, my excess weight, my energy dips. I’m back to my familiar self.

Anyways- Hadn’t shared about my post explant thoughts in a while so thought I would!

Cada día se reinicia un año.

No se si será la mejor fotografía de los últimos 365 días, pero tengo claro es lo mucho que disfruté bajo la nieve ese día.
Hace un par de días pensaba en todas las personas que desde principios de año han estado luchando, luchando por sobrevivir, por mantener su puesto de trabajo, por nuestra salud, por estar alegres, por seguir aquí...
Todos somos luchadores en algún sentido, incluso cuando las cosas van mal.
A esos luchadores que no descansan nunca, GRACIAS, gracias una vez más.

Si tuviera que resumir mi año, os podría contar cientos, algunas de ellas tristes, otras llenas de felicidad, pero todas ellas tienen algo en común, y es algo tan simple como sonreír.

Sonreír, sonreír a las personas que nos rodean, las conozcamos o no, sonreírle a la vida, sonreír ante los problemas que nos parecen imposibles de solucionar.
Es solo un gesto que con la ayuda de la mirada transmite bienestar.

Aunque instagram ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años, para peor en mi parecer. Logra sacar en muchas ocasiones facilitar el crecimiento personal, para bien y para mal, el ego, y sobre todo darle fuerza a la autoestima de los que valoran los likes y la venta de vidas idílicas que os prometo que no existen.

A todos vosotros que habéis llegado hasta el final del escrito, sonrie y vive una vida real.

“conflict in congo is like a babushka (matryoshka) doll....you have conflicts sitting inside conflicts....it’s about local issues, who controls land, which chief is in power....often linked to ethnicity, because at local level ethnicity is the principle organizer of politics....at the next level, it is national power, partially due to collapse of mobutu and effects of belgian colonialism....but there it is more about using ethnicity to leverage a better position in parliament or a piece of a smuggling racket in gold....then you have the regional power politics, which mainly involves rwanda and that role really began in 1994 with the rwandan genocide....the conflict initially was not about minerals, though they became important over time to fund war efforts, esp for a country like rwanda that is small and poor....but when tantalum shot through the roof, which happened to be at a time of extreme violence, it began to shift incentives of those involved in the conflict and it was no longer about national security....around 2000 the various actors became more invested in minerals....but the war here is really about power and access to power, and that passes through local politicians. so you need to understand the politics” - jason stearns

*note: the above may serve to help understand the “conflict in congo,” the atmosphere inside the country, and is not meant to address the past/current influence of foreign powers “outside”

For those who have lost something this week; an opportunity, a relationship, a belief, a job, faith or motivation...your next season is going to be greater!
-
What no longer serves you will eventually be cut, pruned or trimmed away from your life.
-
This hurts in the moment. That moment can last from minutes to months. And that’s entirely upto you. Own it, experience it, feel it.
-
Then there becomes a time when new life starts growing from the very area of your life that has been removed. New life that holds the promise of new opportunities, new memories, new relationships, new jobs and a renewed faith and motivation.
-
A word for anyone going through this right now...your next season is going to take further than your last one.
-
God never removes unless there is something far greater He has planned for our next season. The pruning is just the first step of new opportunities!
-
Believe in the hope of tomorrow, while you experience whole-heartedly and learn from today.
-
Your next season is going to be greater than your last. Have faith in knowing God will replace.

The way I see it, “Mobility” Is kind of like a collaboration effort between our muscles and joints.
 
When our joint mobility is limited, we might be missing out on opportunities to be stronger, more athletic, and more efficient.
 
The ability to move our joints through their full range helps our muscles work more optimally, and when our muscles can do their work, they can also get stronger and help keep our joints healthy in return.
 
💪🏼Having a good balance between strength and joint mobility helps distribute the stress more evenly through the body instead of overstressing our joints (back, hips, knees, ankles, etc.).
 
🚪Our joints are kind of like the hinges to a door; if that door remains unopened for long periods in addition to environmental decay, the hinges in that door will start creaking and get rusty overtime. In our case, it will be arthritis, bursitis, inflammation, and things like that.
 
So you see, just as with the door example, maintenance and movement were keys to extending the life and function of it, in our case, MAINTENANCE and MOVEMENT are also keys to a BETTER QUALITY OF LIFE.🙌🏼

STAY ACTIVE!💪🏼

Energy levels where on the low with some #Adenomyosis aches and pains in the mix. I wasn’t looking to exhaust myself in a long workout and risk feeling super tired afterwards. So I just moved for a bit, worked on some areas that I wanted to target and moved on with the rest of my day.

At the end I was feeling accomplished and still had energy to do other things the rest of the day. 

The are days I push and days I back down, IS MY BALANCE. As long as I am making positive progress is a win for me. I just try my best to be consistent with it.

Don’t compare your journey with anyone else’s.

This month marks 20 years since one of the most impactful moments of my life when a shark took my arm while on a surfing off the coast of Kauai, my birth place. Many people could look at the incident back in 2003 as a major setback for me, but God had so much in store for the future! 🤙🏼

It’s absolutely wild to think how my life started and where it is now and all the amazing yet challenging things in between. I didn’t wake up in the hospital thinking I was invincible and was gonna get back to surfing. After getting a hint of inspiration,  I had to dream it up, flip my mindset and be willing to do what I had not seen anyone else do.  This was a challenge to live in faith. And I am so glad I was willing to try and give it my best shot! 🙏🏼 Now I get to surf with my two eldest sons Tobias and Wesley and my hubby! I get to enjoy these sweet moments with my newborn daughter. There is so much to be grateful for, and these past 20 years have been filled with incredible moments and huge overcoming seasons. 💛

When you have your “Shark Attack” moments in life. I hope you’re willing to try, and give life your best shot! You too CAN OVERCOME!

Changing your mindset is free. Doesn’t mean it’s an easy or fast fix. It’s up to you to be honest with yourself and start working on it. 
It’s wild to me that some people still think surfing with one arm is not possible. I am a living example and there are soooo many other amazing adaptive athletes and people out there doing incredible things that people perceive as impossible. 
What is it about some who are willing to adapt and make the most of what they’ve got? 
MINDSET. It may take time to switch it up and we may have to be forever workin at it. But I promise you, that you won’t regret continually flipping your mind to be more grateful, more optimistic, more of what and how can can I do this life to the best of my abilities… More of - I don’t need easy I just need possible. 🧠✨💪🏽 Hope this pushes you today and onward to adapt in your life. YOU CAN.

TOMORROW our film INHERITANCE (@inheritance_thefilm) will have a second showing at Slamdance Film Festival in Park City, Utah.

INHERITANCE tells the story of an often overlooked America and a family caught in the grips of intergenerational trauma and addiction. Filmed over 11 years in one Appalachian town the film follows a boy as he grows up from age 12 to 18 surrounded by chaos, addiction and powerful love.

We want the film to fuel conversations, provide space for empathy and break stigmas around substance abuse and mental health.

We are so appreciative to our Editor Curtis Whitear (@curtiswhitear), our Composer Kyle Scott Wilson (@kyle_scott_wilson) and our Executive Producers Morgan Pehme and Daniel DiMauro (@dan__dimauro), Sam Cullman, Erik (@e1heyer) and Leslie Heyer, and Dave A. Liu (@liucrative). 

If you would like to support our film:

JOIN US: at Slamdance! INHERITANCE is in competition for a Grand Jury Award so please come out and support us! 

FOLLOW US: keep apprised of our future showings, sign up for our email list on our website (www.inheritancethefilm.com) and follow us here on Instagram @inheritance_thefilm

SHARE: spread the word and share this post and our mission. Let’s build a more compassionate world, one story at a time

FROM MY ARCHIVE | Monhegan Island Post 05 (final):: I got my start at @natgeo in 1999 as a photo intern when I did my first story for the magazine. I was asked if I had an idea for a project and I proposed Monhegan – a small island 10 miles off the coast of Maine. I am from New England and had lived on the Maine coast as a young adult. I had always been curious about the 2 mile long and ½ mile wide island. In the summers the place overflows with tourists, but the year round population is only about 60-70. The islanders’ de facto fishing territory became the Monhegan Lobster Conservation Area in 1996 with a limited season starting in October. The island’s windswept landscape, quirky community and the dramatic cliffs have inspired artists like Robert Henri, George Bellows, Rockwell Kent, Edward Hopper, Lynn Mapp Drexler and three generations of the Wyeth family to name a few. ⁠
⁠
The community took me in and sometimes chewed me up. My time and experiences there changed and shaped my life in profound and beautiful ways that continue to impact me almost 25 years later; working with photo editor Susan Welchman who took me under her wing and has been my mentor and dear friend since and within days of arriving to the island, I also met one of my best friends @tralice_pooltoyphotos ⁠
⁠

Morning fog lifts off the meadow behind the Josiah Starling house, the oldest house on the island, built in 1784.⁠
⁠
Image 02⁠
The island gardener works on the flower beds around the Island Inn.⁠
⁠
Image 03⁠
Lobsterman Bryan Hitchcock⁠

Tulips in the moonlight⁠

10 years ago today I bought my first camera. 
I was 24 at the time, finishing my second degree in Biotechnologies. 
Didn’t know anything about photography, didn’t have any connection or any real reason to start, out of the simple, uncontrollable need to express myself. 
I started so many things trying to find my way, always ending into dropping the latest idea after some months. 
Photography hit me like a bolt and never left me. 
Of all the things I heard during these 10 years, the most important one that kept pushing me in improving over and over again, was probably this: “you can’t”.
You can’t live with photography, you can don’t it without connections, you can’t work without expensive gear, you can’t make it without a specific degree, you can’t work with this “style”, you can’t do it because you’re not good enough. 
After 10 years at 34 years old, after years of absolute dedication and an insane will to improve still pumping in my veins, I’m living with photography the best life I could have imagined. 
I’m so grateful to all the people that believed in me and helped me trough this process; of course believing in yourself is the most important part, but without all the persons I met, I don’t know if I would have been able to make it trough the hardest times. 
This is just a small selection of some fav pictures shot during these years. 
I didn’t include the FaceTime series, even tho is probably one of the biggest steps for me in terms of improving my vision. 
Thanks to all the people involved, hope we’re gonna be able to meet in person soon again, to create, have fun and keep inspiring each other. 
If you have any question about the making of any particular photo, or the process in general, I’d love to talk about it here in comments.

Adm Elektrik, Aydın Söke’de başlattığı ‘Leyleklere Yeni Yuva’ projesi ile doğal yaşamın sürdürülebilirliğine 14 yıldır destek oluyor. Elektrik direklerine özel platformlar kurarak leyleklere güvenli yuva alanları sağlamak, göç dönemlerinde yuvaları kontrol ederek zararlı maddeleri temizlemek ve elektrik hatlarını yalıtarak leyleklerin güvenliğini sağlamak gibi adımlar atarak, hem doğal dengeyi koruma hem de leyleklerin yaşam alanlarını güvence altına alma konusunda çok değerli bir rol üstlenmişler. 
Boyle  çevre dostu projeler, içimizi ısıtan bir umut ışığı gibi parlıyor. “Leyleklere Yeni Yuva” gibi projeler, yalnızca doğal yaşamı değil, dünyamızın daha yaşanabilir olacağına dair  umutları da besliyor 

Projeyi yerinde görebilmek için Söke’de çok güzel bir tarihi Rum köyü olan Doğanbey’i ve Ayşar Köyü’nü ziyaret ettik. Avşar Köyü’nde evine misafir olduğumuz Meryem Nine’nin kurtardığı Efe Leylek’le olan hikayesi ve doğa sevgisi yüreğimize bir başka dokundu. La sala “el Molino” es hoy, un café-concierto y sala de fiestas. Pero su historia comienza en 1898, cuando el propietario de la tasca La Pajarera, un modesto barracón situado en la calle Vila Vilà esquina Rosal, harto de marineros borrachos y de albañiles escandalosos, vende su negocio por 100 pesetas.⠀⠀
·⠀⠀
·⠀⠀
El nuevo propietario, un andaluz llegado a Barcelona para hacer fortuna, le cambia el nombre por el de La Pajarera Catalana y monta un pequeño tablado. Al cabo de tres años ya ofrece una programación musical estable, restaurante a la carta e incluso un servicio gratuito de coches para facilitar el trayecto desde las Ramblas al local.⠀⠀

As a traveler it can be hard to tell whether or not an attraction or activity is harmful to any animals, or we may be too caught up in the excitement of the experience to recognize the reality of what indeed is happening. 

Here are a few things you can ask yourself to avoid cruel attractions: 
1) Are the wild animals kept in cages that do not have all of the following: food, clean water, shelter, ample space, privacy and enrichment?
2) Are animals forced to perform tricks in shows?
3) Are you able to ride, touch, hold, walk or swim with wild animals? 
4) Does the tourist attraction sell parts of products from wild animals? 
5) Does the tour company chase or lure wild animals closer with food or bring people too close to wild animals so they can see them better?

 If you answered yes to any of these, it is not an animal-friendly attraction. Also if the attraction claims to have rescued the wild animals under their care, you can use @worldanimalprotectioncanada’s checklist, to determine if it is a genuine sanctuary.

A couple of points pulled from the checklist are:
1) Does not take animals from the wild (unless they are injured) or breed animals 
2) Does not keep wild animals to make a profit
3) Keeps animals in enclosures that closely resemble their natural habitat and give them enough space and opportunities to move and behave naturally
4) Have veterinarians available at any hour to treat the animals that become sick or hurt. 

 I have linked the checklist in my bio, along with in my stories if you’re wanting to read more. 

You can join the movement by following @worldanimalprotectioncanada, and by sharing this message, which will help us keep wildlife in the wild and end cruel wildlife entertainment’ ✨

Kenya is establishing a vital breeding population of 21 EASTERN BLACK RHINOS rhinos at @Loisaba_Conservancy in Laikipia, Kenya, where they have been absent for the past half-century. Moving a black rhino, an animal weighing over a ton, is a Herculean challenge fraught with danger at every turn. It begins with the risky task of sedating the massive creature, a procedure that requires precision and caution to ensure both the rhino’s safety and that of the vets and handlers. Once subdued, the real test begins as the sedated rhino must be carefully revived and maneuvered into a sturdy crate, a task made all the more daunting by the animal’s immense size and strength. Every step of this delicate operation underscores the inherent risks involved. Watch the sheer force of these creatures and imagine doing it over 21 times over the course of 2 weeks. The teams from @kenyawildlifeservice executed the operation with unparalleled expertise and dedication. In an ideal world, we wouldn’t have to go through these extreme measures but with approximately 80% of the world’s remaining eastern black rhinos under its protection, Kenya’s efforts offer a glimmer of hope for the future of these magnificent creatures.

I am humbled to share another remarkable conservation story from Kenya: the resurgence of eastern black rhinos from the brink of extinction. In a pivotal moment, Kenya is reclaiming its role as a haven for these creatures, establishing a vital breeding population at @Loisaba_Conservancy in Laikipia, Kenya, where they have been absent for the past half-century mainly due to poaching and long ago,  trophy hunting. This first image shows the moment a rhino was resuscitated after it stopped breathing and quickly released. The arduous tasks of tracking, darting, and relocating 21 of these critically endangered giants, each weighing over a ton, posed formidable challenges, yet the teams from @kenyawildlifeservice executed the operation with unparalleled expertise and dedication. Their efforts offer a glimmer of hope for the future of these magnificent creatures. The final image shows the skull of the last rhino poached in the 1970s resting beneath a celestial canopy, symbolizing this hopeful shift as Kenya now stands  as a nation that is expanding habitat and bolstering rhino populations. With approximately 80% of the world's remaining eastern black rhinos under its protection, Kenya is safeguarding endangered populations for future generations.

An international team of scientists and conservationists achieved a groundbreaking milestone in their mission to save northern white rhinos from extinction. They successfully conducted an in vitro embryo transplant in a southern white rhino, resulting in a pregnancy—a crucial proof of concept. However, the joy was short-lived as unforeseen tragedy struck due to heavy rainfall and flooding, unearthing Clostridia bacteria spores and leading to a devastating infection that claimed both the mother, Curra, and the 70 day old fetus.

Despite this profound loss, the team remains determined, having worked tirelessly for years to create 30 embryos with Avantea lab. This awe-inspiring creature was a 70-day-old rhinoceros fetus, an embodiment of perfection in its miniature form. While a typical southern white rhino can tip the scales between 3,080 and 7,920 pounds and 11-15 feet, this little one only reached a delicate 6.4 inches. His life was cut short when his surrogate mother, Curra, a southern white rhino, succumbed to an unforeseen tragedy triggered by heavy rainfall and flooding that unearthed Clostridia bacteria spores, leading to a swift and devastating infection.

The news of Curra's demise struck the team with profound grief. These dedicated individuals have been tirelessly working for years to rescue the northern white rhinos from the brink of extinction. Their journey brought them to Kenya, where they were on the verge of confirming the success of creating the world's first rhino pregnancy through embryo transfer at the Ol Pejeta Conservancy. In a bittersweet twist of fate, the entire team received word of the successful pregnancy by implantation of an embryo using in vitro fertilization (IVF). However, this moment of joy was tinged with the somber acknowledgment of the journey's cost. The next pivotal step is to transfer northern white rhino embryos into a surrogate mother.

I'll be sharing more of this extraordinary story in the coming weeks.  Stay connected with the @biorescue_project, @safariparkdvurkralove, @leibnizizw, @olpejeta, #avantea, and @kenyawildlifeservice for more insights into this pivotal moment for northern white rhinos.

I type this 1st log entry from Barcelona - ~ 2.000 Km into our 8.000 #iberitron road trip

Short summary how things went down till now:
* Austria is HPC heaven - except in Villach (see the drama in @audidriven story iberitron 02)
* Italy is getting better - although after our 3rd visit to @ionity.official Portogruaro - this location is definitely a dump (stinking trash containers next to the chargers, littering, not appealing at all
* @ionity.official France has a serious problem (1st station 4 stalls: 1 of 4 working = 1 broken - where I parked 1st, 2nd working - where I reparked, 3&4 only charging with ~35kW / 2nd station 6 stalls: 2 out of six delivered the full speed (150kW for the e-tron), the other ~35kW. Again lucky as I got the 2nd working one after reparking) Got lucky
* Spain 🇪🇸 - a little to early to tell but was already pleasantly surprised, as proven by this picture. In the middle of nowhere - Figueres - I found this working (!) HPC charger. Biggest challenge was to get the operator app working as it does not accept any of the charging cards

Жемчуг является одним из основных декоративных элементов в коллекции, он ассоциируется со светлым образом Царевны и, конечно, с русским кодом. Из него выполнены аксессуары – сумки, украшения, лифы, оплечья и целое платье.

Многообразие образов сказки Пушкина в коллекции тяготеет к двум полюсам: женское начало, которое воплощает Людмила, проявляется в палитре светлых оттенков в сочетании с россыпями жемчуга в декоре и принтах, а мужское – Руслан и Черномор – в брутальных вещах из кожи и денима и четких структурах.
 
 
The diversity of fairy tale characters in the collection gravitates towards two poles: the feminine principle embodied by Ludmila is manifested in a palette of light shades combined with a scattering of pearls in decor and prints, whereas the masculine - Ruslan and Chernomor - is represented in rugged leather and denim items and clear structures.

Angkor Wat and park in Siem Reap, Cambodia. This is my second time here and it still feels as mystical as the first time. At the beginning of our tour, our guide overwhelmed us with all the mathematical calculations and engineering ingenuity that went into building Angkor Wat. Certain points of the structure lined up perfectly with the Draco Constellation and the sun positioning at sunset. Although there are educated speculation from experts archeologists saying this dates back about 900 years ago, It’s all a mystery.

On the other hand, Spiritual channelers have mentioned this to be older than 5000 BC. It’s a place to activate the pineal gland (third eye) through frequencies, it’s also an informational point for earth to funnel data to and from other planets/galaxies. It’s like another access point of information like the great pyramids. The art carvings hold a lot of relations to Hinduism on many of the Angkor Park structures. But personally, I see a lot of psychedelic reflections on some of the temples. They almost look like what I see as the crossover realm between the mind and other outer dimensions. It’s like the level where you have to overcome the ego before connecting with your higher self. Very interesting place to walk around and wander off into. 

#southeastasia #cambodia #angkorwat #spiritualjourney

Make sure to save this info if you’re thinking about visiting Vietnam. We’re in Ben Tre, Vietnam and this has got to be one of the most underrated places we’ve learned about. I hope people keep going to Bali and leave this place for us 😆

This town is 2 hrs south of Saigon - which around $40 Grab ride.  The town itself is pretty developed as in roads and sidewalks, but this is where you can relax from the crazy traffic and roads of Saigon. I think Ben Tre fits the criteria of what many people think of Saigon. It’s a growing city, with no crazy developments, or high rise.  Many restaurants or stores here cater to the locals, so you will get more of an authentic experience. The locals are pretty friendly as long as you are respectful. The kids like to say “hello” to my bf because they want to use their English. They get a good chuckle when he says “hi” in Vietnamese. We usually greet and thanks in the language of the country we’re in, many folks seem to appreciate it.  The young locals speak English well, older people usually don’t. 

We did 3 tours here with @mrbikerbentreboattour , Troy found him on TripAdvisor. We highly recommend his tours. After doing our first private boat tour, we came back for another tour of the town, and then rented bikes from one of the eco lodges/homestays. @mrbikerbentreboattour has been extremely punctual and helpful with us. His tours gives you a sample of the local lifestyle and Vietnamese tradition. We’ve got to visit the small canals off the Mekong river, and private roads of the locals. We did not experienced any upsell, pressure to buy, or nonsense stops on the tours. It felt more educational and you can see the aunties and uncles on his team working diligently to make a good impression for us. We really appreciated our stay here. It’s so walkable around and the local people love coming out after the sun set but that’s when we are asleep 😴 #travelvietnam #bếntre

Ben Tre, Vietnam

Last year, I was in total hermit mode. I was so eager to build my homestead, I couldn’t focus on anything else. I think that is why I am walking everywhere I possibly can in Vietnam. However, today is a biking day! We rented some bikes at an eco homestay through @mrbikerbentreboattour and it was exactly what I needed. It was so much fun  going around the town on our bikes. There were so many fun fruit shops and Sugarcane juice stand. 🍺 We both got a delicious drink off one of the stands for 50 cents and it was absolutely divine! 
Also, I had one of the most amazing Banh Xeo of my life. We found a random farm that also runs a restaurant and they made us the most incredible Banh Xeo.  I’m already sad to think how much I will miss today 🥲 #vietnamtravel #bentre

Today we decided to check out a park in Saigon. Creating a little reference point gives us a little mission to embark on and get our steps in 😊 This is  always a nice way to discover small gems or see places you would not be able to read or watch about. On our walkie walk, we were able to see the contrast in the city. One of my pics shows the old way of living off a stream (how my parents described their life growing up), and behind it are the new skyscrapers. 

As we walked, we discovered more street foods, mini restaurants, and cafes. I got some sugarcane juice off an auntie from a side stall and then stumbled into a little oasis off a super busy bustling road. It was a little coffee stale with lots of unique and local plants surrounding it. Great place for coffee and plant enthusiasts 🪴 There were little tables and seats hidden around an array of hanging plants. Later I found out it was a plant shop too! This was a nice little break stop for another refresher. Troy got his iced coffee and so we got to sit amongst all these pretty greenery. Everything is such a contrast in Saigon. You see old vs new everywhere, the crazy busy hustle of traffic, and Vietnamese taking their naps in the mist of all the chaos in the streets. I really enjoy observing 👀 and wondering how people adapt to the places they live in.

caption:
My Barbie moment at a super pink church in Saigon! It’s incredibly hot here but I heard it’s -25 back home, so we’re not complaining! I’ll take this heat and over stimulated city for the time being 🧡 

I thought that crowded places gives me anxiety but what I learned is that the environment and people affect me. Crowded places don’t give me anxiety, the collective energy of the same things do. Sometimes my environment can feel like a drag. People talking about the same things, focused on career, status, gossip, politics, limited beliefs, problems after problems. And when I’m around it too much, it sucks the life force out of me, so I retract. Exploring helps me break free from that. Any sort of traveling, mini trips, or taking off on a plane helps me break free from monotony and repetition. Walking in places is also very grounding for me. I’ve noticed that I need a balance of both worlds, the chaotic city and being in nature. When I become extreme in one, I definitely can feel the lack of balance in my overall energy. We are all different and I’m learning more on how to listen to my personal inner guide. #saigon #vietnam

Anthony Bourdain made a lot of videos  in Vietnam. He definitely created a pathway for international foodies to embrace it’s unique culture. A lot has changed here in development but some of his recommended stops are still around. This place specializes on one of my favorite dishes, Banh Xeo! Banh Xeo looks like an omelette; but it’s not, it’s rice flour, turmeric gives it the yellow color, some people add coconut milk, and beer to the batter making the outer crepe shell crispy.  It’s a nicely light dish and can make a great appetizer. It’s often served with a heaping plate of fresh lettuce and herbs. You roll everything up in a big leafy bundle of lettuce and dip it into a sweet tangy fish sauce 😘 Then embrace the explosion of crunch and savory flavor in one bite, it’s so delicious! 🤤 

My verdict with this place, doesn’t compare to mom’s Banh Xeo. However, their version is still delightful but not the best I had 👌 It’s on the lighter side in flavor, maybe good for westerner to train their taste buds. 👅 #vietnamesefood #saigon

caption: Jan 2024: Ok so we sort of made it out alive crossing the busy streets of Saigon today 😅 If you’re someone who easily gets anxiety in crowds where you live, I suggest you travel to Saigon. Because once you come here, I think you’ll be able to handle any chaotic city. Saigon will slap the wimp out in you, it’s a tough love sort of place. You will have to learn about trusting strangers, I don’t mean by handing anyone your wallet. I mean if you want to cross the roads, you will have to steadily walk out into traffic and flow with the chaotic rhythm, trust yourself and the drivers that will move around you 😆 It’s very mental. “Resiliency” is the vibe of this place.

All I can say is thank you. I’m honored to see such positive responses to the first announcement reel. This is going to be interesting. I didn’t know there were so many fans of folk music here! 

This album was tracked live in a small room, which is not the norm in for a studio session. (Either is actually building a pop-up studio in a cabin in the woods). 

There is an undeniable adventure in recording this way. You get what you get, mistakes and all. There lives a certain beauty, and honesty, in these songs because of it. Wear your scars. 

This is the final chorus to Full Moon Fight, the title track to the EP. I hope you enjoy it. I’ve fought a lot in the dark. Big thanks to this band for helping bring it to the light. @eliandwest @mgonigle @forrestliketrees 

Let me know what you think! EP release coming soon. - AM

How big of a wave will your contributions to SeaLegacy generate on today’s #GivingTuesday? The ocean’s impact rushes far beyond the sand, so when you support the sea, you send a ripple of hope throughout the world. This year, thanks to an anonymous donor, your gift to the ocean doubles with every donation matched! 

Every organism on Earth relies on the ocean– many as a home, but all for its services. To advocate for it, and defend its ability to carry out invaluable interactions, our team works with scientific experts, coastal communities, global leaders, and influential figures to generate waves of change. We and our partners know that our interconnected planet survives and thrives as one. So together, we help establish ocean solutions that compound with every ecological interaction. Just this year, our team:

- Helped expand and announce a Panamanian marine protected area that added 90,000 sq km (~35,000 sq mi) of protected waters in the Banco Volcán Area of Managed Resources.
- Shared the ocean’s impact and encouraged its protection to global audiences with co-founders @paulnicklen and @mitty’s feature on CNN’s “Call to Earth” series.
- Completed a Rapid Assessment Visual Expedition (RAVE) in Chilean Patagonia, where we amplified the importance of maintaining the waters holding the largest continuous kelp forest in the world.
- Released new episodes of our “A Sea of Hope” series– capturing and uplifting the realities facing our ocean, while inspiring its protection. Our work was recognized by prestigious peers, and we accepted two finalist nominations at the @jacksonwildorg Media Awards!
- Took over the @UNbiodiversity Instagram to share the importance of the ocean and our unique approach to protecting it through the “Rebuilding Life Roadmap.”
- Amplified the role of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands to our global community while urging protections that would maintain the Southern Ocean’s stability.

And so much more! Thanks to you and your donations, we can continue to shape a brighter future for our ocean and every individual who relies on it. Visit the link in our bio to support our work!

Each day, as we work to amplify our ocean’s stories and restore its health, we do so with Paul’s reliable voice and commitment to change, helping to steer the ship. Fearlessly exploring every corner of the world, he brings unreachable scenes vividly and candidly to our fingertips, opening the door to worlds that may otherwise go unseen. Paul engages us with charismatic creatures and their realities. His love for the ocean and its wildlife radiates through his work, and, with his artistic voice, proximity becomes negligible, and action is inspired.

Moon salutations from the new moon in #capricorn last night. Do you practice moon salutations? Most of us are familiar with Sun salutations but I’ve needed a more gentle, soothing option this season and have always liked moon salutations. It’s also no secret the moon and I have a good thing going. 🌕🌖🌗🌘🌑
🌙 Teaching this flow for my subscription babies. 
Head over to join us. 

There’s so many ways to tap into our power and connectivity - with and in our bodies, with nature, with the sensory body, with the universe. 

Here’s a few things about moon salutations: 

🌙 Less stimulating than sun salutations 
🌙 Said to prepare the body for rest and practiced in the evenings when the moon is out (but can be practiced anytime) 
🌙 Practiced facing the side of the map 
🌙 Ideally you do 3-7 rounds (which would be left and right side back to back as 1 round)

October came & went so quickly. 9+ flights, a birthday and a sprinkle of birthday dinners, lots of hugs, different skylines, so much jet lag and even more collective grief. I’ll be honest, showing up online has been strange for the past three years. It seems the horrors of reality continue existing in macro and micro ways every day, for me and for many of you, which leaves these little squares feeling vapid. I continue to hear the strain and unrest many are feeling and have been feeling. 1) You’re not alone, And 2) we really can’t grow weary, and I do align with the belief that when things are the hardest is when artists, healers, and all of us who can must get to work. Share as we can. Hold each other as we can. Love as we can. See one another and humanity as we can. So I haven’t been online as much but I am starting a newsletter (come say hi on substack,) I am writing a book I’m very proud of, I am moving thru my daily practices and rituals with more intentionality this season (happy to share those if y’all would like,) and I am seeing my lovely people in real, present ways. How is everyone else feeling? ❤️

Coyotes have infiltrated pockets of open land in San Francisco that are completely surrounded by multi-story flats. Incredible how bold some of these families have become due to an attitude that is mostly friendly toward coexistence with urban wildlife in SF. But, it’s not all rosy for both parties.  Urban coyote populations are mostly kept in check by car strikes, and pets are increasingly preyed upon. Survival techniques are on a spectrum from extreme stealth to extremely bold, and both seem to be working for the coyotes.  #urbanwildlife #onassignment #natgeo #coyote @natgeo #sanfrancisco shot for the story “Why Cities are going Wild” in @natgeo magazine July, 2022

Was a great honor to speak at the #natgeostorysummit in Washington D.C. last month and tell the stories behind the images for our “Why Cities are Going Wild” story for @natgeo written by the talented @christinedellamore After spending nearly three years tracking coyotes, bears and raccoons through the pandemic, the births of my daughter and son, a marrriage to @alynicklas, the death of my father, and a move out of Portland to the countryside, it was a great to spend time recapping what just happened on that Apocalypse Now style journey, to build this presentation, and reconnect with the National Geographic community.
