King for a Day, by @cedarwright 

People compare Paragliding to chess in the sky.  I think this analogy is faulty. I once heard, “Paragliding is like playing chess with dice that are a round.”  Closer to the truth?  I think chasing XC records is a little bit like fishing.  You cast your line and hope you catch a big one.  Really, Paragliding is closer to poker than chess... a game of skill and chance.   

This winter in Roldanillo I played my cards and launched my line into some absolutely epic weather. I arrived with the pie in the sky goal of breaking the FAI record for what is probably the most popular winter paragliding destination in the world.  Success was unlikely, but I’ve been working on my delusional self-belief. 

 On the 25th of January I realized an unlikely dream and put myself and the USA flag at the top of the Roldanillo x-contest score! I pushed, I believed, and I closed a 219 Km magical mystery tour of the Valle de Cauca.  Elated and exhausted, I rested.  My glory was short-lived. The next day Bogdan Bialka took his record back pushing it to 230!  And… the next day Kevin Phillip took to the sky with a vengeance setting a new record of 236 km…legend.  The Roldanillo FAI record was beaten 3 days in a row!  I spent the next two weeks in an absurd version of paragliding Groundhog Day trying to reclaim the record.  On three separate occasions, the dream was within grasp but shut down by the unpredictable Pacifico winds and a pace that just wasn’t fast enough. It’s fair to say that this was a historic season for Paragliding in Roldanillo.  

Of the top 50 scored flights on x-contest, 46 of them were from this year!  It’s more the journey than the destination, and I’m grateful for the motivation that being a record chasing psychopath gave me.  Epic scenery, wild low saves, thousands of kms, and almost 200 hours of full-bar obsession on my Enzo and Sub. While the Rolda. FAI record is more elusive than ever, I’m grateful that I got to be king for a day, and learned a ton about paragliding and the power of delusional self-belief....  which is why I’ll be taking the record back next year.

Product development is long and often frustrating. When you watch my videos, you see the sketch then you see the final result in a matter of 60 seconds but the truth is often my designs take anywhere between a year to sometimes 3 years to go from concept to real thing. 

Why?

It all begins with finding the right fabric for what I’m trying to achieve. If I’m lucky, I may already have a fabric I love that I’ve used before that I wanna use again! But often the fabric sourcing bit itself can take months.

The sampling process can take anywhere from a few months minimum to almost a year, sometimes more! During this time, fabric can change, design may change, the perfect fit will always be obsessed over, and I’ll sample over and over and over again until it feels just right. I’ll won’t stop until it feels ready, and I’m happy.

Then there’s the actual production which includes the weaving of the fabric, the dying of the fabric, the cutting of the pattern pieces, the careful sewing of the garment etc etc…

Good things just take time.

MORE GLUTES IN YOUR DEADLIFT 🍑 OR MORE HAMSTRINGS 🍖 Here’s how you get your aim right…

GLUTE FOCUSED DEADLIFT 🍑
This requires more STRETCH of the glute muscle to occur because more stretch = increased tension = more activation & work required to contract the muscles again. And more work = MORE GROWTH!
👉🏼 so what do you need to do? 
Increase the amount of knee bend and lower the hips more. This creates a deeper fold at the hips (and also less tension in the hamstring) increasing the recruitment of the glutes 👌🏼

HAMSTRING FOCUSED DEADLIFT 🍖
The same principle applies. You need to create more stretch & length in the hamstrings compared to the glutes.
👉🏼 so what do you need to do?
Less bend in the knees (bust still a slight bend 😉) and keep the hips higher as you lower the bar. 

🎥 WATCH MY FULL YT VIDEO FOR A DETAILED & VISUAL EXPLANATION ☺️ (link in stories)

It’s important to note that both muscle groups will be active in a deadlift, no matter which variation you do. This technique tip helps you shift more or less tension into each muscle group depending on what your training goals are 😎 Hope this helps! PILATES FOR RUNNERS 👟 If you’re a runner, sprinter, or even walker, you should be doing this!

Building strength in the glutes, stability in the hips & maintaining active feet is so important for efficient & injury free leg driven km’s (or miles!) 🏃🏽‍♀️💨

I’ve sped these videos up a little bit so remember to do each exercise slowly and with purpose!

TRY BEFORE RUNNING:
1-3 rounds depending how much time you have (the more often you do these, the better results you will get 💪🏼)

▪️1. CLAM SEQUENCE
x10 each side

- do all 3 exercises in a row, making sure you don’t collapse in the bottom ribcage between each exercise.
- keep the hips still (like there are in concrete) 

💥WORKS: Glute med & min - important for good lower body gait & hip stability

▪️ 2. SL TUCK CIRCLES
x10 each side

- keep belly button pulled in as you hold hips high & aim to keep hips still.

💥WORKS: Glute max, med & min / hip flexors / abs - helps build hip stability during leg movement

▪️3. SL EXTENDED RDL
x10 each side

- standing leg always has a slight bend
- fold at the hips & keep spine long (sit into standing leg a bit deeper)

💥WORKS: Glute max, med & min, quads, hip flexor - improves balance, hip stability & foot strength

▪️4. HIP HIKES
x10 each side

- move slowly & through full range on every rep (full up - full down)

💥WORKS: Glute med & min / obliques - improves hip stability & lower body gait

▪️5. FOOT SEQUENCE
x10 each side

Heel-Toe
- as you lean back pick up all 10 toes. Spread them as wide as you can as you roll foot forward then rise to toes.

Outdide-Inside
- slight bend in the knees & aim to find edges of your feet while spreading toes.

💥WORKS: Calves / Smaller foot muscles - important for good foot biomechanics and strength (our feet become weak as we are constantly in shoes!)

She let us into her secretive world and helped fuel our passion to protect Africa's threatened wild cats. Although Legadema is no longer with us, her legacy lives on. This #WorldWildlifeDay, we're reflecting on the special time we spent with her, and renewing our dedication to protect our planet's precious wild species and spaces.⁣
⁣
#WorldWildlifeDay #wildlife #nature #leopard

Battles between lions and buffaloes are unpredictable, brutal and intense. Adult male African buffaloes can weigh over 900 kilograms and they are notoriously belligerent. It takes careful coordination, acute timing and immense courage for lions to successfully hunt these massive animals. Often when the fight appears to be nearing its conclusion, a final show of strength from the buffalo – sometimes backed by the rest of the herd – can swing the odds in its favour. Sadly, for this bull, his resilience was overpowered and the lions succeeded.⁣
⁣⁣
#lion #wildlife #nature #bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram

Open mouth, insert foot.⁣
⁣
This young male was surprisingly tolerant of the rough-and-tumble games initiated by the pride's smallest members. For the cubs, playtime – which is most of the time – is an opportunity to learn and discover. For this subadult male who became the unwilling victim of their exuberant pouncing, it's a lesson in patience.⁣
⁣
#lion #wildlife #nature #bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram

Wildebeest may not be the most conventionally handsome antelope, but catch them in the right light – their beards glowing red in the afternoon sun – and they take on a certain distinctive quality. These somewhat ungainly animals are hardy survivors. They face an onslaught of threats during their annual migration across the predator-rich plains of the Serengeti and, for many, its sheer resilience and mettle that see them through the journey.

#wildebeest #wildlife #nature

I've always been in awe of the sheer power and presence of elephants. While spending time with these giants you learn to appreciate the delicate application of that immense strength. A carefully directed blast of water from a trunk provides relief from the scorching African sun, while pillar-like legs are used to dig into the sand when rivers run dry. Their movements are purposeful and intricate fuelled by an intelligence and social cohesion that we are yet to fully understand. Although, we don't speak their language and can only deduce the motivations for their behaviour, we can respect and admire their sentience. And do everything we can to protect them.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#elephant #nature #wildlife

Trees are more than just resting spots for leopards; they provide cover from danger and a safe place to stash a kill where it's beyond the reach of eager scavengers. This cat hastily hauled her warthog kill into the safety of the boughs, but kept a lookout for any rivals on the horizon. Competition for food is tough in the African bush, and wily predators like leopards are only too aware of the looming threat of losing a meal.⁣
⁣
#bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram #leopards

A lion's roar commands attention. Specially adapted vocal folds allow these cats to muster up a reverberating bellow that can be heard from kilometres away. If you're close enough, you'll feel the vibrations of the call rolling through your bones and likely triggering the hairs on the back of your neck to stand up straight. It's a sound we've come to love and appreciate during our time documenting these apex predators. Sadly, we have also witnessed this iconic sound fading from more and more corners of the African wild. We stand to lose so much more than just a roar if we allow these cats to vanish.⁣
⁣
#lions #bigcats #bigcatsofinstagram #bigcatconservation #wildlife #wildlifelovers #conservation #nature

There's a special elegance and grace reserved for giraffes. That silhouette, unmistakable against a golden sky, floats with purpose and poise across the savannah. Their unique form has awed visitors to Africa for centuries, but like so many other species, giraffes are in trouble. Populations have plummeted by 40% in just the last 30 years, and there are now fewer than 70,000 mature individuals left in the wild. We know what must be done to save them: prioritise conservation efforts, safeguard habitats, address threats like illegal hunting. If we don't act now, we stand to lose these iconic creatures forever.⁣
⁣
#giraffes #giraffeconservation #wildlifeconservation

#Repost from @natgeo

Intensely focused, this cheetah gives a piercing gaze across the plains of Kenya’s Masai Mara. Among Africa’s iconic big cats, cheetahs stand out as perhaps the most stark example of threats converging to imperil a species—from shallow gene pools to habitat loss to the illegal trade. New and emerging issues, including some related to climate change, are adding to the pressure—and often unfolding in unexpected ways. Recent research, for example, shows that rising temperatures are pushing cheetahs to shift their hunting habits to the cooler night hours, a behavior that not only complicates their survival strategies but also intensifies competition with other carnivores. In the face of these complex challenges, it is crucial for us to recognize the urgency of conservation efforts for both cheetahs and precious ecosystems like the Masai Mara.

Spotting a pangolin in the wild is rare. In all our years documenting wildlife, often spending weeks embedded in the bush, we've only seen a handful of these elusive mammals in the wild. They're often more active at night, shuffling through the undergrowth in search of termites, ants and larvae, which they dig out of nests and burrows using their impressive claws. Once they've carved an opening in the dirt, a long sticky tongue goes to work sucking up insects en masse. ⁣
⁣
They are profoundly unique animals. But they are also under threat. All eight species of pangolins found throughout the world are threatened by the illegal wildlife trade and populations are rapidly declining. Despite their shy nature, they remain one of the most trafficked mammals in the world and are illegally trapped in their thousands to feed a growing demand for their scales and meat. Without strict regulations and enforcement, these remarkable animals may be pushed to extinction. This #WorldPangolinDay, let's join forces and pledge to never let that happen.⁣
⁣⁣
#pangolin #PangolinsDay #wildlife #nature #wildlifeconservation

So much hope rests on those wobbly legs. It’ll take at least 10 years for this elephant to reach maturity. Ten long years where the youngster may encounter shrinking habitats, altered landscapes, and malicious humans. If the calf makes it, he’ll have an important role to play in helping nurture the next generation of elephants – a generation that may face even greater threats. These giants need safe space to roam in protected landscapes where they can live in harmony with humans. ⁣
⁣
@DereckJoubert and I recently hosted a number of speaking events in Florida where our goal was to share the urgent need to protect wild spaces and species and safeguard them for future generations. An African savannah without elephants is something we cannot  fathom. ⁣
⁣
Visit www.greatplainsfoundation to find out more about what we are doing to protect our planet and how you can get involved.⁣
⁣
#wildlifeconservation #elephants

It's astonishing to witness the speed and agility of hippos. Although they spend the majority of the daylight hours basking, semi-submerged, in rivers or ponds, hippos venture out of the water at night or when the weather is cooler to feed on grass. Those dainty ankles are carrying around a ton and a half of territorial hippo and, despite his size, he can turn on a dime. Deeply scarred from territorial disputes – the wounds of which were likely made more severe by opportunistic oxpecker birds that feast on blood and parasites – this male clearly means business. Hippos are famously possessive over their pools and will aggressively defend them, sometimes even charging at innocuous animals like impalas. A herd of buffalo ventured a bit too close, and the enraged hippo voiced his displeasure at their presence. Although buffaloes can definitely hold their own against an aggressive hippo, this herd thought  better of taking on the challenge and instead watched the angry behemoth from a distance.⁣⁣
⁣⁣

Pre & post menopause has been a rollercoaster! I’m 49, and I’ve been navigating this ride for the past 9 years. (Peri menopause started at age 40🫠)

One thing I forgot to mention in this video is that SLOW weight loss is the BEST kind of weight loss! There is no rush. Be consistent even if it takes years because the slower it comes off the better for long term success.

It’s taken me over 2 (maybe more) years to lose the belly fat. Before I get comments about how I looked great before and didn’t need to lose the weight… here’s the deal:

Visceral fat is fat around your organs & can lead to many health complications. When I started gaining weight around my belly, it wasn’t subcutaneous fat that you could pinch. It was hard, and felt so uncomfortable.

I knew that I had to figure out why this was happening or rather what I could do to stop & reverse the weight gain.

I’ve written several blogs about my discoveries from diet to exercise & exactly the changes I made so please check them out for more info.

I get messages from women every day about weight gain, specifically belly fat, & I’m posting this content for them.

When our hormones decline, we are at much greater health risks like heart disease, osteoporosis, and diabetes.

I recommend talking to your doctor & getting a full blood work up. Vitamin, mineral, & fiber deficiencies can make menopause even worse so it’s always good to know how well (nutrient-wise) you are eating.

With exercise, resistance based workouts to help build muscle will help protect your bones and increase your metabolism.

Consistency is hard for a lot of people. My only advice is to not make it a choice. 

Just like brushing your teeth, doing your laundry, or cleaning your dishes, you do it because it just has to get done.🙌🏻

Но парадокс заключается знаете, в чём? В том, что арбузер очень часто (за всех не могу сказать, но за своего точно скажу) делает это ИЗ ДОБРЫХ ПОБУЖДЕНИЙ, ОТ БОЛЬШОЙ ЛЮБВИ. Представляете? Я сейчас не про нарциссов, у которых с чувством эмпатии глухо, я про других, которые вполне себе умеют чувствовать, но на каком-то своём уровне.
⠀
Поверьте, мне есть, с чем сравнивать, и не каждый абьюзер - нарц, у них ооооочень большая разница. Мне кажется, я уже диссертацию о поведенческих признаках и методах общения с этими товарищами могу написать😅.

Он же хотел, как лучше. Только вот не понимал, что хотел, как лучше, ДЛЯ СЕБЯ. А как лучше для него самого, он НЕ ЗНАЕТ😬.
⠀
Просто в один момент за бесконечными подстройками и переделками себя под абьюзера (которыми он ВСЁ РАВНО будет недоволен) можно очнуться и себя не узнать. А жизнь-то прошла…

Альмира и Ярослав встали в пару меньше года назад…после того, как мама предыдущего партнёра, с которым Альмира станцовывалась полгода и к которому сильно прикипела, заявила мне, что «НЕ ВИДИТ В НАС ЗАИНТЕРЕСОВАННОСТИ» и единолично «отменила» нашу пару.
⠀

⠀

Сколько её слёз было пролито и сколько моих нервов потрачено, но надо понимать, что бальные танцы - это парный спорт, и чем раньше станцовываешься с партнёром, тем сильнее пара в будущем.
⠀
Прошло совсем немного времени, и перед вами уже СИЛЬНАЯ ПАРА. Сколько турниров уже оттанцовано! Какая колоссальная работа проделана! ⠀
Хотя…кубки не главное! И даже не главное, что её предыдущий партнер кукует без партнёрши! Главное - огонь в глазах ребят и то, что они видят, ради чего они так много работают!
⠀
Иногда Альмира спрашивает, как там Лёня…но теперь я вижу, насколько верным было решение не оставаться в солистках и пережить те слёзы! У девочки проснулся азарт и жажда победы, но важнее всего то, что она получает удовольствие и сияет на турнирах! А то ли ещё будет, вот увидите!
⠀

• BIEN NETTOYER SA GOURDE 💦 C’est vraiment un super allié durable, écologique et zéro déchet mais aussi un véritable NID À BACTÉRIES 🙀🦠 alors mieux vaut les bichonner !

1️⃣ Ne pas passer les gourdes en inox au lave vaisselle (ni au micro-ondes et ni au congélateur).
2️⃣ Nettoyer en profondeur avec du vinaigre blanc (1/3 du volume de la gourde + eau chaude) et/ou du bicarbonate de soude (2 cuillères + eau chaude) puis fermer, secouer, laisser agir 10min minimum sans le bouchon avant de rincer abondamment à l’eau chaude.
3️⃣ Utiliser simplement du liquide vaisselle + de l’eau chaude pour un nettoyage quotidien. 
4️⃣ Laver l’intérieur sans oublier l’extérieur et le bouchon à part dans un bain d’eau chaude + vinaigre blanc et/ou bicarbonate de soude. Si le bouchon de votre gourde comporte un joint, le retirer délicatement et le laver à part également. 
5️⃣ Faire sécher la gourde à l’air libre, tête en bas sans la refermer, idéalement sur un porte biberon si vous en avez un.
6️⃣ Stocker votre gourde ouverte sans le bouchon pour éviter la condensation et les mauvaises odeurs si vous ne l’utilisez pas.

🥤 Personnellement, je ne mets que de l’eau dans mes gourdes mais si vous avez l’habitude de boire d’autres types de boissons (sodas, thé, café ou mojito… 🌿😂) il est bien sûr important de procéder à un nettoyage en profondeur à chaque utilisation.

Connaissiez-vous ces astuces ? Si vous aussi, vous buvez toujours dans une gourde et ne sortez jamais sans, partager vos rituels pour bien entretenir vos gourdes !💧⤵️

• ALLAITER ENCEINTE 🤱🤰 mon expérience ⤵️

👉 1ER TRIMESTRE : mon fils est passé naturellement de 4/5 TT / 24h à 2/3 TT. Les TT se sont également énormément réduites en durée passant de 10/15min à 2/5min. Le sommeil 💤 s’est aussi grandement amélioré puisqu’il a commencé à faire des nuits complètes cet été. Un combo entre son arrêt des protéines de lait de vache quelques mois plus tôt soignants ses maux mais peut être aussi le ressenti que ses parents avaient besoin d’un peu de repos avant de replonger dans les nuits hachées (ou pas sait-on jamais haha) ?

Comme mon fils est un petit gabarit, on surveille sa prise de poids grossomodo 1 fois tous les 2 mois. Nous nous sommes aperçu qu’il avait perdu 300g. J’ai compris à ce moment là que ma lactation avait énormément baissé. 📉  Moins de bon lait maternel = il faut mettre l’accent sur des sources de calcium et de bons gras différents. Quelques ajustements plus tard et il avait repris son poids plume 🪶 (merci Julie de @hamstouille_bambin de nous avoir conseillé).

Mes seins devenus très sensibles, j’ai énormément communiqué mon ressenti à mon fils pour qu’il adapte ses tétées sans me gêner. Une des joies d’allaiter un bambin c’est qu’il comprend absolument TOUT.

👉 2EME TRIMESTRE : les TT se maintiennent voir ralentissent, je me dis même qu’il pourrait se sevrer naturellement s’il en ressentait le besoin. Depuis ses 2 ans environ, je ne lui propose plus le sein, c’est à son initiative avec mon consentement bien sûr. Je vis notre allaitement au jour le jour, comme une chance. 🍀 Peut être s’arrêtera-t-il naturellement pendant ma grossesse ? Peut être irons-nous vers un co-allaitement ? L’avenir nous le dira !

👉 3EME TRIMESTRE : je sais maintenant qu’une aventure de co-allaitement nous attend. 🥹 Je prépare au maximum mon fils en lui expliquant tout « tu sais il y a 2 titis ça tombe bien un pour toi et un pour ta petite sœur qui aura besoin de boire beaucoup de lait car les bébés ne peuvent pas manger comme nous ».

Hello,

If you don’t know who I am, allow me to introduce myself. I’m Alex, I’m French but I grew up in Madrid, and I’ve been creating with a camera since 2009. “Professionally” since 2012. 

What gets me out of bed every morning is the deep desire to connect with people and environments. Meeting people and seeing places for the first time is a bit of an addiction.

I make photographs for brands when they hire me. I also make films for them too. I’m known for shooting landscapes and outdoors sports like cycling and hiking. I’ve also built a few companies such as @stayandwander (creative agency) and @wildistco (online photography school). I take pride in sharing what I know about the world of photography and have spent the last five years doing that both online and offline on photography retreats. 

Becoming a photographer happened by accident. As soon as I moved from France to Quebec to finish my design studies I got totally drawn in by the boreal forest and the harsh winters. It was, and still is an endless source of inspiration and peace. 

I struggle with scheduling because I am interested in a lot of things. I also struggle to make the time to go shoot more outside. Also, I’m a pretty bad handyman. 

I know it is very timely to hate on this app and what it is becoming. Although I agree with a lot of it, I’m also immensely thankful for this app that has allowed me to meet thousands of people. Some of which have become friends for life. It has also changed my life by helping create a career path for me and drawing sizeable exposure to my work. That I’ll never forget. 

With that said, It’s up to us to make IG what we want it to be… So here are my commitments to you: 

1. To always tell you like it is
2. To share work I’m proud of
3. To help you if you’re trying to help yourself.. (continued in comments)

Talvez a ficha nunca caia, mas fazer parte de mais essa tour com meus irmãos do @nxzerooficial foi sem dúvida a melhor coisa que decidi fazer esse ano. 

São muitos anos, muitos mesmo… algumas pessoas até nem saibam que antes de ser fotógrafo, cheguei a dividir palco com o NX com a minha banda também - se não me engano isso rolou em 2003 em Caçapava/SP, na extinta Posso! Skate Bar. 

Corta pra 2005 e nos reencontramos, eu já como fotógrafo e morando em Curitiba. Depois de vários shows fazendo foto deles por lá, chegou a hora de voltar pra SP e aceitar o convite pra acompanhar a banda em definitivo… não hesitei em dizer sim, afinal de contas, eu já acreditava no potencial deles antes mesmo de assinarem com gravadora.

Deu certo, deu muito certo. Foram anos de estrada, convivência, aprendizados e muita troca. Eu sou quem sou hoje por causa do NXZERO, e sei que lá no fundo alguma coisa disso é recíproca também, afinal, durante muitos anos tudo o que as pessoas viam e tinham acesso era através do meu olhar, do que eu queria mostrar e como eu enxergava aquilo tudo.

Já essa tour foi algo que nunca imaginei que viveria. Essa experiência de lotar duas vezes um estádio é pra poucos… e eu já não tava ali como fotógrafo, eu tava ali como um espectador com privilégios. Eu não sei até agora o que rolou, mas talvez essa última cena do carrossel diga mais que tudo. Foi mais forte que eu.
Obrigado por confiarem no meu trabalho e acreditarem nas maluquices que propus… obrigado também a toda equipe que sempre entregou o melhor que podiam - vcs não fazem ideia do que eles fazem pra tudo acontecer.

NXZERO é uma energia onde todos nós fazemos parte. A troca é necessária e só assim que tudo flui.

Muito obrigado, parabéns a todos e até breve 🥹❤️

Curitiba tem um peso importantíssimo pra mim e acredito muito que pra eles também. 

Mas vou contar aqui uma curiosidade: em todos esses anos que estive com eles, apenas UMA sessão fotográfica em estúdio foi feita, marcada e planejada. Todas as outras vezes, sempre improvisando onde quer que fosse, na hora que dava e com o que a gente tinha… e talvez essa seja a “nossa” marca haha.

Essa sessão não deixou de ser também um pouco improvisada e com o tempo disponível que a gente tinha, mas pelo menos o lugar eu consegui escolher… e o desafio era: todas as fotos apenas com luz natural.

Pedi que levassem dois figurinos, um na atual paleta que definimos no início da tour e o outro com o clássico todo preto, e assim foi. Tínhamos duas horas pra fazer tudo isso aí acontecer.

No geral a sessão foi bem tranquila, todos se divertindo, tudo fluiu sem problema e acho que a vibe que ficou diz muita coisa disso, não?

A couple of weeks ago, I shared a collection of some commercial work that I’ve done over the years and I thought I’d share another round of some old favorites. It’s so common on Instagram to only see highlights or just the final product and I think it’s really important to show a larger scope of what it takes to be successful in the creative industry - and commercial work has been a huge part of that for me. My approach was always to combine inspiring, landscapes, and adventure with companies that I worked with - taking what I knew how to do well and finding a way to integrate their product in.. some thing I think aspiring photographers to ask themselves… how does your style and expertise mesh with a brand that way that makes sense?

Iceland’s highlands have long been a playground for both locals and newcomers.. offering the ability to connect with an astonishing variety of natural features all within close proximity to each other. You might be crossing glacial rivers, moving past steaming geothermal vents, or traversing colorful ridge lines that look as if painted by nature’s brush. This part of the world always sparks imagination and rejuvenates me every time I return... offering a little more perspective on where my next expedition could be or what creative project might capture it’s beauty for those to see who are unable to make the trip. Last fall I was lucky enough to share some spectacular weather in the highlands on a ride with the @maap.cc ALT-ROAD crew - traversing from hut to hut and scoring some of the best views Iceland has to offer... couldn’t think of a better way to spend a few days with friends.

I’m not a wildlife photographer - I leave that to my good friends @paulnicklen & @mitty who’ve spent many years & countless hours perfecting the craft… but occasionally, if I’m lucky, an animal gets in the way of my camera. 
To me, whales cresting the ocean’s surface remains as one of the more special human experiences. The two orcas shown above swam just off the shores of the Kurils - a chain of islands located between Russia and Japan. Besides the sound of disturbed seagulls and the creaking of our boat, all outside distractions and sense of time seemed to fade away as I witnessed these beautiful creatures breach… fortunately having the presence of mind to haphazardly hold up my camera and try to capture one of the purest wildlife moments I can remember. During this expedition in 2019 with @renan_ozturk & @taylorfreesolo - we shared a piece of what we found in an environmental documentary called “From the Kurils with Love” which you can find on YouTube

This are images from an old project from 2002.
The project was born out of one of the most traumatic experiences I had as a journalist - and it is - in a way - the beginning of my career.

In the Summer of 2002 I traveled to Israel and the West Bank and Gaza - fresh out of school hoping to find my way into the industry. I did whatever naive kid did back then, and parachuted my way into a story that I had little nuanced appreciation for. 

In the midst of trying to document life in Hebron between the Jewish settlers and Palestinian residents, I was beaten by a mob of 20 Jewish settlers during a violent funeral/riot in the center of the city. Interestingly enough an Israeli soldier was also beaten by the settler mob. 

I lost all my photography equipment I had saved up for, driving the “drunk bus” route in school, and dislocated my shoulder, and fractured my elbow and knee.

My mentor at the time - James Colburn (the DC bureau photo editor for Time Magazine) told me I couldn’t leave. That if I left - “I would always be scared” 

So I stayed - and he shipped me some old Nikon F3s he had lying in his office.

I spent the next month looking for a different story, and I found it in the most cliche place - A mental institution.

There was an old geriatric wing of this psychiatric facility in Bethlehem. For patients from all over the country. The doctors said some were Jewish, some were Muslim, some were Christian. No one knew for sure, many had been dropped off as infants. The facility had originally been administered by German, then British, then TransJordanian, then Israel and at the time I was there - the Palestinian Authority. 

And it was filled with many patients. They were all psychologically damaged or impaired. But interestingly enough - they got along with each other.

They were insane. But at peace.
And everyone outside was sane, but waging war.

Makes you think about who is really in their right minds. 

#photojournalism #palestine #israel #reportage #documentary

The US border patrol would cut the wire that the National Guard put up to let people in. Children and women first, then men.

One of the other projects I did in Yemen were these portraits of Yemenis that played into the assignment I was working on, along with people I met during wanderings around different cities. 

This project could be the indirect reason I was detailed when I came back to the US. 

The second image is a portrait of the leader (at the time) of Al Qaeda’s political wing in Yemen.  He really liked the image and asked if I could send it to him. We used the old “bump” iPhone app to exchange the image. And I’m pretty sure my phone was compromised from there on out. 

To make matters worse - we were meeting in a large cafe for safety - the next interview subject came in to meet the writer and I a bit early. The third image is a portrait of the last Rabbi in Yemen. Obviously the head of Al Qaeda and the Rabbi kept their affiliations on the DL - so neither knew who each one was. They actually exchanged pleasant greetings and traded places - as the rabbi stayed for an interview and portrait.

The fourth image is a former Guantanamo prisoner who was returned to Yemen after serving a few years in the prison and found either not guilty or not worth US efforts to interrogate him. He was unemployed and trying to figure out how to continue a life cut short.

Snippets from the woodworking studio with Yoshida-san @monkeyhold_japan in 大垣 (Ogaki), Japan over the summer. 

Shaping these holds was a lesson in allowing the medium lead to the final form rather than having the mind dictate the outcome. The practice was about inhibiting the urge to mold the wood into a shape I had pre-envisioned; instead, surrendering to the wood, imagining how best to reveal its beauty and unique form. 

To hold something is gratifying, but the more I climb, the more curious I become about the entire ecosystem that holds the boulders. When examined more closely, the 侘寂 of the wood is unveiled through the imperfections of the gnarled knots, the layers and swirls of age lines that hold the stories of the tree the wood came from 🤍 🌳

Shibori w mom and friends🪁 
🌱I’ve been fascinated by this form of textile art for quite some time but never took the initiative to experiment w it till this year. In a conversation w my mom about folk art in Japan, the topic of this ancient method of manual resist dying came up and her eyes instantly sparkled with excitement as she shared her story of working with dye in her youth. As a child to immigrant parents who are reserved in speaking of their past, i have a hazy idea of what they were like in their youth and the environment in which they grew up in. Anyways, I love how shibori became a catalyst to paint a more vivid picture of my mom’s past 🌿It felt extra special to learn some shibori techniques from my mom with dear friends💖 

Some quotes I love from master dyer Fukumi Shimura: 

“I have received color without limit from the natural world in the years since I entered the dyer’s way. It has poured down on me endlessly, too much for this meager vessel to hold. Joyful as a child with a new set of paints, I have woven and woven yarn dyed by the grasses and trees”. 

“I don’t tell the acorn or gardenia seed pod or plum bar what color I want – I listen to the voice of the plants.” 

Hope I get the chance to practice and learn from the shibori masters in Japan soon 🎨

One of the things I’m most thankful for is the ability to explore West Coast nature, like this spot: Malibu Tunnels⛰🕳

It’s a windy channel of conglomerate rock that acts like a barrier from the turbulence of civilization. There’s a canopy of cottonwoods and live oaks scattered about. Rattlers basking in the sun. A honeycomb mounted in a hueco. A flow of creek water cascades down and through the rock piles. Further down the stream, a face of cobblestone rocks- purple, green, brown, red- protruding upon a beige sandy looking canvas.

There’s a busy road a hundred feet above; honking and roadside noise remind us that this respite is in close proximity to a bustling city. But then the gurgling water overwhelms the sound of motor vehicles emanating from above, dislodging you from the constraints of spatial and temporal associations, you can almost close your eyes and forget where you are.

Spring in the quilted hills, and the perennial question. Where to go next, or perhaps better stated, how to grow next? I really enjoy the notion, that ideas are alive and independent, like butterflies flittering about. There’s two ways to catch ‘um. You can run yourself ragged chasing. Or you can chill and enlarge the net.

Wyoming has quickly become one of my favorite backpacking destinations. Two years ago I spent a week in the Wind River Range, then last summer I joined @elisabethontheroad as she documented our climb up Cloud Peak in the Bighorn Mountains for @visitwyoming

I’ve followed the work of plein air painters from this state before I ever picked up a camera. It’s been fun growing familiar with the language of the landscape first hand, to see the peaks and valleys that translated to such inspiration. 

Finding beauty can be straightforward, it shines unabashed, but exploring what you have to say about a place takes time. It may even be through the creative process itself that you discover it. I often learn as much during a week on the computer with a digital paintbrush, as a week on the trail. Wouldn’t trade the epiphanies provided by either.

If your curious about the specifics of our climb, you can find Elisabeth’s article at TravelWyoming.com. #ThatsWY #WYresponsibly
Exploring an idea. One-new, two-an update, three-from a few years back.

“Unlike Earth, the atmosphere of Mars is dominated by micron-size dust aerosols, and the sky during sunset takes on a bluish glow.” From: Applied Optics Vol. 53, Issue 9

I’ve been experimenting with the public domain images available on the NASA website. What you see here are constructed entirely from that source. It’s been strange, and wasn’t until I found the article referenced above that I realized why. The light on Mars is ‘weird’ because the atmosphere is different. Go figure.

As I worked, the project became as much about understanding this unique light as playing with Martin landforms. The images here explore a few ways to bridge a blue light source - with golden/orange scattering, across a few different angles and times of day in a variety of atmospheric dust. It’s definitely not accurate, and surely exaggerated. (Check out the article, lots of math above my ability) The science was simply a point of departure for experimentation. The main gist i held in mind, is that blue can transition through purple & red or green & yellow to get to orange. Just walk your way around a color wheel. Fun. After a month tho, I’m ready to go look at some foliage.

There’s a balance between surface and substance, the aesthetics of an image and its meaning. I tend to think craft is important, but offers diminishing returns. In contrast, the possibilities for conceptual exploration are endless. It’s the difference between learning a language and finding what you have to say with it.

My favorite time in art history was between the late 1800’s and the early 1900’s, when the method used to create something started gaining awareness of its contribution to content. An interest in the mechanics of light and sight created the dappled visual color mixing of the impressionists. An interest in the mechanics of time and space gave birth to the multiple overlaid perspectives of cubism. I keep thinking about this as I flew about the mountains, collecting images from multiple moments and perspective.

Does any of this matter to the viewer and the final? Maybe. There are plenty of images I’ve enjoyed for their ideas, and plenty for aesthetics alone. But on this side of the image, the one of discovery and creation, building something with a conceptual foundation makes all the difference between a meaningful process and a simply stylish one. It’s powerfully good to stay in touch with that little kid inside, who endlessly asks “why?!”

One of my favorite fascinations is searching for repeated patterns in scale, micro and macro. Maybe it has to do with searching for something fundamental in the nature of things, or maybe it’s just fun to pretend you’re giant or very very small. 

This digital painting came together with shots from the mavic3 while climbing, and macro shots of rocks collected along the way.

Matching light and atmosphere is the most important factor to make a realistic scene, but texture is one of the biggest scale giveaways, so drones are the perfect tool to marry the two.

Migratory interests. I’ve been taking a little break from pixel painting and posting,  exploring a few new fascinations.  Then last month, DJI asked me to try out their Mavic3. Always happy to see through a different lens, I spent a couple weeks dodging fall storms in Idaho. (Really digging the extended battery life BTW.) Ironically, I’m now realizing my artistic process; harmonizing an eclectic array of images (somewhere around 30 here), isn’t so different than life process; harmonizing an eclectic array of interests. I really think the key is remembering to identify with the fascination, not the subject of it. Trust that single source of light, and the rest will sort itself in time, or Photoshop.

The clam diggers. A rainy day conversation with, James Abbott McNeill Whistler, and Idris Khan, perhaps a drop in by Todd Hido...

I don’t know any of these cats. Idris and Todd are making powerful work today, but James was born in 1834, so it might be a challenge for us to get together. But, that’s the cool thing about art. We can dialogue with anyone throughout time.

This one finds me curious about their feelings on substance vs style. Inspiration vs appropriation. The relationship between how we make something, and why. 

Idris created a seminal series that appropriated the work of Bernd and Hilla Becher, with (it appears) the intent of adding meaning. Todd’s style is highly copied by other contemporary photographers, who arguably don’t add additional meaning. And James was a big proponent of art for aesthetics alone - meaning be damned (and fought over in lawsuits.) Of course his stance was taken in an age when images were relatively rare and filled with allegory, which to him might have made this fight feel - quite meaningful. 🙃

American badlands. 

There is freedom being an outsider, to see culture in memetic terms, languages modular and mutable. To identify, simply through that which you happen to be appreciating. Right now, there is blue sky and sunlight on the hills.

Rock arrangement in sea minor. I grew up on this beach, playing with toy boats, pretending boulders were islands. Things haven’t changed much. My fascination with scale is the same as it ever was. The large central rocks are actually just close up photos of the same stones from the beach. I built a small pool and arranged them separately in still water.

Some of my favorite experiences with art started in boredom or confusion, then - after learning about the ideas behind a work, continued in appreciation. How cool is it that we can dialogue with anyone throughout history by responding to them with a few ideas of our own.

This scene may just be a simple sunset (or a boring one), but in addition to memories and scale, here are a few of the random things I was musing on while working:

Six Persimmons - The classic Chinese painting by the Buddhist monk Muqi. (An image that’s taken me years to understand).

Zen gardens and stones - They’re often used as a cliche representation for dreamy, sleepy relaxation, spa treatments and the like, when the reality of Zen practice can be quite serious and ardent effort towards waking up. I’m fascinated by the popular culture misunderstandings, perhaps because I held them so long myself.

Music - Visual spacing and rhythm, horizontal bars and notes; the staccato feeling of eye movement related to musical spacing and rhythm and spacing and rhythm and spacing and rhythm.

Two photos of Common Terns bringing back fish for their chicks that tell a story of climate change in the Gulf of Maine –
 
As seawater temperatures increase, native fish species that sustain seabirds become scarce, forcing parents to bring their chicks fish that they cannot swallow.
 
In the first image the parent returns to its nest with a Sand Lance – a slender-bodied silver fish that the chicks can easily swallow.
 
The second photo shows a tern parent with a Butterfish in its mouth, a meal the baby birds cannot eat.
 
The result is an increase in chick mortality rates.

A harp seal pup, about 16 days old swims among the ice in Canada’s Gulf of St. Lawrence.

A school of Alewife fish swim into a waterfall during their annual spawning migration in a river in Maine.
 
Alewife are an anadromous species of herring that spend most of their lives in the ocean, but migrate through freshwater rivers to lakes where they spawn each spring.
 
Their stocks had been severely depleted, but have improved in the Gulf of Maine due to the removal of dams in coastal rivers.

Don’t shove your cat in their pet carrier right before their vet appointment / traveling causing Meowing and anxiety.
Start acclimating them to their pet carrier now by…
Step 1 Pet carrier near feeding area. Bowl of food placed a few feet from carrier. 
Step 2 Every 2 to 4 days (or at your cats comfortable pace), move food bowl a tadbit closer to carrier.
Step 3 eventually place bowl right inside carrier 
Step 4 Bowl inching its way (every 2-4 days) towards the back of the carrier. 
Step 5 once your cat is comfortably eating the food in the back of the carrier, move the door to see how your cat responds, little by little to desensitise them from the strange and scary sound the door can make closing. Do this a little bit each meal eventually closing and opening the door. 
once you can close it open it and your cat is still eating and comfortable, once closed gently pickup carrier and set back down opening up the carrier. Repeat a few times each meal before carrying it to another room. 
Tips: Use higher value food to speed up the acclamation process. 
Don’t move to the next step until your cat is comfortable. You can also incorporate toy games in and around the carrier for a positive experience. 
You want to use the same incremental desensitisation  process to acclimate them to your vehicle.
